1.33.e: The waters flowed according to their nature; he raid the navigable streams waxed mighty.  Then Indra, with his spirit concentrated, smote him for ever with his strongest weapon.

1.33.d: नयाविध्यदिलीबिशस्य दर्ल्हा वि शर्ङगिणमभिनच्छुष्णमिन्द्रः | यावत तरो मघवन यावदोजो वज्रेण शत्रुमवधीः पर्तन्युम ||
1.33.e: Indra broke through Ilībiśa's strong castles, and Śuṣṇa with his horn he cut to pieces:  Thou, Maghavan, for all his might and swiftness, slewest thy fighting foeman with thy thunder

1.33.d: अभि सिध्मो अजिगादस्य शत्रून वि तिग्मेन वर्षभेण पुरो.अभेत | सं वज्रेणास्र्जद वर्त्रमिन्द्रः पर सवां मतिमतिरच्छाशदानः ||
1.33.e: Fierce on his enemies fell Indra's weapon: with. his sharp bull he rent their forts in pieces.  He with his thunderbolt dealt blows on Vṛtra; and conquered, executing all his purpose.

1.33.d: आवः कुत्सम इन्द्र यस्मि चाकन परावो युध्यन्तं वर्षभं दशद्युम | शफच्युतो रेणुर नक्षत दयाम उच छवैत्रेयो नर्षाह्याय तस्थौ ||
1.33.e: Indra, thou helpest Kutsa whom thou lovedst, and guardedst brave Daśadyu when he battled,  The dust of trampling horses rose to heaven, and Śvitrā's son stood up again for conquest.

1.33.d: आवः शमं वर्षभं तुग्र्यासु कषेत्रजेषे मघवञ्छ्वित्र्यं गाम | जयोक चिद अत्र तस्थिवांसो अक्रञ्छत्रूयताम अधरा वेदनाकः ||
1.33.e: Śvitrā's mild steer, O Maghavan thou helpest in combat for the land, mid Tugra's houses.  Long stood they there before the task was ended: thou wast the master of the foemen's treasure.

1.34.d: तरिश चिन नो अद्या भवतं नवेदसा विभुर वां याम उत रातिर अश्विना | युवोर हि यन्त्रं हिम्येव वाससो ऽभयायंसेन्या भवतम मनीषिभिः ||
1.34.e: Ye who observe this day be with us even thrice: far-stretching is you bounty, Aśvins and your course.  To you, as to a cloak in winter, we cleave close: you are to be drawn nigh unto us by the wise.

1.34.d: तरयः पवयो मधुवाहने रथे सोमस्य वेनाम अनु विश्व इद विदुः | तरय सकम्भास सकभितास आरभे तरिर नक्तं याथस तरिर व अश्विना दिवा ||
1.34.e: Three are the fellies in your honey-bearing car, that travels after Soma's loved one, as all know.  Three are the pillars set upon it for support: thrice journey ye by night, O Aśvins, thrice by day.

1.34.d: समाने अहन तरिर अवद्यगोहना तरिर अद्य यज्ञम मधुना मिमिक्षतम | तरिर वाजवतीर इषो अश्विना युवं दोषा अस्मभ्यम उषसश च पिन्वतम ||
1.34.e: Thrice in the self-same day, ye Gods who banish want, sprinkle ye thrice to-day our sacrifice with meath;  And thrice vouchsafe us store of food with plenteous strength, at evening, O ye Aśvins, and at break of day.

1.34.d: तरिर वर्तिर यातं तरिर अनुव्रते जने तरिः सुप्राव्येत्रेधेव शिक्षतम | तरिर नान्द्यं वहतम अश्विना युवं तरिः पर्क्षो अस्मे अक्षरेव पिन्वतम ||
1.34.e: Thrice come ye to our home, thrice to the righteous folk, thrice triply aid the man who well deserves your help.  Thrice, O ye Aśvins, bring us what shall make us glad; thrice send us store of food as nevermore to fail.

1.34.d: तरिर नो रयिं वहतम अश्विना युवं तरिर देवताता तरिर उतावतं धियः | तरिः सौभगत्वं तरिर उत शरवांसि नस तरिष्ठं वां सूरे दुहिता रुहद रथम ||
1.34.e: Thrice, O ye Aśvins, bring to us abundant wealth: thrice in the Gods’ assembly, thrice assist our thoughts.  Thrice, grant ye us prosperity, thrice grant us fame; for the Sun's daughter hath mounted your three-wheeled car.

1.34.d: तरिर नो अश्विना दिव्यानि भेषजा तरिः पार्थिवानि तरिर उ दत्तम अद्भ्यः | ओमानं शंयोर ममकाय सूनवे तरिधातु शर्म वहतं शुभस पती ||
1.34.e: Thrice, Aśvins, grant to us the heavenly medicines, thrice those of earth and thrice those that the waters hold,  Favour and health and strength bestow upon my son; triple protection, Lords of Splendour, grant to him.

1.34.d: तरिर नो अश्विना यजता दिवे-दिवे परि तरिधातु पर्थिवीम अशायतम | तिस्रो नासत्या रथ्या परावत आत्मेव वातः सवसराणि गछतम ||
1.34.e: Thrice are ye to be worshipped day by day by us: thrice, O ye Aśvins, ye travel around the earth.  Car-borne from far away, O ye Nāsatyas, come, like vital air to bodies, come ye to the three.

1.34.d: तरिर अश्विना सिन्धुभिः सप्तमात्र्भिस तरय आहावास तरेधा हविष कर्तम | तिस्रः पर्थिवीर उपरि परवा दिवो नाकं रक्षेथे दयुभिर अक्तुभिर हितम ||
1.34.e: Thrice, O ye Aśvins, with the Seven Mother Streams; three are the jars, the triple offering is prepared.  Three are the worlds, and moving on above the sky ye guard the firm-set vault of heaven through days and nights.

1.34.d: कव तरी चक्रा तरिव्र्तो रथस्य कव तरयो वन्धुरो ये सनीळाः | कदा योगो वाजिनो रासभस्य येन यज्ञं नासत्योपयाथः ||
1.34.e: Where are the three wheels of your triple chariot, where are the three seats thereto firmly fastened?  When will ye yoke the mighty ass that draws it, to bring you to our sacrifice. Nāsatyas?

1.34.d: आ नासत्या गछतं हूयते हविर मध्वः पिबतम मधुपेभिर आसभिः | युवोर हि पूर्वं सवितोषसो रथम रताय चित्रं घर्तवन्तम इष्यति ||
1.34.e: Nāsatyas, come: the sacred gift is offered up; drink the sweet juice with lips that know the sweetness well.  Savitar sends, before the dawn of day, your car, fraught with oil, various-coloured, to our sacrifice.

1.34.d: आ नासत्या तरिभिर एकादशैर इह देवेभिर यातम मधुपेयम अश्विना | परायुस तारिष्टं नी रपांसि मर्क्षतं सेधतं दवेषो भवतं सचाभुवा ||
1.34.e: Come, O Nāsatyas, with the thrice-eleven Gods; come, O ye Aśvins, to the drinking of the meath.  Make long our days of life, and wipe out all our sins: ward off our enemies; be with us evermore.

1.34.d: आ नो अश्विना तरिव्र्ता रथेनार्वाञ्चं रयिं वहतं सुवीरम | शर्ण्वन्ता वाम अवसे जोहवीमि वर्धे च नो भवतं वाजसातौ ||
1.34.e: Borne in your triple car, O Aśvins, bring us present prosperity with noble offspring.  I cry to you who hear me for protection be ye our helpers where men win the booty.

1.35.d: हवयाम्य अग्निम परथमं सवस्तये हवयामि मित्रावरुणाव इहावसे | हवयामि रात्रीं जगतो निवेशनीं हवयामि देवं सवितारम ऊतये ||
1.35.e: AGNI I first invoke for our prosperity; I call on Mitra, Varuṇa, to aid us here.  I call on Night who gives rest to all moving life; I call on Savitar the God to lend us help.

1.35.d: आ कर्ष्णेन रजसा वर्तमानो निवेशयन्न अम्र्तम मर्त्यं च | हिरण्ययेन सविता रथेना देवो याति भुवनानि पश्यन ||
1.35.e: Throughout the dusky firmament advancing, laying to rest the immortal and the mortal,  Borne in his golden chariot he cometh, Savitar, God who looks on every creature.

1.35.d: याति देवः परवता यात्य उद्वता याति शुभ्राभ्यां यजतो हरिभ्याम | आ देवो याति सविता परावतो ऽप विश्वा दुरिता बाधमानः ||
1.35.e: The God moves by the upward path, the downward; with two bright Bays, adorable, he journeys.  Savitar comes, the God from the far distance, and chases from us all distress and sorrow.

1.35.d: अभीव्र्तं कर्शनैर विश्वरूपं हिरण्यशम्यं यजतो बर्हन्तम | आस्थाद रथं सविता चित्रभानुः कर्ष्णा रजांसि तविषीं दधानः ||
1.35.e: His chariot decked with pearl, of various colours, lofty, with golden pole, the God hath mounted,  The many-rayed One, Savitar the holy, bound, bearing power and might, for darksome regions.

1.35.d: वि जनाञ्छ्यावाः शितिपादो अख्यन रथं हिरण्यप्ररौगं वहन्तः | शश्वद विशः सवितुर दैव्यस्योपस्थे विश्वा भुवनानि तस्थुः ||
1.35.e: Drawing the gold-yoked car his Bays, white-footed, have manifested light to all the peoples.  Held in the lap of Savitar, divine One, all men, all beings have their place for ever.

1.35.d: तिस्रो दयावः सवितुर दवा उपस्थां एका यमस्य भुवने विराषाट | आणिं न रथ्यम अम्र्ताधि तस्थुर इह बरवीतु य उ तच चिकेतत ||
1.35.e: Three heavens there are; two Savitar's, adjacent: in Yama's world is one, the home of heroes,  As on a linch-pin, firm, rest things immortal: he who hath known it let him here declare it.

1.35.d: वि सुपर्णो अन्तरिक्षाण्य अख्यद गभीरवेपा असुरः सुनीथः | कवेदानीं सूर्यः कश चिकेत कतमां दयां रश्मिर अस्या ततान ||
1.35.e: He, strong of wing, hath lightened up the regions, deep-quivering Asura, the gentle Leader.  Where now is Sūrya, where is one to tell us to what celestial sphere his ray hath wandered?

1.35.d: अष्टौ वय अख्यत ककुभः पर्थिव्यास तरी धन्व योजना सप्त सिन्धून | हिरण्याक्षः सविता देव आगाद दधद रत्ना दाशुषे वार्याणि ||
1.35.e: The earth's eight points his brightness hath illumined, three desert regions and the Seven Rivers.  God Savitar the gold-eyed hath come hither, giving choice treasures unto him who worships.

1.35.d: हिरण्यपाणिः सविता विचर्षणिर उभे दयावाप्र्थिवी अन्तर ईयते | अपामीवाम बाधते वेति सूर्यम अभि कर्ष्णेन रजसा दयाम रणोति ||
1.35.e: The golden-handed Savitar, far-seeing, goes on his way between the earth and heaven,  Drives away sickness, bids the Sun approach us, and spreads the bright sky through the darksome region.

1.35.d: हिरण्यहस्तो असुरः सुनीथः सुम्र्ळीकः सववान यात्वर्वां | अपसेधन रक्षसो यातुधानानस्थाद देवः परतिदोषं गर्णानः ||
1.35.e: May he, gold-handed Asura, kind Leader, come hither to us with his help and favour.  Driving off Rākṣasas and Yātudhānas, the God is present, praised in hymns at evening.

1.35.d: ये ते पन्थाः सवितः पूर्व्यासो.अरेणवः सुक्र्ता अन्तरिक्षे | तेभिर्नो अद्य पथिभिः सुगेभी रक्षा च नो अधि च बरूहि देव ||
1.35.e: O Savitar, thine ancient dustless pathways are well established in the air's mid-region:  O God, come by those paths so fair to travel, preserve thou us from harm this day, and bless us.

1.36.d: पर वो यह्वं पुरूणां विशां देवयतीनाम | अग्निं सूक्तेभिर्वचोभिरीमहे यं सीमिदन्य ईळते ||
1.36.e: WITH words sent forth in holy hymns, Agni we supplicate, the Lord  Of many families who duly serve the Gods, yea, him whom others also praise.

1.36.d: जनासो अग्निं दधिरे सहोव्र्धं हविष्मन्तो विधेम ते | स तवं नो अद्य सुमना इहाविता भवा वाजेषु सन्त्य ||
1.36.e: Men have won Agni, him who makes their strength abound: we, with oblations, worship thee.  Our gracious-minded Helper in our deeds of might, be thou, O Excellent, this day.

1.36.d: पर तवा दूतं वर्णीमहे होतारं विश्ववेदसम | महस्ते सतो वि चरन्त्यर्चयो दिवि सप्र्शन्ति भानवः ||
1.36.e: Thee for our messenger we choose, thee, the Omniscient, for our Priest.  The flames of thee the mighty are spread wide around: thy splendour reaches to the sky.

1.36.d: देवासस्त्वा वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा सं दूतं परत्नमिन्धते | विश्वं सो अग्ने जयति तवया धनं यस्ते ददाश मर्त्यः ||
1.36.e: The Gods enkindle thee their ancient messenger,—Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman.  That mortal man, O Agni, gains through thee all wealth, who hath poured offerings unto thee.

1.36.d: मन्द्रो होता गर्हपतिरग्ने दूतो विशामसि | तवे विश्वा संगतानि वरता धरुवा यानि देवा अक्र्ण्वत ||
1.36.e: Thou, Agni, art a cheering Priest, Lord of the House, men's messenger:  All constant high decrees established by the Gods, gathered together, meet in thee.

1.36.d: तवे इदग्ने सुभगे यविष्ठ्य विश्वमा हूयते हविः | सत्वं नो अद्य सुमना उतापरं यक्षि देवान सुवीर्या ||
1.36.e: In thee, the auspicious One, O Agni, youthfullest, each sacred gift is offered up:  This day, and after, gracious, worship thou our Gods, that we may have heroic sons.

1.36.d: तं घेमित्था नमस्विन उप सवराजमासते | होत्राभिरग्निं मनुषः समिन्धते तितिर्वांसो अति सरिधः ||
1.36.e: To him in his own splendour bright draw near in worship the devout.  Men kindle Agni with their sacrificial gifts, victorious o’er the enemies.

1.36.d: घनन्तो वर्त्रमतरन रोदसी अप उरु कषयाय चक्रिरे | भुवत कण्वे वर्षा दयुम्न्याहुतः करन्ददश्वो गविष्टिषु ||
1.36.e: Vṛtra they smote and slew, and made the earth and heaven and firmament a wide abode.  The glorious Bull, invoked, hath stood at Kaṇva's side: loud neighed the Steed in frays for kine.

1.36.d: सं सीदस्व महानसि शोचस्व देववीतमः | वि धूममग्ने अरुषं मियेध्य सर्ज परशस्त दर्शतम ||
1.36.e: Seat thee, for thou art mighty; shine, best entertainer of the Gods.  Worthy of sacred food, praised Agni! loose the smoke, ruddy and beautiful to see.

1.36.d: यं तवा देवासो मनवे दधुरिह यजिष्ठं हव्यवाहन | यं कण्वो मेध्यातिथिर्धनस्प्र्तं यं वर्षा यमुपस्तुतः ||
1.36.e: Bearer of offerings, whom, best sacrificing Priest, the Gods for Manu's sake ordained;  Whom Kaṇva, whom Medhyātithi made the source of wealth, and Vṛṣan and Upastuta.

1.36.d: यमग्निं मेध्यातिथिः कण्व ईध रतादधि | तस्य परेषो दीदियुस्तमिमा रचस्तमग्निं वर्धयामसि ||
1.36.e: Him, Agni, whom Medhyātithi, whom Kaṇva kindled for his rite,  Him these our songs of praise, him, Agni, we extol: his powers shine out preeminent.

1.36.d: रायस पूर्धि सवधावो.अस्ति हि ते.अग्ने देवेष्वाप्यम | तवंवाजस्य शरुत्यस्य राजसि स नो मर्ळ महानसि ||
1.36.e: Make our wealth perfect thou, O Agni, Lord divine: for thou hast kinship with the Gods.  Thou rulest as a King o’er widely-famous strength: be good to us, for thou art great.

1.36.d: ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु ण ऊतये तिष्ठा देवो न सविता | ऊर्ध्वोवाजस्य सनिता यदञ्जिभिर्वाघद्भिर्विह्वयामहे ||
1.36.e: Stand up erect to lend us aid, stand up like Savitar the God:  Erect as strength-bestower we call aloud, with unguents and with priests, on thee.

1.36.d: ऊर्ध्वो नः पाह्यंहसो नि केतुना विश्वं समत्रिणं दह | कर्धी न ऊर्ध्वाञ्चरथाय जीवसे विदा देवेषु नो दुवः ||
1.36.e: Erect, preserve us from sore trouble; with thy flame burn thou each ravening demon dead.  Raise thou us up that we may walk and live: so thou shalt find our worship mid the Gods.

1.36.d: पाहि नो अग्ने रक्षसः पाहि धूर्तेरराव्णः | पाहि रीषत उत वा जिघांसतो बर्हद्भानो यविष्ठ्य ||
1.36.e: Preserve us, Agni, from the fiend, preserve us from malicious wrong.  Save us from him who fain would injure us or slay, Most Youthful, thou with lofty light.

1.36.d: घनेव विष्वग वि जह्यराव्णस्तपुर्जम्भ यो अस्मध्रुक | यो मर्त्यः शिशीते अत्यक्तुभिर्मा नः स रिपुरीशत ||
1.36.e: Smite down as with a club, thou who hast fire for teeth, smite thou the wicked, right and left.  Let not the man who plots against us in the night, nor any foe prevail o’er us.

1.36.d: अग्निर्वव्ने सुवीर्यमग्निः कण्वाय सौभगम | अग्निः परावन मित्रोत मेध्यातिथिमग्निः साता उपस्तुतम ||
1.36.e: Agni hath given heroic might to Kaṇva, and felicity:  Agni hath helped our friends, hath helped Medhyātithi, hath helped Upastuta to win.

1.36.d: अग्निना तुर्वशं यदुं परावत उग्रादेवं हवामहे | अग्निर्नयन नववास्त्वं बर्हद्रथं तुर्वीतिं दस्यवे सहः ||
1.36.e: We call on Ugradeva, Yadu, Turvaśa, by means of Agni, from afar;  Agni, bring Navavāstva and Bṛhadratha, Turvīti, to subdue the foe.

1.36.d: नि तवामग्ने मनुर्दधे जयोतिर्जनाय शश्वते | दीदेथ कण्व रतजात उक्षितो यं नमस्यन्ति कर्ष्टयः ||
1.36.e: Manu hath stablished thee a light, Agni, for all the race of men:  Sprung from the Law, oil-fed, for Kaṇva hast thou blazed, thou whom the people reverence.

1.36.d: तवेषासो अग्नेरमवन्तो अर्चयो भीमासो न परतीतये | रक्षस्विनः सदमिद यातुमावतो विश्वं समत्रिणं दह ||
1.36.e: The flames of Agni full of splendour and of might are fearful, not to be approached.  Consume for ever all demons and sorcerers, consume thou each devouring fiend.

1.37.d: करीळं वः शर्धो मारुतमनर्वाणं रथेशुभम | कण्वा अभि पर गायत ||
1.37.e: SING forth, O Kaṇvas, to your band of Maruts unassailable,  Sporting, resplendent on their car

1.37.d: ये पर्षतीभिर्र्ष्टिभिः साकं वाशीभिरञ्जिभिः | अजायन्त सवभानवः ||
1.37.e: They who, self-luminous, were born together, with the spotted deer,  Spears, swords, and glittering ornaments.

1.37.d: इहेव शर्ण्व एषां कशा हस्तेषु यद वदान | नि यामञ्चित्रं रञ्जते ||
1.37.e: One hears, as though ’twere close at hand, the cracking of the whips they hold  They gather glory on their way.

1.37.d: पर वः शर्धाय घर्ष्वये तवेषद्युम्नाय शुष्मिणे | देवत्तं बरह्म गायत ||
1.37.e: Now sing ye forth the God-given hymn to your exultant Marut host,  The fiercely-vigorous, the strong.

1.37.d: पर शंसा गोष्वघ्न्यं करीळं यच्छर्धो मारुतम | जम्भे रसस्य वाव्र्धे ||
1.37.e: Praise ye the Bull among the cows; for ’tis the Maruts’ sportive band:  It strengthened as it drank the rain.

1.37.d: को वो वर्षिष्ठ आ नरो दिवश्च गमश्च धूतयः | यत सीम अन्तं न धूनुथ ||
1.37.e: Who is your mightiest, Heroes, when, O shakers of the earth and heaven,  Ye shake them like a garment's hem?

1.37.d: नि वो यामाय मानुषो दध्र उग्राय मन्यवे | जिहीत पर्वतो गिरिः ||
1.37.e: At your approach man holds him down before the fury of your wrath:  The rugged-jointed mountain yields.

1.37.d: येषाम अज्मेषु पर्थिवी जुजुर्वां इव विश्पतिः | भिया यामेषु रेजते ||
1.37.e: They at whose racings forth the earth, like an age-weakened lord of men,  Trembles in terror on their ways.

1.37.d: सथिरं हि जानम एषां वयो मातुर निरेतवे | यत सीम अनु दविता शवः ||
1.37.e: Strong is their birth: vigour have they to issue from their Mother; strength,  Yea, even twice enough, is theirs.

1.37.d: उद उ तये सूनवो गिरः काष्ठा अज्मेष्व अत्नत | वाश्रा अभिज्ञु यातवे ||
1.37.e: And these, the Sons, the Singers, in their racings have enlarged the bounds,  So that the kine must walk knee-deep.

1.37.d: तयं चिद घा दीर्घम पर्थुम मिहो नपातम अम्र्ध्रम | पर चयावयन्ति यामभिः ||
1.37.e: Before them, on the ways they go, they drop this offspring of the cloud,  Long, broad, and inexhaustible.

1.37.d: मरुतो यद ध वो बलं जनां अचुच्यवीतन | गिरींर अचुच्यवीतन ||
1.37.e: O Maruts, as your strength is great, so have ye cast men down on earth,  So have ye made the mountains fall.

1.37.d: यद ध यान्ति मरुतः सं ह बरुवते ऽधवन्न आ | शर्णोति कश चिद एषाम ||
1.37.e: The while the Maruts pass along, they talk together on the way:  Doth any hear them as they speak?

1.37.d: पर यात शीभम आशुभिः सन्ति कण्वेषु वो दुवः | तत्रो षु मादयाध्वै ||
1.37.e: Come quick with swift steeds, for ye have worshippers among Kaṇva's sons  May you rejoice among them well.

1.37.d: अस्ति हि षमा मदाय वः समसि षमा वयम एषाम | विश्वं चिद आयुर जीवसे ||
1.37.e: All is prepared for your delight. We are their servants evermore,  To live as long as life may last.

1.38.d: कद ध नूनं कधप्रियः पिता पुत्रं न हस्तयोः | दधिध्वे वर्क्तबर्हिषः ||
1.38.e: WHAT now? When will ye take us by both hands, as a dear sire his son,  Gods, for whom sacred grass is clipped?

1.38.d: कव नूनं कद वो अर्थं गन्ता दिवो न पर्थिव्याः | कव वो गावो न रण्यन्ति ||
1.38.e: Now whither? To what goal of yours go ye in heaven, and not on earth?  Where do your cows disport themselves?

1.38.d: कव वः सुम्ना नव्यांसि मरुतः कव सुविता | कव विश्वानि सौभगा ||
1.38.e: Where are your newest favours shown? Where, Maruts, your prosperity?  Where all your high felicities?

1.38.d: यद यूयम पर्श्निमातरो मर्तासः सयातन | सतोता वो अम्र्तः सयात ||
1.38.e: If, O ye Maruts, ye the Sons whom Pṛśni bore, were mortal, and  Immortal he who sings your praise.

1.38.d: मा वो मर्गो न यवसे जरिता भूद अजोष्यः | पथा यमस्य गाद उप ||
1.38.e: Then never were your praiser loathed like a wild beast in pasture-land,  Nor should he go on Yama's path.

1.38.d: मो षु णः परा-परा निर्र्तिर दुर्हणा वधीत | पदीष्ट तर्ष्णया सह ||
1.38.e: Let not destructive plague on plague hard to be conquered, strike its down:  Let each, with drought, depart from us.

1.38.d: सत्यं तवेषा अमवन्तो धन्वञ चिद आ रुद्रियासः | मिहं कर्ण्वन्त्य अवाताम ||
1.38.e: Truly, they the fierce and mighty Sons of Rudra send their windless  Rain e’en on the desert places.

1.38.d: वाश्रेव विद्युन मिमाति वत्सं न माता सिषक्ति | यद एषां वर्ष्टिर असर्जि ||
1.38.e: Like a cow the lightning lows and follows, motherlike, her youngling,  When their rain-flood hath been loosened.

1.38.d: दिवा चित तमः कर्ण्वन्ति पर्जन्येनोदवाहेन | यत पर्थिवीं वयुन्दन्ति ||
1.38.e: When they inundate the earth they spread forth darkness e’en in day time,  With the water-laden rain-cloud.

1.38.d: अध सवनान मरुतां विश्वम आ सद्म पार्थिवम | अरेजन्त पर मानुषाः ||
1.38.e: O Maruts, at your voice's sound this earthly habitation shakes,  And each man reels who dwells therein.

1.38.d: मरुतो वीळुपाणिभिश चित्रा रोधस्वतीर अनु | यातेम अखिद्रयामभिः ||
1.38.e: O Maruts, with your strong-hoofed steeds, unhindered in their courses, haste  Along the bright embanked streams.

1.38.d: सथिरा वः सन्तु नेमयो रथा अश्वास एषाम | सुसंस्क्र्ता अभीशवः ||
1.38.e: Firm be the fellies of your wheels, steady your horses and your cars,  And may your reins be fashioned well.

1.38.d: अछा वदा तना गिरा जरायै बरह्मणस पतिम | अग्निम मित्रं न दर्शतम ||
1.38.e: Invite thou hither with this song, for praise, Agni the Lord of Prayer,  Him who is fair as Mitra is.

1.38.d: मिमीहि शलोकम आस्यपर्जन्य इव ततनः | गाय गायत्रम उक्थ्यम ||
1.38.e: Form in thy mouth the hymn of praise expand thee like, a rainy cloud  Sing forth the measured eulogy.

1.38.d: वन्दस्व मारुतं गणं तवेषम पनस्युम अर्किणम | अस्मे वर्द्धा असन्न इह ||
1.38.e: Sing glory to the Marut host, praiseworthy, tuneful, vigorous:  Here let the Strong Ones dwell with us.

1.39.d: पर यद इत्था परावतः शोचिर न मानम अस्यथ | कस्य करत्वा मरुतः कस्य वर्पसा कं याथ कं ह धूतयः ||
1.39.e: WHEN thus, like flame, from far away, Maruts, ye cast your measure forth,  To whom go Ye, to whom, O shakers of the earth, moved by whose wisdom, whose design?

1.39.d: सथिरा वः सन्त्व आयुधा पराणुदे वीळू उत परतिष्कभे | युष्माकम अस्तु तविषी पनीयसी मा मर्त्यस्य मायिनः ||
1.39.e: Strong let your weapons be to drive away your foes, firm for resistance let them be.  Yea, passing glorious must be your warrior might, not as a guileful mortal's strength.

1.39.d: परा ह यत सथिरं हथ नरो वर्तयथा गुरु | वि याथन वनिनः पर्थिव्या वय आशाः पर्वतानाम ||
1.39.e: When what is strong ye overthrow, and whirl about each ponderous thing,  Heroes, your course is through the forest trees of earth, and through the fissures of the rocks.

1.39.d: नहि वः शत्रुर विविदे अधि दयवि न भूम्यां रिशादसः | युष्माकम अस्तु तविषी तना युजा रुद्रासो नू चिद आध्र्षे ||
1.39.e: Consumers of your foes, no enemy of yours is found in heaven or on the earth:  Ye Rudras, may the strength, held in this bond, be yours, to bid defiance even now.

1.39.d: पर वेपयन्ति पर्वतान वि विञ्चन्ति वनस्पतीन | परो आरत मरुतो दुर्मदा इव देवासः सर्वया विशा ||
1.39.e: They make the mountains rock and reel, they rend the forest-kings apart.  Onward, ye Maruts, drive, like creatures drunk with wine, ye, Gods with all your company.

1.39.d: उपो रथेषु पर्षतीर अयुग्ध्वम परष्टिर वहति रोहितः | आ वो यामाय पर्थिवी चिद अश्रोद अबीभयन्त मानुषाः ||
1.39.e: Ye to your chariot have yoked the spotted deer: a red deer, as a leader, draws.  Even the Earth herself listened as ye came near, and men were sorely terrified.

1.39.d: आ वो मक्षू तनाय कं रुद्रा अवो वर्णीमहे | गन्ता नूनं नो ऽवसा यथा पुरेत्था कण्वाय बिभ्युषे ||
1.39.e: O Rudras, quickly we desire your succour for this work of ours.  Come to us with your aid as in the days of old, so now for frightened Kaṇva's sake.

1.39.d: युष्मेषितो मरुतो मर्त्येषित आ यो नो अभ्व ईषते | वि तं युयोत शवसा वय ओजसा वि युष्माकाभिर ऊतिभिः ||
1.39.e: Should any monstrous foe, O Maruts, sent by you or sent by mortals threaten us,  Tear ye him from us with your power and with your might, and with the succours that are yours.

1.39.d: असामि हि परयज्यवः कण्वं दद परचेतसः | असामिभिर्मरुत आ न ऊतिभिर्गन्ता वर्ष्तिं न विद्युतः ||
1.39.e: For ye, the worshipful and wise, have guarded Kaṇva perfectly.  O Maruts, come to us with full protecting help, as lightning flashes seek the rain.

1.39.d: असाम्योजो बिभ्र्था सुदानवो.असामि धूतयः शवः | रषिद्विषे मरुतः परिमन्यव इषुं न सर्जत दविषम ||
1.39.e: Whole strength have ye, O Bounteous Ones; perfect, earth-shakers, is your might.  Maruts, against the poet's wrathful enemy send ye an enemy like a dart.

1.40.d: उत तिष्ठ बरह्मणस पते देवयन्तस्त्वेमहे | उप पर यन्तु मरुतः सुदानव इन्द्र पराशूर्भवा सचा ||
1.40.e: O BRAHMAṆASPATI, stand up: God-serving men we pray to thee.  May they who give good gifts, the Maruts, come to us. Indra, most swift, be thou with them.

1.40.d: तवामिद धि सहसस पुत्र मर्त्य उपब्रूते धने हिते | सुवीर्यं मरुत आ सवश्व्यं दधीत यो व आचके ||
1.40.e: O Son of Strength, each mortal calls to thee for aid when spoil of battle waits for him.  O Maruts, may this man who loves you well obtain wealth of good steeds and hero might.

1.40.d: परैतु बरह्मणस पतिः पर देव्येतु सून्र्ता | अछा वीरंनर्यं पङकतिराधसं देवा यज्ञं नयन्तु नः ||
1.40.e: May Brahmaṇaspati draw nigh, may Sūnṛtā the Goddess come,  And Gods bring to this rite which gives the five-fold gift the Hero, lover of mankind.

1.40.d: यो वाघते ददाति सूनरं वसु स धत्ते अक्षिति शरवः | तस्मा इळां सुवीरामा यजामहे सुप्रतूर्तिमनेहसम ||
1.40.e: He who bestows a noble guerdon on the priest wins fame that never shall decay.  For him we offer sacred hero-giving food, peerless and conquering easily.

1.40.d: पर नूनं बरह्मणस पतिर्मन्त्रं वदत्युक्थ्यम | यस्मिन्निन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा देवा ओकांसि चक्रिरे ||
1.40.e: Now Brahmaṇaspati speaks forth aloud the solemn hymn of praise,  Wherein Indra and Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, the Gods, have made their dwelling place.

1.40.d: तमिद वोचेमा विदथेषु शम्भुवं मन्त्रं देवा अनेहसम | इमां च वाचं परतिहर्यथा नरो विश्वेद वामा वो अश्नवत ||
1.40.e: May we in holy synods, Gods! recite that hymn, peerless, that brings felicity.  If you, O Heroes, graciously accept this word, may it obtain all bliss from you.

1.40.d: को देवयन्तमश्नवज्जनं को वर्क्तबर्हिषम | पर-पर दाश्वान पस्त्याभिरस्थितान्तर्वावत कषयं दधे ||
1.40.e: Who shall approach the pious? who the man whose sacred grass is trimmed?  The offerer with his folk advances more and more: he fills his house with precious things.

1.40.d: उप कष्स्त्रं पर्ञ्चीत हन्ति राजभिर्भये चित सुक्षितिं दधे | नास्य वर्ता न तरुता महाधने नार्भे अस्ति वज्रिणः ||
1.40.e: He amplifies his lordly might, with kings he slays: e’en mid alarms he dwells secure  In great or lesser fight none checks him, none subdues,—the wielder of the thunderbolt.

1.41.d: यं रक्षन्ति परचेतसो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा | नू चित स दभ्यते जनः ||
1.41.e: NE’ER is he injured whom the Gods Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,  The excellently wise, protect.

1.41.d: यं बाहुतेव पिप्रति पान्ति मर्त्यं रिषः | अरिष्टः सर्व एधते ||
1.41.e: He prospers ever, free from scathe, whom they, as with full hands, enrich,  Whom they preserve from every foe.

1.41.d: वि दुर्गा वि दविषः पुरो घनन्ति राजान एषाम | नयन्ति दुरिता तिरः ||
1.41.e: The Kings drive far away from him his troubles and his enemies,  And lead him safely o’er distress.

1.41.d: सुगः पन्था अन्र्क्षर आदित्यास रतं यते | नात्रावखादो अस्ति वः ||
1.41.e: Thornless, Ādityas, is the path, easy for him who seeks the Law:  With him is naught to anger you.

1.41.d: यं यज्ञं नयथा नर आदित्या रजुना पथा | पर वः स धीतये नशत ||
1.41.e: What sacrifice, Ādityas, ye Heroes guide by the path direct,—  May that come nigh unto your thought.

1.41.d: स रत्नं मर्त्यो वसु विश्वं तोकमुत तमना | अछा गछत्यस्त्र्तः ||
1.41.e: That mortal, ever unsubdued, gains wealth and every precious thing,  And children also of his own.

1.41.d: कथा राधाम सखायः सतोमं मित्रस्यार्यम्णः | महि पसरो वरुणस्य ||
1.41.e: How, my friends, shall we prepare Aryaman's and Mitra's laud,  Glorious food of Varuṇa?

1.41.d: मा वो घनन्तं मा शपन्तं परति वोचे देवयन्तम | सुम्नैरिद व आ विवासे ||
1.41.e: I point not out to you a man who strikes the pious, or reviles:  Only with hymns I call you nigh.

1.41.d: चतुरश्चिद ददमानाद बिभीयादा निधातोः | न दुरुक्ताय सप्र्हयेत ||
1.41.e: Let him not love to speak ill words: but fear the One who holds all four  Within his hand, until they fall.

1.42.d: सं पूषन्नध्वनस्तिर वयंहो विमुचो नपात | सक्ष्वा देवप्र णस पुरः ||
1.42.e: SHORTEN our ways, O Pūṣan, move aside obstruction in the path:  Go close before us, cloud-born God.

1.42.d: यो नः पूषन्नघो वर्को दुःशेव आदिदेशति | अप सम तम्पथो जहि ||
1.42.e: Drive, Pūṣan, from our road the wolf, the wicked inauspicious wolf,  Who lies in wait to injure us.

1.42.d: अप तयं परिपन्थिनं मुषीवाणं हुरश्चितम | दूरमधिस्रुतेरज ||
1.42.e: Who lurks about the path we take, the robber with a guileful heart:  Far from the road chase him away.

1.42.d: तवं तस्य दवयाविनो.अघशंसस्य कस्य चित | पदाभि तिष्ठ तपुषिम ||
1.42.e: Tread with thy foot and trample out the firebrand of the wicked one,  The double-tongued, whoe’er he be.

1.42.d: आ तत ते दस्र मन्तुमः पूषन्नवो वर्णीमहे | येन पितॄनचोदयः ||
1.42.e: Wise Pūṣan, Wonder-Worker, we claim of thee now the aid wherewith  Thou furtheredst our sires of old.

1.42.d: अधा नो विश्वसौभग हिरण्यवाशीमत्तम | धनानि सुषणा कर्धि ||
1.42.e: So, Lord of all prosperity, best wielder of the golden sword,  Make riches easy to be won.

1.42.d: अति नः सश्चतो नय सुगा नः सुपथा कर्णु | पूषन्निहक्रतुं विदः ||
1.42.e: Past all pursuers lead us, make pleasant our path and fair to tread:  O Pūṣan, find thou power for this.

1.42.d: अभि सूयवसं नय न नवज्वारो अध्वने | पूषन्निहक्रतुं विदः ||
1.42.e: Lead us to meadows rich in grass: send on our way no early heat:  O Pūṣan, find thou power for this.

1.42.d: शग्धि पूर्धि पर यंसि च शिशीहि परास्युदरम | पूषन्निहक्रतुं विदः ||
1.42.e: Be gracious to us, fill us full, give, feed us, and invigorate:  O Pūṣan, find thou power for this.

1.42.d: न पूषणं मेथामसि सूक्तैरभि गर्णीमसि | वसूनि दस्ममीमहे ||
1.42.e: No blame have we for Pūṣan; him we magnify with songs of praise:  We seek the Mighty One for wealth.

1.43.d: कद रुद्राय परचेतसे मीळ्हुष्टमाय तव्यसे | वोचेम शन्तमं हर्दे ||
1.43.e: WHAT shall we sing to Rudra, strong, most bounteous, excellently wise,  That shall be dearest to his heart?

1.43.d: यथा नो अदितिः करत पश्वे नर्भ्यो यथा गवे | यथा तोकाय रुद्रियम ||
1.43.e: That Aditi may grant the grace of Rudra to our folk, our kine,  Our cattle and our progeny;

1.43.d: यथा नो मित्रो वरुणो यथा रुद्रश्चिकेतति | यथा विश्वे सजोषसः ||
1.43.e: That Mitra and that Varuṇa, that Rudra may remember us,  Yea, all the Gods with one accord.

1.43.d: गाथपतिं मेधपतिं रुद्रं जलाषभेषजम | तच्छंयोः सुम्नमीमहे ||
1.43.e: To Rudra Lord of sacrifice, of hymns and balmy medicines,  We pray for joy and health and strength.

1.43.d: यः शुक्र इव सूर्यो हिरण्यमिव रोचते | शरेष्ठो देवानां वसुः ||
1.43.e: He shines in splendour like the Sun, refulgent as bright gold is he,  The good, the best among the Gods.

1.43.d: शं नः करत्यर्वते सुगं मेषाय मेष्ये | नर्भ्यो नारिभ्यो गवे ||
1.43.e: May he grant health into our steeds, wellbeing to our rams and ewes,  To men, to women, and to kine.

1.43.d: अस्मे सोम शरियमधि नि धेहि शतस्य नर्णाम | महि शरवस्तुविन्र्म्णम ||
1.43.e: O Soma, set thou upon us the glory of a hundred men,  The great renown of mighty chiefs.

1.43.d: मा नः सोमपरिबाधो मारातयो जुहुरन्त | आ न इन्दो वाजे भज ||
1.43.e: Let not malignities, nor those who trouble Soma, hinder us.  Indu, give us a share of strength.

1.43.d: यास्ते परजा अम्र्तस्य परस्मिन धामन्न्र्तस्य | मूर्धा नाभा सोम वेन आभूषन्तीः सोम वेदः ||
1.43.e: Soma! head, central point, love these; Soma! know these as serving thee,  Children of thee Immortal, at the highest place of holy law.

1.44.d: अग्ने विवस्वदुषसश्चित्रं राधो अमर्त्य | आ दाशुषे जातवेदो वहा तवमद्या देवानुषर्बुधः ||
1.44.e: IMMORTAL Jātavedas, thou many-hued fulgent gift of Dawn,  Agni, this day to him who pays oblations bring the Gods who waken with the morn.

1.44.d: जुष्टो हि दूतो असि हव्यवाहनो.अग्ने रथीरध्वराणाम | सजूरश्विभ्यामुषसा सुवीर्यमस्मे धेहि शरवो बर्हत ||
1.44.e: For thou art offering-bearer and loved messenger, the charioteer of sacrifice:  Accordant with the Aśvins and with Dawn grant us heroic strength and lofty fame.

1.44.d: अद्या दूतं वर्णीमहे वसुमग्निं पुरुप्रियम | धूमकेतुं भार्जीकं वयुष्टिषु यज्ञानामध्वरश्रियम ||
1.44.e: As messenger we choose to-day Agni the good whom many love,  Smoke-bannered spreader of the light, at break of day glory of sacrificial rites.

1.44.d: शरेष्ठं यविष्ठमतिथिं सवाहुतं जुष्टं जनाय दाशुषे | देवानछा यातवे जातवेदसमग्निमीळे वयुष्टिषु ||
1.44.e: Him noblest and most youthful, richly worshipped guest, dear to the men who offer gifts,  Him, Agni Jātavedas, I beseech at dawn that he may bring the Gods to us.

1.44.d: सतविष्यामि तवामहं विश्वस्याम्र्त भोजन | अग्ने तरातारमम्र्तं मियेध्य यजिष्ठं हव्यवाहन ||
1.44.e: Thee, Agni, will I glorify, deathless nourisher of the world,  Immortal, offering-bearer, meet for sacred food, preserver, best at sacrifice.

1.44.d: सुशंसो बोधि गर्णते यविष्ठ्य मधुजिह्वः सवाहुतः | परस्कण्वस्य परतिरन्नायुर्जीवसे नमस्या दैव्यं जनम ||
1.44.e: Tell good things to thy praiser, O most youthful God, as richly worshipped, honey-tongued,  And, granting to Praskaṇva lengthened days of life, show honour to the Heavenly Host.

1.44.d: होतारं विश्ववेदसं सं हि तवा विश इन्धते | स आ वह पुरुहूत परचेतसो.अग्ने देवानिह दरवत ||
1.44.e: For the men, Agni, kindle thee as all possessor and as Priest;  So Agni, much-invoked, bring hither with all speed the Gods, the excellently wise,

1.44.d: सवितारमुषसमश्विना भगमग्निं वयुष्टिषु कषपः | कण्वासस्त्वा सुतसोमास इन्धते हव्यवाहं सवध्वर ||
1.44.e: At dawn of day, at night, Uṣas and Savitar, the Aśvins, Bhaga, Agni's self:  Skilled in fair rites, with Soma poured, the Kaṇvas light thee, the oblation-wafting God.

1.44.d: पतिर हि अध्वराणाम अग्ने दूतो विशाम असि | उषर्बुध आवह सोमपीतये देवानद्य सवर्द्र्शः ||
1.44.e: For, Agni, Lord of sacrifice and messenger of men art thou:  Bring thou the Gods who wake at dawn who see the light, this day to drink the Soma juice.

1.44.d: अग्ने पूर्वा अनूषसो विभावसो दीदेथ विश्वदर्षतः | असि गरामेष्वविता पुरोहितो.असि यज्ञेषु मानुषः ||
1.44.e: Thou shonest forth, O Agni, after former dawns, all visible, O rich in light.  Thou art our help in battle-strife, the Friend of man, the great high priest in sacrifice.

1.44.d: नि तवा यज्ञस्य साधनमग्ने होतारं रत्विजम | मनुष्वद देव धीमहि परचेतसं जीरं दूतममर्त्यम ||
1.44.e: Like Manu, we will stablish thee, Agni, performer of the rite,  Invoker, ministering Priest, exceeding wise, the swift immortal messenger.

1.44.d: यद देवानां मित्रमहः पुरोहितो.अन्तरो यासि दूत्यम | सिन्धोरिव परस्वनितास ऊर्मयो.अग्नेर्भ्राजन्ते अर्चयः ||
1.44.e: When as the Gods’ High Priest, by many loved, thou dost their mission as their nearest Friend,  Then, like the far-resounding billows of the flood, thy flames, O Agni, roar aloud.

1.44.d: शरुधि शरुत्कर्ण वह्निभिर्देवैरग्ने सयावभिः | आ सीदन्तु बर्हिषि मित्रो अर्यमा परातर्यावाणो अध्वरम ||
1.44.e: Hear, Agni, who hast ears to hear, with all thy train of escort Gods;  Let Mitra, Aryaman, seeking betimes our rite, seat them upon the sacred grass.

1.44.d: शर्ण्वन्तु सतोमं मरुतः सुदानवो.अग्निजिह्वा रताव्र्धः | पिबतु सोमं वरुणो धर्तव्रतो.अश्विभ्यामुषसा सजूः ||
1.44.e: Let those who strengthen Law, who bountifully give, the life-tongued Maruts, hear our praise.  May Law-supporting Varuṇa with the Aśvins twain and Uṣas, drink the Soma juice.

1.45.d: तवमग्ने वसून्रिह रुद्रानादित्यानुत | यजा सवध्वरं जनं मनुजातं घर्तप्रुषम ||
1.45.e: WORSHIP the Vasus, Agni! here, the Rudras, the Ādityas, all  Who spring from Manu, those who know fair rites, who pour their blessings down.

1.45.d: शरुष्टीवानो हि दाशुषे देवा अग्ने विचेतसः | तान रोहिदश्व गिर्वणस्त्रयस्त्रिंशतमा वह ||
1.45.e: Agni, the Gods who understand give ear unto the worshipper:  Lord of Red Steeds, who lovest song, bring thou those Three-and-Thirty Gods.

1.45.d: परियमेधवदत्रिवज्जातवेदो विरूपवत | अङगिरस्वन महिव्रत परस्कण्वस्य शरुधी हवम ||
1.45.e: O Jātavedas, great in act, hearken thou to Praskaṇva's call,  As Priyamedha erst was heard, Atri, Virūpa, Aṅgiras.

1.45.d: महिकेरव ऊतये परियमेधा अहूषत | राजन्तमध्वराणामग्निं शुक्रेण शोचिषा ||
1.45.e: The sons of Priyamedha skilled in lofty praise have called for help  On Agni who with fulgent flame is Ruler of all holy rites.

1.45.d: घर्ताहवन सन्त्येमा उ षु शरुधी गिरः | याभिः कण्वस्य सूनवो हवन्ते.अवसे तवा ||
1.45.e: Hear thou, invoked with holy oil, bountiful giver of rewards,  These eulogies, whereby the sons of Kaṇva call thee to their aid.

1.45.d: तवां चित्रश्रवस्तम हवन्ते विक्षु जन्तवः | शोचिष्केशम्पुरुप्रियाग्ने हव्याय वोळ्हवे ||
1.45.e: O Agni, loved by many, thou of fame most wondrous, in their homes  Men call on thee whose hair is flame, to be the bearer of their gifts.

1.45.d: नि तवा होतारं रत्विजं दधिरे वसुवित्तमम | शरुत्कर्णं सप्रथस्तमं विप्रा अग्ने दिविष्टिषु ||
1.45.e: Thee, Agni, best to find out wealth, most widely famous, quick to hear,  Singers have stablished in their rites Herald and ministering Priest.

1.45.d: आ तवा विप्रा अचुच्यवुः सुतसोमा अभि परयः | बर्हद भा बिभ्रतो हविरग्ने मर्ताय दाशुषे ||
1.45.e: Singers with Soma pressed have made thee, Agni, hasten to the feast,  Great light to mortal worshipper, what time they bring the sacred gift.

1.45.d: परातर्याव्णः सहस्क्र्त सोमपेयाय सन्त्य | इहाद्य दैव्यंजनं बर्हिरा सादया वसो ||
1.45.e: Good, bounteous, Son of Strength, this day seat here on sacred grass the Gods  Who come at early morn, the host of heaven, to drink the Soma juice

1.45.d: अर्वाञ्चं दैव्यं जनमग्ने यक्ष्व सहूतिभिः | अयं सोमः सुदानवस्तं पात तिरोह्न्यम ||
1.45.e: Bring with joint invocations thou, O Agni, the celestial host:  Here stands the Soma, bounteous Gods drink this expressed ere yesterday.

1.46.d: एषो उषा अपूर्व्य वयुछति परिया दिवः | सतुषे वामश्विना बर्हत ||
1.46.e: Now Morning with her earliest light shines forth, dear Daughter of the Sky:  High, Aśvins, I extol your praise,

1.46.d: या दस्रा सिन्धुमातरा मनोतरा रयीणाम | धिया देवा वसुविदा ||
1.46.e: Sons of the Sea, mighty to save discoverers of riches, ye  Gods with deep thought who find out wealth.

1.46.d: वच्यन्ते वां ककुहासो जूर्णायामधि विष्टपि | यद वांरथो विभिष पतात ||
1.46.e: Your giant coursers hasten on over the region all in flames,  When your car flies with winged steeds.

1.46.d: हविषा जारो अपां पिपर्ति पपुरिर्नरा | पिता कुटस्य चर्षणिः ||
1.46.e: He, liberal, lover of the flood, Lord of the House, the vigilant,  Chiefs! with oblations feeds you full.

1.46.d: आदारो वां मतीनां नासत्या मतवचसा | पातं सोमस्य धर्ष्णुया ||
1.46.e: Ye have regard unto our hymns, Nāsatyas, thinking of our words:  Drink boldly of the Soma juice.

1.46.d: या नः पीपरदश्विना जयोतिष्मती तमस्तिरः | तामस्मे रासाथामिषम ||
1.46.e: Vouchsafe to us, O Aśvin Pair, such strength as, with attendant light,  May through the darkness carry us.

1.46.d: आ नो नावा मतीनां यातं पाराय गन्तवे | युञ्जाथामश्विना रथम ||
1.46.e: Come in the ship of these our hymns to bear you to the hither shore  O Aśvins, harness ye the car.

1.46.d: अरित्रं वां दिवस पर्थु तीर्थे सिन्धूनां रथः | धिया युयुज्र इन्दवः ||
1.46.e: The heaven's wide vessel is your own on the flood's shore your chariot waits  Drops, with the hymn, have been prepared.

1.46.d: दिवस कण्वास इन्दवो वसु सिन्धूनां पदे | सवं वव्रिं कुह धित्सथः ||
1.46.e: Kaṇvas, the drops are in the heaven; the wealth is at the waters' place:  Where will ye manifest your form?

1.46.d: अभूदु भा उ अंशवे हिरण्यं परति सूर्यः | वयख्यज्जिह्वयासितः ||
1.46.e: Light came to lighten up the branch, the Sun appeared as it were gold:  And with its tongue shone forth the dark.

1.46.d: अभूदु पारमेतवे पन्था रतय्स साधुया | अदर्शि वि सरुतिर्दिवः ||
1.46.e: The path of sacrifice was made to travel to the farther goal:  The road of heaven was manifest.

1.46.d: तत-तदिदश्विनोरवो जरिता परति भूषति | मदे सोमस्यपिप्रतोः ||
1.46.e: The singer of their praise awaits whatever grace the Aśvins give,  who save when Soma gladdens them.

1.46.d: वावसाना विवस्वति सोमस्य पीत्या गिरा | मनुष्वच्छम्भूा गतम ||
1.46.e: Ye dwellers with Vivasvān come, auspicious, as to Manu erst;  come to the Soma and our praise.

1.46.d: युवोरुषा अनु शरियं परिज्मनोरुपाचरत | रता वनथो अक्तुभिः ||
1.46.e: O circumambient Aśvins, Dawn follows the brightness of your way:  Approve with beams our solemn rites.

1.46.d: उभा पिबतमश्विनोभा नः शर्म यछतम | अविद्रियाभिरूतिभिः ||
1.46.e: Drink ye of our libations, grant protection, O ye Aśvins Twain,  With aids which none may interrupt.

1.47.d: अयं वां मधुमत्तमः सुतः सोम रताव्र्धा | तमश्विना पिबतं तिरोह्न्यं धत्तं रत्नानि दाशुशे ||
1.47.e: AŚVINS, for you who strengthen Law this sweetest Soma hath been shed.  Drink this expressed ere yesterday and give riches to him who offers it.

1.47.d: तरिवन्धुरेण तरिव्र्ता सुपेशसा रथेना यातमश्विना | कण्वासो वां बरह्म कर्ण्वन्त्यध्वरे तेषां सु शर्णुतं हवम ||
1.47.e: Come, O ye Aśvins, mounted on your triple car three-seated, beautiful of form  To you at sacrifice the Kaṇvas send the prayer: graciously listen to their call.

1.47.d: अश्विना मधुमत्तमं पातं सोमं रताव्र्धा | अथाद्य दस्रा वसु बिभ्रता रथे दाश्वांसमुप गछतम ||
1.47.e: O Aśvins, ye who strengthen Law, drink ye this sweetest Soma juice.  Borne on your wealth-fraught car come ye this day to him who offers, ye of wondrous deeds.

1.47.d: तरिषधस्थे बर्हिषि विश्ववेदसा मध्वा यज्ञं मिमिक्षतम | कण्वासो वां सुतसोमा अभिद्यवो युवां हवन्ते अश्विना ||
1.47.e: Omniscient Aśvins, on the thrice-heaped grass bedew with the sweet juice the sacrifice.  The sons of Kaṇva, striving heavenward, call on you with draughts of Soma juice out-poured.

1.47.d: याभिः कण्वमभिष्टिभिः परावतं युवमश्विना | ताभिः षवस्मानवतं शुभस पती पातं सोमं रताव्र्धा ||
1.47.e: O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye guarded Kaṇva carefully,  Keep us, O Lords of Splendour: drink the Soma juice, ye strengtheners of holy law.

1.47.d: सुदासे दस्रा वसु बिभ्रता रथे पर्क्षो वहतमश्विना | रयिं समुद्रादुत वा दिवस पर्यस्मे धत्तं पुरुस्प्र्हम ||
1.47.e: O Mighty Ones, ye gave Sudās abundant food, brought on your treasure-laden car;  So now vouchsafe to us the wealth which many crave, either from heaven or from the sea.

1.47.d: यन नासत्या परावति यद वा सथो अधि तुर्वशे | अतो रथेन सुव्र्ता न आ गतं साकं सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिः ||
1.47.e: Nāsatyas, whether ye be far away or close to Turvaśa,  Borne on your lightly-rolling chariot come to us, together with the sunbeams come.

1.47.d: अर्वाञ्चा वां सप्तयो.अध्वरश्रियो वहन्तु सवनेदुप | इषं पर्ञ्चन्ता सुक्र्ते सुदानव आ बर्हिः सीदतं नरा ||
1.47.e: So let your coursers, ornaments of sacrifice, bring you to our libations here.  Bestowing food on him who acts and gives aright, sit, Chiefs, upon the sacred grass.

1.47.d: तेन नासत्या गतं रथेन सूर्यत्वचा | येन शश्वदूहथुर्दाशुषे वसु मध्वः सोमस्य पीतये ||
1.47.e: Come, O Nāsatyas, on your car decked with a sunbright canopy,  Whereon ye ever bring wealth to the worshipper, to drink the Soma's pleasant juice.

1.47.d: उक्थेभिरर्वागवसे पुरूवसू अर्कैश्च नि हवयामहे | शश्वत कण्वानां सदसि परिये हि कं सोमं पपथुरश्विना ||
1.47.e: With lauds and songs of praise we call them down to us, that they, most rich, may succour us;  For ye have ever in the Kaṇvas' well-loved house, O Aśvins, drunk the Soma juice.

1.48.d: सह वामेन न उषो वयुछा दुहितर्दिवः | सह दयुम्नेन बर्हता विभावरि राया देवि दास्वती ||
1.48.e: DAWN on us with prosperity, O Uṣas, Daughter of the Sky,  Dawn with great glory, Goddess, Lady of the Light, dawn thou with riches, Bounteous One.

1.48.d: अश्वावतीर्गोमतीर्विश्वसुविदो भूरि चयवन्त वस्तवे | उदीरय परति मा सून्र्ता उषश्चोद राधो मघोनाम ||
1.48.e: They, bringing steeds and kine, boon-givers of all wealth, have oft sped forth to lighten us.  O Uṣas, waken up for me the sounds of joy: send us the riches of the great.

1.48.d: उवासोषा उछाच्च नु देवी जीरा रथानाम | ये अस्या आचरणेषु दध्रिरे समुद्रे न शरवस्यवः ||
1.48.e: Uṣas hath dawned, and now shall dawn, the Goddess, driver forth of cars  Which, as she cometh nigh, have fixed their thought on her, like glory-seekers on the flood.

1.48.d: उषो ये ते पर यामेषु युञ्जते मनो दानाय सूरयः | अत्राह तत कण्व एषां कण्वतमो नाम गर्णाति नर्णाम ||
1.48.e: Here Kaṇva, chief of Kaṇva's race, sings forth aloud the glories of the heroes’ names,—  The. princes who, O Uṣas, as thou comest near, direct their thoughts to liberal gifts.

1.48.d: आ घा योषेव सूनर्युषा याति परभुञ्जती | जरयन्ती वर्जनं पद्वदीयत उत पातयति पक्षिणः ||
1.48.e: Like a good matron Uṣas comes carefully tending everything:  Rousing all life she stirs all creatures that have feet, and makes the birds of air fly up.

1.48.d: वि या सर्जति समनं वयर्थिनः पदां न वेत्योदती | वयो नकिष टे पप्तिवांस आसते वयुष्टौ वाजिनीवति ||
1.48.e: She sends the busy forth, each man to his pursuit: delay she knows not as she springs.  O rich in opulence, after thy dawning birds that have flown forth no longer rest.

1.48.d: एषायुक्त परावतः सूर्यस्योदयनादधि | शतं रथेभिः सुभगोषा इयं वि यात्यभि मानुषान ||
1.48.e: This Dawn hath yoked her steeds afar, beyond the rising of the Sun:  Borne on a hundred chariots she, auspicious Dawn, advances on her way to Men.

1.48.d: विश्वमस्या नानाम चक्षसे जगज्ज्योतिष कर्णोति सूनरी | अप दवेषो मघोनी दुहिता दिव उषा उछदप सरिधः ||
1.48.e: To meet her glance all living creatures bend them down: Excellent One, she makes the light.  Uṣas, the Daughter of the Sky, the opulent, shines foes and enmities away.

1.48.d: उष आ भाहि भानुना चन्द्रेण दुहितर्दिवः | आवहन्ती भूर्यस्मभ्यं सौभगं वयुछन्ती दिविष्टिषु ||
1.48.e: Shine on us with thy radiant light, O Uṣas, Daughter of the Sky,  Bringing to us great store of high felicity, and beaming on our solemn rites.

1.48.d: विश्वस्य हि पराणनं जीवनं तवे वि यदुछसि सूनरि | सा नो रथेन बर्हता विभावरि शरुधि चित्रामघे हवम ||
1.48.e: For in thee is each living creature's breath and life, when, Excellent! thou dawnest forth.  Borne on thy lofty car, O Lady of the Light, hear, thou of wondrous wealth, our call.

1.48.d: उषो वाजं हि वंस्व यश्चित्रो मानुषे जने | तेना वह सुक्र्तो अध्वरानुप ये तवा गर्णन्ति वह्नयः ||
1.48.e: O Uṣas, win thyself the strength which among men is wonderful.  Bring thou thereby the pious unto holy rites, those who as priests sing praise to thee.

1.48.d: विश्वान देवाना वह सोमपीतये.अन्तरिक्षादुषस्त्वम | सास्मासु धा गोमदश्वावदुक्थ्यमुषो वाजं सुवीर्यम ||
1.48.e: Bring from the firmament, O Uṣas, all the Gods, that they may drink our Soma juice,  And, being what thou art, vouchsafe us kine and steeds, strength meet for praise and hero might.

1.48.d: यस्या रुशन्तो अर्चयः परति भद्रा अद्र्क्षत | सा नो रयिं विश्ववारं सुपेशसमुषा ददातु सुग्म्यम ||
1.48.e: May Uṣas whose auspicious rays are seen resplendent round about,  Grant us great riches, fair in form, of all good things, wealth which light labour may attain.

1.48.d: ये चिद धि तवां रषयः पूर्व ऊतये जुहूरे.अवसे महि | सा न सतोमानभि गर्णीहि राधसोषः शुक्रेण शोचिषा ||
1.48.e: Mighty One, whom the Ṛṣis of old time invoked for their protection and their help,  O Uṣas, graciously answer our songs of praise with bounty and with brilliant light.

1.48.d: उषो यदद्य भानुना वि दवाराव रणवो दिवः | पर नो यछतादव्र्कं पर्थु छर्दिः पर देवि गोमतीरिषः ||
1.48.e: Uṣas, as thou with light to day hast opened the twin doors of heaven,  So grant thou us a dwelling wide and free from foes. O Goddess, give us food with kine.

1.48.d: सं नो राया बर्हता विश्वपेशसा मिमिक्ष्वा समिळाभिरा | सं दयुम्नेन विश्वतुरोषो महि सं वाजैर्वाजिनीवति ||
1.48.e: Bring us to wealth abundant, sent in every shape, to plentiful refreshing food,  To all-subduing splendour, Uṣas, Mighty One, to strength, thou rich in spoil and wealth.

1.49.d: उषो भद्रेभिरा गहि दिवश्चिद रोचनादधि | वहन्त्वरुणप्सव उप तवा सोमिनो गर्हम ||
1.49.e: E'EN from above the sky's bright realm come, Uṣas, by auspicious ways:  Let red steeds bear thee to the house of him who pours the Soma, juice.

1.49.d: सुपेशसं सुखं रथं यमध्यस्था उषस्त्वम | तेना सुश्रवसं जनं परावाद्य दुहितर्दिवः ||
1.49.e: The chariot which thou mountest, fair of shape, O Uṣas light to move,—  Therewith, O Daughter of the Sky, aid men of noble fame today.

1.49.d: वयश्चित ते पतत्रिणो दविपच्चतुष्पदर्जुनि | उषः परारन्न्र्तून्रनु दिवो अन्तेभ्यस परि ||
1.49.e: Bright Uṣas, when thy times return, all quadrupeds and bipeds stir,  And round about flock winged birds from all the boundaries of heaven.

1.49.d: वयुछन्ती हि रश्मिभिर्विश्वमाभासि रोचनम | तां तवामुषर्वसूयवो गीर्भिः कण्वा अहूषत ||
1.49.e: Thou dawning with thy beams of light illumest all the radiant realm.  Thee, as thou art, the Kaṇvas, fain for wealth, have called with sacred songs.

1.50.d: उदु तयं जातवेदसं देवं वहन्ति केतवः | दर्शे विश्वाय सूर्यम ||
1.50.e: HIS bright rays bear him up aloft, the God who knoweth all that lives,  Sūrya, that all may look on him.

1.50.d: अप तये तायवो यथा नक्षत्रा यन्त्यक्तुभिः | सूराय विश्वचक्षसे ||
1.50.e: The constellations pass away, like thieves, together with their beams,  Before the all-beholding Sun.

1.50.d: अद्र्श्रमस्य केतवो वि रश्मयो जनाननु | भराजन्तो अग्नयो यथा ||
1.50.e: His herald rays are seen afar refulgent o’er the world of men,  Like flames of fire that burn and blaze.
Swift and all beautiful art thou, O Sūrya, maker of the light,  Illuming all the radiant realm.

1.50.d: परत्यं देवानां विशः परत्यङङ उदेषि मानुषान | परत्यं विश्वं सवर्द्र्शे ||
1.50.e: Thou goest to the hosts of Gods, thou comest hither to mankind,  Hither all light to be beheld.

1.50.d: येना पावक चक्षसा भुरण्यन्तं जनाननु | तवं वरुण पश्यसि ||
1.50.e: With that same eye of thine wherewith thou lookest brilliant Varuṇa,  Upon the busy race of men,

1.50.d: वि दयामेषि रजस पर्थ्वहा मिमानो अक्तुभिः | पश्यञ जन्मानि सूर्य ||
1.50.e: Traversing sky and wide mid-air, thou metest with thy beams our days,  Sun, seeing all things that have birth.

1.50.d: सप्त तवा हरितो रथे वहन्ति देव सूर्य | शोचिष्केशं विचक्षण ||
1.50.e: Seven Bay Steeds harnessed to thy car bear thee, O thou farseeing One,  God, Sūrya, with the radiant hair.

1.50.d: अयुक्त सप्त शुन्ध्युवः सूरो रथस्य नप्त्यः | ताभिर्याति सवयुक्तिभिः ||
1.50.e: Sūrya hath yoked the pure bright Seven, the daughters of the car; with these,  His own dear team, he goeth forth.

1.50.d: उद वयं तमसस परि जयोतिष पश्यन्त उत्तरम | देवं देवत्रा सूर्यमगन्म जयोतिरुत्तमम ||
1.50.e: Looking upon the loftier light above the darkness we have come  To Sūrya, God among the Gods, the light that is most excellent.

1.50.d: उद्यन्नद्य मित्रमह आरोहन्नुत्तरां दिवम | हर्द्रोगं ममसूर्य हरिमाणं च नाशय ||
1.50.e: Rising this day, O rich in friends, ascending to the loftier heaven,  Sūrya remove my heart's disease, take from me this my yellow hue.

1.50.d: शुकेषु मे हरिमाणं रोपणाकासु दध्मसि | अथो हारिद्रवेषु मे हरिमाणं नि दध्मसि ||
1.50.e: To parrots and to starlings let us give away my yellowness,  Or this my yellowness let us transfer to Haritāla trees.

1.50.d: उदगादयमादित्यो विश्वेन सहसा सह | दविषन्तं मह्यं रन्धयन मो अहम दविषते रधम ||
1.50.e: With all his conquering vigour this Āditya hath gone up on high,  Giving my foe into mine hand: let me not be my foeman's prey.

1.51.d: अभि तयं मेषं पुरुहूतं रग्मियमिन्द्रं गीर्भिर्मदता वस्वो अर्णवम | यस्य दयावो न विचरन्ति मानुषा भुजे मंहिष्ठमभि विप्रमर्चत ||
1.51.e: MAKE glad with songs that Ram whom many men invoke, worthy of songs of praise, Indra, the sea of wealth;  Whose gracious deeds for men spread like the heavens abroad: sing praise to him the Sage, most liberal for our good.

1.51.d: अभीमवन्वन सवभिष्टिमूतयो.अन्तरिक्षप्रां तविषीभिराव्र्तम | इन्द्रं दक्षास रभवो मदच्युतं शतक्रतुं जवनी सून्र्तारुहत ||
1.51.e: As aids the skilful Ṛbhus yearned to Indra strong to save, who fills mid-air, encompassed round with might,  Rushing in rapture; and o’er Śatakratu came the gladdening shout that urged him on to victory.

1.51.d: तवं गोत्रमङगिरोभ्यो.अव्र्णोरपोतात्रये शतदुरेषु गातुवित | ससेन चिद विमदायावहो वस्वाजावद्रिं वावसानस्यनर्तयन ||
1.51.e: Thou hast disclosed the kine's stall for the Aṅgirases, and made a way for Atri by a hundred doors.  On Vimada thou hast bestowed both food and wealth, making thy bolt dance in the sacrificer's fight.

1.51.d: तवमपामपिधानाव्र्णोर अपाधारयः पर्वते दानुमद वसु | वर्त्रं यदिन्द्र शवसावधीरहिमादित सूर्यं दिव्यारोहयो दर्शे ||
1.51.e: Thou hast unclosed the prisons of the waters; thou hast in the mountain seized the treasure rich in gifts.  When thou hadst slain with might the dragon Vṛtra, thou, Indra, didst raise the Sun in heaven for all to see.

1.51.d: तवं मायाभिरप मायिनो.अधमः सवधाभिर्ये अधि शुप्तावजुह्वत | तवं पिप्रोर्न्र्मणः परारुजः पुरः पर रजिश्वानं दस्युहत्येष्वाविथ ||
1.51.e: With wondrous might thou blewest enchanter fiends away, with powers celestial those who called on thee in jest.  Thou, hero-hearted, hast broken down Pipru's forts, and helped Ṛjiśvan when the Dasyus were struck dead.

1.51.d: तवं कुत्सं शुष्णहत्येष्वाविथारन्धयो.अतिथिग्वाय शम्बरम | महान्तं चिदर्बुदं नि करमीः पदा सनादेव दस्युहत्याय जज्ञिषे ||
1.51.e: Thou savedst Kutsa when Śuṣṇa was smitten down; to Atithigva gavest Śambara for a prey.  E’en mighty Arbuda thou troddest under foot: thou from of old wast born to strike the Dasyus dead.

1.51.d: तवे विश्वा तविषी सध्र्यग घिता तव राधः सोमपीथाय हर्षते | तव वज्रश्चिकिते बाह्वोर्हितो वर्श्चा शत्रोरव विश्वानि वर्ष्ण्या ||
1.51.e: All power and might is closely gathered up in thee; thy bounteous spirit joys in drinking Soma juice.  Known is the thunderbolt that lies within thine arms: rend off therewith all manly prowess of our foe.

1.51.d: वि जानीह्यार्यान ये च दस्यवो बर्हिष्मते रन्धया शासदव्रतान | शाकी भव यजमानस्य चोदिता विश्वेत ता ते सधमादेषु चाकन ||
1.51.e: Discern thou well Āryas and Dasyus; punishing the lawless give them up to him whose grass is strewn.  Be thou the sacrificer's strong encourager all these thy deeds are my delight at festivals.

1.51.d: अनुव्रताय रन्धयन्नपव्रतानाभूभिरिन्द्रः शनथयन्ननाभुवः | वर्द्धस्य चिद वर्धतो दयामिनक्षत सतवानो वम्रो वि जघान सन्दिहः ||
1.51.e: Indra gives up the lawless to the pious man, destroying by the Strong Ones those who have no strength.  Vamra when glorified destroyed the gathered piles of the still waxing great one who would reach the heaven.

1.51.d: तक्षद यत त उशना सहसा सहो वि रोदसी मज्मना बाधते शवः | आ तवा वातस्य नर्मणो मनोयुज आ पूर्यमाणमवहन्नभि शरवः ||
1.51.e: The might which Uśanā hath formed for thee with might rends in its greatness and with strength both worlds apart.  O Hero-souled, the steeds of Vāta, yoked by thought, have carried thee to fame while thou art filled with power.

1.51.d: मन्दिष्ट यदुशने काव्ये सचानिन्द्रो वङकू वङकुतराधि तिष्ठति | उग्रो ययिं निरपः सरोतसास्र्जद वि शुष्णस्य दरंहिता ऐरयत पुरः ||
1.51.e: When Indra hath rejoiced with Kāvya Uśanā, he mounts his steeds who swerve wider and wider yet.  The Strong hath loosed his bolt with the swift rush of rain, and he hath rent in pieces Śuṣṇa's firm-built forts.

1.51.d: आ समा रथं वर्षपाणेषु तिष्ठसि शार्यातस्य परभ्र्तायेषु मन्दसे | इन्द्र यथा सुतसोमेषु चाकनो.अनर्वाणंश्लोकमा रोहसे दिवि ||
1.51.e: Thou mountest on thy car amid strong Soma draughts: Śāryāta brought thee those in which thou hast delight.  Indra, when thou art pleased with men whose Soma flows thou risest to unchallenged glory in the sky.

1.51.d: अददा अर्भां महते वचस्यवे कक्षीवते वर्चयामिन्द्र सुन्वते | मेनाभवो वर्षणश्वस्य सुक्रतो विश्वेत ता ते सवनेषु परवाच्या ||
1.51.e: To old Kakṣīvān, Soma-presser, skilled in song, O Indra, thou didst give the youthful Vṛcayā.  Thou, very wise, wast Menā, Vrsanśva's child: those deeds of thine must all be told at Soma feasts.

1.51.d: इन्द्रो अश्रायि सुध्यो निरेके पज्रेषु सतोमो दुर्यो न यूपः | अश्वयुर्गव्यू रथयुर्वसूयुरिन्द्र इद रायः कषयति परयन्ता ||
1.51.e: The good man's refuge in his need is Indra, firm as a doorpost, praised among the Pajras.  Indra alone is Lord of wealth, the Giver, lover of riches, chariots, kine, and horses.

1.51.d: इदं नमो वर्षभाय सवराजे सत्यशुष्माय तवसे.अवाचि | अस्मिन्निन्द्र वर्जने सर्ववीराः समत सूरिभिस्तव शर्मन सयाम ||
1.51.e: To him the Mighty One, the self-resplendent, verily strong and great, this praise is uttered.  May we and all the heroes, with the princes, be, in this fray, O Indra, in thy keeping.

1.52.d: तयं सु मेषं महया सवर्विदं शतं यस्य सुभ्वः साकमीरते | अत्यं न वाजं हवनस्यदं रथमेन्द्रं वव्र्त्यामवसे सुव्र्क्तिभिः ||
1.52.e: I GLORIFY that Ram who finds the light of heaven, whose hundred nobly-natured ones go forth with him.  With hymns may I turn hither Indra to mine aid,—the Car which like a strong steed hasteth to the call.

1.52.d: स पर्वतो न धरुणेष्वच्युतः सहस्रमूतिस्तविषीषु वाव्र्धे | इन्द्रो यद वर्त्रमवधीन नदीव्र्तमुब्जन्नर्णांसिजर्ह्र्षाणो अन्धसा ||
1.52.e: Like as a mountain on firm basis, unremoved, he, thousandfold protector, waxed in mighty strength,  When Indra, joying in the draughts of Soma juice, forced the clouds, slaying Vṛtra stayer of their flow.

1.52.d: स हि दवरो दवरिषु वव्र ऊधनि चन्द्रबुध्नो मदव्र्द्धो मनीषिभिः | इन्द्रं तमह्वे सवपस्यया धिया मंहिष्ठरातिं स हि पप्रिरन्धसः ||
1.52.e: For he stays e’en the stayers, spread o’er laden cloud, rooted in light, strengthened in rapture by the wise.  Indra with thought, with skilled activity, I call, most liberal giver, for he sates him with the juice.

1.52.d: आ यं पर्णन्ति दिवि सद्मबर्हिषः समुद्रं न सुभ्वः सवा अभिष्टयः | तं वर्त्रहत्ये अनु तस्थुरूतयः शुष्मािन्द्रमवाता अह्रुतप्सवः ||
1.52.e: Whom those that flow in heaven on sacred grass, his own assistants, nobly-natured, fill full like the sea,—  Beside that Indra when he smote down Vṛtra stood his helpers, straight in form, mighty, invincible.

1.52.d: अभि सवव्र्ष्टिं मदे अस्य युध्यतो रघ्वीरिव परवणे सस्रुरूतयः | इन्द्रो यद वज्री धर्षमाणो अन्धसा भिनद वलस्य परिधीन्रिव तरितः ||
1.52.e: To him, as in wild joy he fought with him who stayed the rain, his helpers sped like swift streams down a slope,  When Indra, thunder-armed, made bold by Soma draughts, as Tṛta cleaveth Vala's fences, cleft him through.

1.52.d: परीं घर्णा चरति तित्विषे शवो.अपो वर्त्वी रजसो बुध्नमाशयत | वर्त्रस्य यत परवणे दुर्ग्र्भिश्वनो निजघन्थ हन्वोरिन्द्र तन्यतुम ||
1.52.e: Splendour encompassed thee, forth shone thy warrior might: the rain-obstructer lay in mid-air's lowest deep,  What time, O Indra, thou didst cast thy thunder down upon the jaws of Vṛitra hard to be restrained.

1.52.d: हरदं न हि तवा नय्र्षन्त्यूर्मयो बरह्माणीन्द्र तव यानि वर्धना | तवष्टा चित ते युज्यं वाव्र्धे शवस्ततक्ष वज्रमभिभूत्योजसम ||
1.52.e: The hymns which magnify thee, Indra, reach to thee even as water-brooks flow down and fill the lake.  Tvaṣṭar gave yet more force to thine appropriate strength, and forged thy thunderbolt of overpowering might.

1.52.d: जघन्वानु हरिभिः सम्भ्र्तक्रतविन्द्र वर्त्रं मनुषे गातुयन्नपः | अयछथा बाह्वोर्वज्रमायसमधारयो दिव्या सूर्यं दर्शे ||
1.52.e: When, Indra, thou whose power is linked with thy Bay Steeds hadst smitten Vṛtra, causing floods to flow for man,  Thou heldst in thine arms the metal thunderbolt, and settest in the heaven the Sun for all to see.

1.52.d: बर्हत सवश्चन्द्रममवद यदुक्थ्यमक्र्ण्वत भियसा रोहणं दिवः | यन मानुषप्रधना इन्द्रमूतयः सवर्न्र्षाचो मरुतो.अमदन्ननु ||
1.52.e: In fear they raised the lofty self-resplendent hymn, praise giving and effectual, leading up to heaven,  When Indra's helpers fighting for the good of men, the Maruts, faithful to mankind, joyed in the light.

1.52.d: दयौश्चिदस्यामवानहेः सवनादयोयवीद भियसा वज्र इन्द्र ते | वर्त्रस्य यद बद्बधानस्य रोदसी मदे सुतस्य शवसाभिनच्छिरः ||
1.52.e: Then Heaven himself, the mighty, at that Dragon's roar reeled back in terror when, Indra, thy thunderbolt  In the wild joy of Soma had struck off with might the head of Vṛtra, tyrant of the earth and heaven.

1.52.d: यदिन नविन्द्र पर्थिवी दशभुजिरहानि विश्वा ततनन्तक्र्ष्टयः | अत्राह ते मघवन विश्रुतं सहो दयामनु शवसा बर्हणा भुवत ||
1.52.e: O Indra, were this earth extended forth tenfold, and men who dwell therein multiplied day by day,  Still here thy conquering might, Maghavan, would be famed: it hath waxed vast as heaven in majesty and power.

1.52.d: तवमस्य पारे रजसो वयोमनः सवभूत्योजा अवसे धर्षन्मनः | चक्र्षे भूमिं परतिमानमोजसो.अपः सवः परिभूरेष्या दिवम ||
1.52.e: Thou, bold of heart, in thine own native might, for help, upon the limit of this mid-air and of heaven,  Hast made the earth to be the pattern of thy strength: embracing flood and light thou reachest to the sky.

1.52.d: तवं भुवः परतिमानं पर्थिव्या रष्ववीरस्य बर्हतः पतिर्भूः | विश्वमाप्रा अन्तरिक्षं महित्वा सत्यमद्धा नकिरन्यस्त्वावान ||
1.52.e: Thou art the counterpart of earth, the Master of lofty heaven with all its mighty Heroes:  Thou hast filled all the region with thy greatness: yea, of a truth there is none other like thee.

1.52.d: न यस्य दयावाप्र्थिवी अनु वयचो न सिन्धवो रजसो अन्तमानशुः | नोत सवव्र्ष्टिं मदे अस्य युध्यत एको अन्यच्चक्र्षे विश्वमानुषक ||
1.52.e: Whose amplitude the heaven and earth have not attained, whose bounds the waters of mid-air have never reached,—  Not, when in joy he fights the stayer of the rain: thou, and none else, hast made all things in order due.

1.52.d: आर्चन्नत्र मरुतः सस्मिन्नाजौ विश्वे देवासो अमदन्ननुत्वा | वर्त्रस्य यद भर्ष्टिमता वधेन नि तवमिन्द्र परत्यानं जघन्थ ||
1.52.e: The Maruts sang thy praise in this encounter, and in thee all the Deities delighted,  What time thou, Indra, with thy spiky weapon, thy deadly bolt, smotest the face of Vṛtra.

1.53.d: नयू षु वाचं पर महे भरामहे गिर इन्द्राय सदने विवस्वतः | नू चिद धि रत्नं ससतामिवाविदन न दुष्टुतिर्द्रविणोदेषु शस्यते ||
1.53.e: WE will present fair praise unto the Mighty One, our hymns to Indra in Vivasvān's dwelling-place;  For he hath ne’er found wealth in those who seem to sleep: those who give wealth to men accept no paltry praise.

1.53.d: दुरो अश्वस्य दुर इन्द्र गोरसि दुरो यवस्य वसुन इनस पतिः | शिक्षानरः परदिवो अकामकर्शनः सखा सखिभ्यस्तमिदं गर्णीमसि ||
1.53.e: Giver of horses, Indra, giver, thou, of kine, giver of barley, thou art Lord and guard of wealth:  Man's helper from of old, not disappointing hope, Friend of our friends, to thee as such we sing this praise.

1.53.d: शचीव इन्द्र पुरुक्र्द दयुमत्तम तवेदिदमभितश्चेकिते वसु | अतः संग्र्भ्याभिभूत आ भर मा तवायतो जरितुः काममूनयीः ||
1.53.e: Indra, most splendid, powerful, rich in mighty deeds, this treasure spread around is known to be thine own.  Gather therefrom, O Conqueror, and bring to us: fail not the hope of him who loves and sings to thee.

1.53.d: एभिर्द्युभिः सुमना एभिरिन्दुभिर्निरुन्धानो अमतिं गोभिरश्विना | इन्द्रेण दस्युं दरयन्त इन्दुभिर्युतद्वेषसःसमिषा रभेमहि ||
1.53.e: Well pleased with these bright flames and with these Soma drops, take thou away our poverty with seeds and kine.  With Indra scattering the Dasyu through these drops, freed from their hate may we obtain abundant food.

1.53.d: समिन्द्र राया समिषा रभेमहि सं वाजेभिः पुरुश्चन्द्रैरभिद्युभिः | सं देव्या परमत्या वीरशुष्मया गोग्रयाश्वावत्या रभेमहि ||
1.53.e: Let us obtain, O Indra, plenteous wealth and food, with strength exceeding glorious, shining to the sky:  May we obtain the Goddess Providence, the strength of heroes, special source of cattle, rich in steeds.

1.53.d: ते तवा मदा अमदन तानि वर्ष्ण्या ते सोमासो वर्त्रहत्येषु सत्पते | यत कारवे दश वर्त्राण्यप्रति बर्हिष्मते नि सहस्राणि बर्हयः ||
1.53.e: These our libations strength-inspiring, Soma draughts, gladdened thee in the fight with Vṛtra, Hero Lord,  What time thou slewest for the singer with trimmed grass ten thousand Vṛtras, thou resistless in thy might.

1.53.d: युधा युधमुप घेदेषि धर्ष्णुया पुरा पुरं समिदं हंस्योजसा | नम्या यदिन्द्र सख्या परावति निबर्हयो नमुचिं नाम मायिनम ||
1.53.e: Thou goest on from fight to fight intrepidly, destroying castle after castle here with strength.  Thou, Indra, with thy friend who makes the foe bow down, slewest from far away the guileful Namuci.

1.53.d: तवं करञ्जमुत पर्णयं वधीस्तेजिष्ठयातिथिग्वस्यवर्तनी | तवं शता वङगर्दस्याभिनत पुरो.अनानुदः परिषूता रजिश्वना ||
1.53.e: Thou hast struck down in death Karañja, Parṇaya, in Atithigva's very glorious going forth.  Unyielding, when Ṛjiśvan compassed them with siege, thou hast destroyed the hundred forts of Vaṅgṛida.

1.53.d: तवमेताञ जनराज्ञो दविर्दशाबन्धुना सुश्रवसोपजग्मुषः | षष्टिं सहस्रा नवतिं नव शरुतो नि चक्रेण रथ्या दुष्पदाव्र्णक ||
1.53.e: With all-outstripping chariot-wheel, O Indra, thou far-famed, hast overthrown the twice ten Kings of men,  With sixty thousand nine-and-ninety followers, who came in arms to fight with friendless Suśravas.

1.53.d: तवमाविथ सुश्रवसं तवोतिभिस्तव तरामभिरिन्द्र तूर्वयाणम | तवमस्मै कुत्समतिथिग्वमायुं महे राज्ञे यूने अरन्धनायः ||
1.53.e: Thou hast protected Suśravas with succour, and Tūrvayāṇa with thine aid, O Indra.  Thou madest Kutsa, Atithigva, Āyu, subject unto this King, the young, the mighty.

1.53.d: य उद्र्चीन्द्र देवगोपाः सखायस्ते शिवतमा असाम | तवां सतोषाम तवया सुवीरा दराघीय आयुः परतरं दधानाः ||
1.53.e: May we protected by the Gods hereafter remain thy very prosperous friends, O Indra.  Thee we extol, enjoying through thy favour life long and joyful and with store of heroes.

1.54.d: मा नो अस्मिन मघवन पर्त्स्वंहसि नहि ते अन्तः शवसः परीणशे | अक्रन्दयो नद्यो रोरुवद वना कथा न कषोणीर्भियसा समारत ||
1.54.e: URGE us not, Maghavan, to this distressful fight, for none may comprehend the limit of thy strength.  Thou with fierce shout hast made the woods and rivers roar: did not men run in crowds together in their fear?

1.54.d: अर्चा शक्राय शाकिने शचीवते शर्ण्वन्तमिन्द्रं महयन्नभि षटुहि | यो धर्ष्णुना शवसा रोदसी उभे वर्षा वर्षत्वा वर्षभो नय्र्ञ्जते ||
1.54.e: Sing hymns of praise to Śakra, Lord of power and might; laud thou and magnify Indra who heareth thee,  Who with his daring might, a Bull exceeding strong in strength, maketh him master of the heaven and earth.

1.54.d: अर्चा दिवे बर्हते शूष्यं वचः सवक्षत्रं यस्य धर्षतो धर्षन मनः | बर्हच्छ्रवा असुरो बर्हणा कर्तः पुरो हरिभ्यां वर्षभो रथो हि षः ||
1.54.e: Sing forth to lofty Dyaus a strength-bestowing song, the Bold, whose resolute mind hath independent sway.  High glory hath the Asura, compact of strength, drawn on by two Bay Steeds: a Bull, a Car is he.

1.54.d: तवं दिवो बर्हतः सानु कोपयो.अव तमना धर्षता शम्बरं भिनत | यन मायिनो वरन्दिनो मन्दिना धर्षच्छितां गभस्तिमशनिं पर्तन्यसि ||
1.54.e: The ridges of the lofty heaven thou madest shake; thou, daring, of thyself smotest through Śambara,  When bold with gladdening juice, thou warredst with thy bolt, sharp and two-edged, against the banded sorcerers.

1.54.d: नि यद वर्णक्षि शवसनस्य मूर्धनि शुष्णस्य चिद वरन्दिनोरोरुवद वना | पराचीनेन मनसा बर्हणावता यदद्या चित कर्णवः कस्त्वा परि ||
1.54.e: When with a roar that fills the woods, thou forcest down on wind's head the stores which Śuṣṇa kept confined,  Who shall have power to stay thee firm and eager-souled from doing still this day what thou of old hast done?

1.54.d: तवमाविथ नर्यं तुर्वशं यदुं तवं तुर्वीतिं वय्यंशतक्रतो | तवं रथमेतशं कर्त्व्ये धने तवं पुरो नवतिं दम्भयो नव ||
1.54.e: Thou helpest Narya, Turvaśa, and Yadu, and Vayya's son Turvīti, Śatakratu!  Thou helpest horse and car in final battle thou breakest down the nine-and-ninety castles.

1.54.d: स घा राजा सत्पतिः शूशुवज्जनो रातहव्यः परति यः शासमिन्वति | उक्था वा यो अभिग्र्णाति राधसा दानुरस्मा उपरा पिन्वते दिवः ||
1.54.e: A hero-lord is he, King of a mighty folk, who offers free oblations and promotes the Law,  Who with a bounteous guerdon welcomes hymns of praise: for him flows down the abundant stream below the sky.

1.54.d: असमं कषत्रमसमा मनीषा पर सोमपा अपसा सन्तु नेमे | ये त इन्द्र ददुषो वर्धयन्ति महि कषत्रं सथविरं वर्ष्ण्यं च ||
1.54.e: His power is matchless, matchless is his wisdom; chief, through their work, be some who drink the Soma,  Those, Indra, who increase the lordly power, the firm heroic strength of thee the Giver.

1.54.d: तुभ्येदेते बहुला अद्रिदुग्धाश्चमूषदश्चमसा इन्द्रपानाः | वयश्नुहि तर्पया काममेषामथा मनो वसुदेयाय कर्ष्व ||
1.54.e: Therefore for thee are these abundant beakers Indra's drink, stone-pressed juices held in ladles.  Quaff them and satisfy therewith thy longing; then fix thy mind upon bestowing treasure.

1.54.d: अपामतिष्ठद धरुणह्वरं तमो.अन्तर्व्र्त्रस्य जठरेषुपर्वतः | अभीमिन्द्रो नद्यो वव्रिणा हिता विश्वा अनुष्ठाः परवणेषु जिघ्नते ||
1.54.e: There darkness stood, the vault that stayed the waters’ flow: in Vṛtra's hollow side the rain-cloud lay concealed.  But Indra smote the rivers which the obstructer stayed, flood following after flood, down steep declivities.

1.54.d: स शेव्र्धमधि धा दयुम्नमस्मे महि कषत्रं जनाषाळिन्द्र तव्यम | रक्षा च नो मघोनः पाहि सूरीन राये च नः सवपत्या इषे धाः ||
1.54.e: So give us, Indra, bliss-increasing glory give us great sway and strength that conquers people.  Preserve our wealthy patrons, save our princes; vouchsafe us wealth and food with noble offspring.

1.55.d: दिवश्चिदस्य वरिमा वि पप्रथ इन्द्रं न मह्ना पर्थिवीचन परति | भीमस्तुविष्माञ्चर्षणिभ्य आतपः शिशीते वज्रं तेजसे न वंसगः ||
1.55.e: THOUGH e’en this heaven's wide space and earth have spread them out, nor heaven nor earth may be in greatness Indra's match.  Awful and very mighty, causing woe to men, he whets his thunderbolt for sharpness, as a bull.

1.55.d: सो अर्णवो न नद्यः समुद्रियः परति गर्भ्णाति विश्रिता वरीमभिः | इन्द्रः सोमस्य पीतये वर्षायते सनात स युध्म ओजसा पनस्यते ||
1.55.e: Like as the watery ocean, so doth he receive the rivers spread on all sides in their ample width.  He bears him like a bull to drink of Soma juice, and will, as Warrior from of old, be praised for might.

1.55.d: तवं तमिन्द्र पर्वतं न भोजसे महो नर्म्णस्य धर्मणामिरज्यसि | पर वीर्येण देवताति चेकिते विश्वस्मा उग्रः कर्मणे पुरोहितः ||
1.55.e: Thou swayest, Indra, all kinds of great manly power, so as to bend, as’t were, even that famed mountain down.  Foremost among the Gods is he through hero might, set in the van, the Strong One, for each arduous deed.

1.55.d: स इद वने नमस्युभिर्वचस्यते चारु जनेषु परब्रुवाण इन्द्रियम | वर्षा छन्दुर्भवति हर्यतो वर्षा कषेमेण धेनाम्मघवा यदिन्वति ||
1.55.e: He only in the wood is praised by worshippers, when he shows forth to men his own fair Indra-power.  A friendly Bull is he, a Bull to be desired when Maghavan auspiciously sends forth his voice.

1.55.d: स इन महानि समिथानि मज्मना कर्णोति युध्म ओजसा जनेभ्यः | अधा चन शरद दधति तविषीमत इन्द्राय वज्रं निघनिघ्नते वधम ||
1.55.e: Yet verily the Warrior in his vigorous strength stirreth up with his might great battles for mankind;  And men have faith in Indra, the resplendent One, what time he hurleth down his bolt, his dart of death.

1.55.d: स हि शरवस्युः सदनानि कर्त्रिमा कष्मया वर्धान ओजसाविनाशयन | जयोतींषि कर्ण्वन्नव्र्काणि यज्यवे.अव सुक्रतुः सर्तवा अपः सर्जत ||
1.55.e: Though, fain for glory, and with strength increased on earth, he with great might destroys the dwellings made with art,  He makes the lights of heaven shine forth secure, he bids, exceeding wise, the floods flow for his worshipper.

1.55.d: दानाय मनः सोमपावन्नस्तु ते.अर्वाञ्चा हरी वन्दनश्रुदा कर्धि | यमिष्ठासः सारथयो य इन्द्र ते न तवा केताा दभ्नुवन्ति भूर्णयः ||
1.55.e: Drinker of Soma, let thy heart incline to give; bring thy Bays hitherward, O thou who hearest praise.  Those charioteers of thine, best skilled to draw the rein, the rapid sunbeams, Indra, lead thee not astray.

1.55.d: अप्रक्षितं वसु बिभर्षि हस्तयोरषाळ्हं सहस्तन्वि शरुतो दधे | आव्र्तासो.अवतासो न कर्त्र्भिस्तनूषु ते करतवैन्द्र भूरयः ||
1.55.e: Thou bearest in both hands treasure that never fails; the famed One in his body holds unvanquished might.  O Indra, in thy members many powers abide, like wells surrounded by the ministering priests.

1.56.d: एष पर पूर्वीरव तस्य चम्रिषो.अत्यो न योषामुदयंस्त भुर्वणिः | दक्षं महे पाययते हिरण्ययं रथमाव्र्त्या हरियोगं रभ्वसम ||
1.56.e: FOR this man's full libations held in ladles, he hath roused him, eager, as a horse to meet the mare.  He stays his golden car, yoked with Bay Horses, swift, and drinks the Soma juice which strengthens for great deeds.

1.56.d: तं गूर्तयो नेमन्निषः परीणसः समुद्रं न संचरणे सनिष्यवः | पतिं दक्षस्य विदथस्य नू सहो गिरिं न वेना अधि रोह तेजसा ||
1.56.e: To him the guidance-following songs of praise flow full, as those who seek gain go in company to the flood.  To him the Lord of power, the holy synod's might, as to a hill, with speed, ascend the loving ones.

1.56.d: स तुर्वणिर्महानरेणु पौंस्ये गिरेर्भ्र्ष्टिर्न भराजते तुजा शवः | येन शुष्णं मायिनमायसो मदे दुध्राभूषु रामयन नि दामनि ||
1.56.e: Victorious, great is he; in manly battle shines, unstained with dust, his might, as shines a mountain peak;  Wherewith the iron one, fierce e’en against the strong, in rapture, fettered wily Śushṇa fast in bonds.

1.56.d: देवी यदि तविषी तवाव्र्धोतय इन्द्रं सिषक्त्युषसं न सूर्यः | यो धर्ष्णुना शवसा बाधते तम इयर्ति रेणुं बर्हदर्हरिष्वणिः ||
1.56.e: When Strength the Goddess, made more strong for help by thee, waits upon Indra as the Sun attends the Dawn,  Then. he who with his might unflinching kills the gloom stirs up the dust aloft, with joy and triumphing.

1.56.d: वि यत तिरो धरुणमच्युतं रजो.अतिष्ठिपो दिव आतासुबर्हणा | सवर्मीळ्हे यन मद इन्द्र हर्ष्याहन वर्त्रं निरपामौब्जो अर्णवम ||
1.56.e: When thou with might, upon the framework of the heaven, didst fix, across, air's region firmly, unremoved,  In the light-winning war, Indra, in rapturous joy, thou smotest Vṛtra dead and broughtest floods of rain.

1.56.d: तवं दिवो धरुणं धिष ओजसा पर्थिव्या इन्द्र सदनेषु माहिनः | तवं सुतस्य मदे अरिणा अपो वि वर्त्रस्य समया पाष्यारुजः ||
1.56.e: Thou with thy might didst grasp, the holder-up of heaven, thou who art mighty also in the seats of earth.  Thou, gladdened by the juice, hast set the waters free, and broken Vṛtra's stony fences through and through.

1.57.d: पर मंहिष्ठाय बर्हते बर्हद्रये सत्यशुष्माय तवसे मतिं भरे | अपामिव परवणे यस्य दुर्धरं राधो विश्वायुशवसे अपाव्र्तम ||
1.57.e: To him most liberal, lofty Lord of lofty wealth, verily powerful and strong, I bring my hymn,—  Whose checkless bounty, as of waters down a slope, is spread abroad for all that live, to give them strength.

1.57.d: अध ते विश्वमनु हासदिष्टय आपो निम्नेव सवना हविष्मतः | यत पर्वते न समशीत हर्यत इन्द्रस्य वज्रः शनथिता हिरण्ययः ||
1.57.e: Now all this world, for worship, shall come after thee—the offerer's libations like floods to the depth,  When the well-loved one seems to rest upon the hill, the thunderbolt of Indra, shatterer wrought of gold.

1.57.d: अस्मै भीमाय नमसा समध्वर उषो न शुभ्र आ भरापनीयसे | यस्य धाम शरवसे नामेन्द्रियं जयोतिरकारिहरितो नायसे ||
1.57.e: To him the terrible, most meet for lofty praise, like bright Dawn, now bring gifts with reverence in this rite,  Whose being, for renown, yea, Indra-power and light, have been created, like bay steeds, to move with speed.

1.57.d: इमे त इन्द्र ते वयं पुरुष्टुत ये तवारभ्य चरामसि परभूवसो | नहि तवदन्यो गिर्वणो गिरः सघत कषोणीरिव परति नो हर्य तद वचः ||
1.57.e: Thine, Indra, praised by many, excellently rich! are we who trusting in thy help draw near to thee.  Lover of praise, none else but thou receives our laud: as earth loves all her creatures, love thou this our hymn.

1.57.d: भूरि त इन्द्र वीर्यं तव समस्यस्य सतोतुर्मघवन काममा पर्ण | अनु ते दयौर्ब्र्हती वीर्यं मम इयं च ते पर्थिवी नेम ओजसे ||
1.57.e: Great is thy power, O Indra, we are thine. Fulfil, O Maghavan, the wish of this thy worshipper.  After thee lofty heaven hath measured out its strength: to thee and to thy power this earth hath bowed itself.

1.57.d: तवं तमिन्द्र पर्वतं महामुरुं वज्रेण वज्रिन पर्वशश्चकर्तिथ | अवास्र्जो निव्र्ताः सर्तवा अपः सत्रा विश्वं दधिषे केवलं सहः ||
1.57.e: Thou, who hast thunder for thy weapon, with thy bolt hast shattered into pieces this broad massive cloud.  Thou hast sent down the obstructed floods that they may flow: thou hast, thine own for ever, all victorious might.

1.58.d: नू चित सहोजा अम्र्तो नि तुन्दते होता यद दूतो अभवद विवस्वतः | वि साधिष्ठेभिः पथिभी रजो मम आ देवताताहविषा विवासति ||
1.58.e: NE’ER waxeth faint the Immortal, Son of Strength, since he, the Herald, hath become Vivasvān's messenger.  On paths most excellent he measured out mid-air: he with oblation calls to service of the Gods.

1.58.d: आ सवमद्म युवमानो अजरस्त्र्ष्वविष्यन्नतसेषु तिष्ठति | अत्यो न पर्ष्ठं परुषितस्य रोचते दिवो न सानु सतनयन्नचिक्रदत ||
1.58.e: Never decaying, seizing his appropriate food, rapidly, eagerly through the dry wood he spreads.  His back, as he is sprinkled, glistens like a horse: loud hath he roared and shouted like the heights of heaven?

1.58.d: कराणा रुद्रेभिर्वसुभिः पुरोहितो होता निषत्तो रयिषाळमर्त्यः | रथो न विक्ष्व रञ्जसान आयुषु वयानुषग वार्या देव रण्वति ||
1.58.e: Set high in place o’er all that Vasus, Rudras do, immortal, Lord of riches, seated as High Priest;  Hastening like a car to men, to those who live, the God without delay gives boons to be desired.

1.58.d: वि वातजूतो अतसेषु तिष्ठते वर्था जुहूभिः सर्ण्या तुविष्वणिः | तर्षु यदग्ने वनिनो वर्षायसे कर्ष्णं त एम रुशदूर्मे अजर ||
1.58.e: Urged by the wind be spreads through dry wood as he lists, armed with his tongues for sickles, with a mighty roar.  Black is thy path, Agni, changeless, with glittering waves! when like a bull thou rushest eager to the trees.

1.58.d: तपुर्जम्भो वन आ वातचोदितो यूथे न साह्वानव वाति वंसगः | अभिव्रजन्नक्षितं पाजसा रजः सथातुश्चरथं भयते पतत्रिणः ||
1.58.e: With teeth of flame, wind-driven, through the wood he speeds, triumphant like a bull among the herd of cows,  With bright strength roaming to the everlasting air: things fixed, things moving quake before him as he flies.

1.58.d: दधुष टवा भर्गवो मानुषेष्वा रयिं न चारुं सुहवं जनेभ्यः | होतारमग्ने अतिथिं वरेण्यं मित्रं न शेवं दिव्याय जन्मने ||
1.58.e: The Bhṛgus established thee among mankind for men, like as a treasure, beauteous, easy to invoke;  Thee, Agni, as a herald and choice-worthy guest, as an auspicious Friend to the Celestial Race.

1.58.d: होतारं सप्त जुह्वो यजिष्ठं यं वाघतो वर्णते अध्वरेषु | अग्निं विश्वेषामरतिं वसूनां सपर्यामि परयसा यामि रत्नम ||
1.58.e: Agni, the seven tongues' deftest Sacrificer, him whom the priests elect at solemn worship,  The Herald, messenger of all the Vasus, I serve with dainty food, I ask for riches.

1.58.d: अछिद्रा सूनो सहसो नो अद्य सतोत्र्भ्यो मित्रमहः शर्म यछ | अग्ने गर्णन्तमंहस उरुष्योर्जो नपात पूर्भिरायसीभिः ||
1.58.e: Grant, Son of Strength, thou rich in friends, a refuge without a flaw this day to us thy praisers.  O Agni, Son of Strength, with forts of iron preserve thou from distress the man who lauds thee.

1.58.d: भवा वरूथं गर्णते विभावो भवा मघवन मघवद्भ्यःशर्म | उरुष्याग्ने अंहसो गर्णन्तं परातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात ||
1.58.e: Be thou a refuge, Bright One, to the singer, a shelter, Bounteous Lord, to those who worship.  Preserve the singer from distress, O Agni. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

1.59.d: वया इदग्ने अग्नयस्ते अन्ये तवे विश्वे अम्र्ता मादयन्ते | वैश्वानर नाभिरसि कषितीनां सथूणेव जनानुपमिद ययन्थ ||
1.59.e: THE other fires are, verily, thy branches; the Immortals all rejoice in thee, O Agni.  Centre art thou, Vaiśvānara, of the people, sustaining men like a deep-founded pillar.

1.59.d: मूर्धा दिवो नाभिरग्निः पर्थिव्या अथाभवदरती रोदस्योः | तं तवा देवासो.अजनयन्त देवं वैश्वानर जयोतिरिदार्याय ||
1.59.e: The forehead of the sky, earth's centre, Agni became the messenger of earth and heaven.  Vaiśvānara, the Deities produced thee, a God, to be a light unto the Ārya.

1.59.d: आ सूर्ये न रश्मयो धरुवासो वैश्वानरे दधिरे.अग्ना वसूनि | या पर्वतेष्वोषधीष्वप्सु या मानुषेष्वसि तस्य राजा ||
1.59.e: As in the Sun firm rays are set for ever, treasures are in Vaiśvānara, in Agni.  Of all the riches in the hills, the waters, the herbs, among mankind, thou art the Sovran.

1.59.d: बर्हती इव सूनवे रोदसी गिरो होता मनुष्यो न दक्षः | सवर्वते सत्यशुष्माय पूर्वीर्वैश्वानराय नर्तमाय यह्वीः ||
1.59.e: As the great World-halves, so are their Son's praises; skilled, as a man, to act, is he the Herald.  Vaiśvānara, celestial, truly mighty, most manly One, hath many a youthful consort.

1.59.d: दिवश्चित ते बर्हतो जातवेदो वैश्वानर पर रिरिचे महित्वम | राजा कर्ष्टीनामसि मानुषीणां युधा देवेभ्यो वरिवश्चकर्थ ||
1.59.e: Even the lofty heaven, O Jātavedas Vaiśvānara, hath not attained thy greatness.  Thou art the King of lands where men are settled, thou hast brought comfort to the Gods in battle.

1.59.d: पर नू महित्वं वर्षभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वर्त्रहणं सचन्ते | वैश्वानरो दस्युमग्निर्जघन्वानधूनोत काष्ठा अव शम्बरं भेत ||
1.59.e: Now will I tell the greatness of the Hero whom Pūru's sons follow as Vṛtra's slayer:  Agni Vaiśvānara struck down the Dasyu, cleave Śambara through and shattered down his fences.

1.59.d: वैश्वानरो महिम्ना विश्वक्र्ष्टिर्भरद्वाजेषु यजतो विभावा | शातवनेये शतिनीभिरग्निः पुरुणीथे जरते सून्र्तावान ||
1.59.e: Vaiśvānara, dwelling by his might with all men, far-shining, holy mid the Bharadvājas,  Is lauded, excellent, with hundred praises by Purūṇītha, son of Śatavani.

1.60.d: वह्निं यशसं विदथस्य केतुं सुप्राव्यं दूतं सद्योर्थम | दविजन्मानं रयिमिव परशस्तं रातिं भरद भर्गवेमातरिश्वा ||
1.60.e: As ’twere Some goodly treasure Mātariśvan brought, as a gift, the glorious Priest to Bhṛgu,  Banner of sacrifice, the good Protector, child of two births, the swiftly moving envoy.

1.60.d: अस्य शासुरुभयासः सचन्ते हविष्मन्त उशिजो ये च मर्ताः | दिवश्चित पूर्वो नयसादि होताप्र्छ्यो विश्पतिर्विक्षुवेधाः ||
1.60.e: Both Gods and men obey this Ruler's order, Gods who are worshipped, men who yearn and worship.  As Priest he takes his seat ere break of morning, House-Lord, adorable with men, Ordainer.

1.60.d: तं नव्यसी हर्द आ जायमानमस्मत सुकीर्तिर्मधुजिह्वमश्याः | यं रत्विजो वर्जने मानुषासः परयस्वन्त आयवो जीजनन्त ||
