1.60.e: May our fair praise, heart-born, most recent, reach him whose tongue, e’en at his birth, is sweet as honey;  Whom mortal priests, men, with their strong endeavour, supplied with dainty viands, have created.

1.60.d: उशिक पावको वसुर्मानुषेषु वरेण्यो होताधायि विक्षु | दमूना गर्हपतिर्दम आ अग्निर्भुवद रयिपती रयीणाम ||
1.60.e: Good to mankind, the yearning Purifier hath among men been placed as Priest choice-worthy.  May Agni be our Friend, Lord of the Household, protector of the riches in the dwelling.

1.60.d: तं तवा वयं पतिमग्ने रयीणां पर शंसामो मतिभिर्गोतमासः | आशुं न वाजम्भरं मर्जयन्तः परातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात ||
1.60.e: As such we Gotamas with hymns extol thee, O Agni, as the guardian Lord of riches,  Decking thee like a horse, the swift prizewinner. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

1.61.d: अस्मा इदु पर तवसे तुराय परयो न हर्मि सतोमं माहिनाय | रचीषमायाध्रिगव ओहमिन्द्राय बरह्माणि राततमा ||
1.61.e: EVEN to him, swift, strong and high. exalted, I bring my song of praise as dainty viands,  My thought to him resistless, praise-deserving, prayers offered most especially to Indra.

1.61.d: अस्मा इदु परय इव पर यंसि भराम्याङगूषं बाधे सुव्र्क्ति | इन्द्राय हर्दा मनसा मनीषा परत्नाय पत्ये धियोमर्जयन्त ||
1.61.e: Praise, like oblation, I present, and utter aloud my song, my fair hymn to the Victor.  For Indra, who is Lord of old, the singers have decked their lauds with heart and mind and spirit.

1.61.d: अस्मा इदु तयमुपमं सवर्षां भराम्याङगूषमास्येन | मंहिष्ठमछोक्तिभिर्मतीनां सुव्र्क्तिभिः सूरिं वाव्र्धध्यै ||
1.61.e: To him then with my lips mine adoration, winning heaven's light, most excellent, I offer,  To magnify with songs of invocation and with fair hymns the Lord, most bounteous Giver.

1.61.d: अस्मा इदु सतोमं सं हिनोमि रथं न तष्टेव तत्सिनाय | गिरश्च गिर्वाहसे सुव्र्क्तीन्द्राय विश्वमिन्वं मेधिराय ||
1.61.e: Even for him I frame a laud, as fashions the wright a chariot for the man who needs it,—  Praises to him who gladly hears our praises, a hymn well-formed, all-moving, to wise Indra.

1.61.d: अस्मा इदु सप्तिमिव शरवस्येन्द्रायार्कं जुह्वा समञ्जे | वीरं दानौकसं वन्दध्यै पुरां गूर्तश्रवसं दर्माणम ||
1.61.e: So with my tongue I deck, to please that Indra, my hymn, as ’twere a horse, through love of glory,  To reverence the Hero, bounteous Giver, famed far and wide, destroyer of the castles.

1.61.d: अस्मा इदु तवष्टा तक्षद वज्रं सवपस्तमं सवर्यं रणाय | वर्त्रस्य चिद विदद येन मर्म तुजन्नीशानस्तुजता कियेधाः ||
1.61.e: Even for him hath Tvaṣṭar forged the thunder, most deftly wrought, celestial, for the battle,  Wherewith he reached the vital parts of Vṛtra, striking-the vast, the mighty with the striker.

1.61.d: अस्येदु मातुः सवनेषु सद्यो महः पितुं पपिवाञ्चार्वन्ना | मुषायद विष्णुः पचतं सहीयान विध्यद वराहन्तिरो अद्रिमस्ता ||
1.61.e: As soon as, at libations of his mother, great Viṣṇu had drunk up the draught, he plundered.  The dainty cates, the cooked mess; but One stronger transfixed the wild boar, shooting through the mountain.

1.61.d: अस्मा इदु गनाश्चिद देवपत्नीरिन्द्रायार्कमहिहत्य ऊवुः | परि दयावाप्र्थिवी जभ्र उर्वी नास्य ते महिमानं परिष्टः ||
1.61.e: To him, to Indra, when he slew the Dragon, the Dames, too, Consorts of the Gods, wove praises.  The mighty heaven and earth hath he encompassed: thy greatness heaven and earth, combined, exceed not.

1.61.d: अस्येदेव पर रिरिचे महित्वं दिवस पर्थिव्याः पर्यन्तरिक्षात | सवराळ इन्द्रो दम आ विश्वगूर्तः सवरिरमत्रो ववक्षे रणाय ||
1.61.e: Yea, of a truth, his magnitude surpasseth the magnitude of earth, mid-air, and heaven.  Indra, approved by all men, self-resplendent, waxed in his home, loud-voiced and strong for battle.

1.61.d: अस्येदेव शवसा शुषन्तं वि वर्श्चद वज्रेण वर्त्रमिन्द्रः | गा न वराणा अवनीरमुञ्चदभि शरवो दावने सचेताः ||
1.61.e: Through his own strength Indra with bolt of thunder cut piece-meal Vṛtra, drier up of waters.  He let the floods go free, like cows imprisoned, for glory, with a heart inclined to bounty.

1.61.d: अस्येदु तवेषसा रन्त सिन्धवः परि यद वज्रेण सीमयछत | ईशानक्र्द दाशुषे दशस्यन तुर्वीतये गाधं तुर्वणिः कः ||
1.61.e: The rivers played, through his impetuous splendour, since with his bolt he compassed them on all sides.  Using his might and favouring him who worshipped, he made a ford, victorious, for Turvīti.

1.61.d: अस्मा इदु पर भरा तूतुजानो वर्त्राय वज्रमीशानः कियेधाः | गोर्न पर्व वि रदा तिरश्चेष्यन्नर्णांस्यपां चरध्यै ||
1.61.e: Vast, with thine ample power, with eager movement, against this Vṛtra cast thy bolt of thunder.  Rend thou his joints, as of an ox, dissevered, with bolt oblique, that floods of rain may follow.

1.61.d: अस्येदु पर बरूहि पूर्व्याणि तुरस्य कर्माणि नव्य उक्थैः | युधे यदिष्णान आयुधान्य रघायमाणो निरिणाति शत्रून ||
1.61.e: Sing with new lauds his exploits wrought aforetime, the deeds of him, yea, him who moveth swiftly,  When, hurling forth his weapons in the battle, he with impetuous wrath lays low the foemen.

1.61.d: अस्येदु भिया गिरयश्च दर्ळ्हा दयावा च भूमा जनुषस्तुजेते | उपो वेनस्य जोगुवान ओणिं सद्यो भुवद वीर्याय नोधाः ||
1.61.e: When he, yea, he, comes forth the firm. Set mountains and the whole heaven and earth, tremble for terror.  May Nodhas, ever praising the protection of that dear Friend, gain quickly strength heroic.

1.61.d: अस्मा इदु तयदनु दाय्येषामेको यद वव्ने भूरेरीशानः | परैतशं सूर्ये पस्प्र्धानं सौवश्व्ये सुष्विमावदिन्द्रः ||
1.61.e: Now unto him of these things hath been given what he who rules alone o’er much, electeth.  Indra hath helped Etaśa, Soma-presser, contending in the race of steeds with Sūrya.

1.61.d: एवा ते हारियोजना सुव्र्क्तीन्द्र बरह्माणि गोतमासो अक्रन | ऐषु विश्वपेशसं धियं धाः परातर मक्षू धियावसुर जगम्यात||
1.61.e: Thus to thee, Indra, yoker of Bay Coursers, the Gotamas have brought their prayers to please thee.  Bestow upon them thought, decked with all beauty. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

1.62.d: पर मन्महे शवसानाय शूषमाङगूषं गिर्वणसे अङगिरस्वत | सुव्र्क्तिभिः सतुवत रग्मियायार्चामार्कं नरे विश्रुताय ||
1.62.e: LIKE Aṅgiras a gladdening laud we ponder to him who loveth song, exceeding mighty.  Let us sing glory to the far-famed Hero who must be praised with fair hymns by the singer.

1.62.d: पर वो महे महि नमो भरध्वमाङगूष्यं शवसानाय साम | येना नः पूर्वे पितरः पदज्ञा अर्चन्तो अङगिरसो गा अविन्दन ||
1.62.e: Unto the great bring ye great adoration, a chant with praise to him exceeding mighty,  Through whom our sires, Aṅgirases, singing praises and knowing well the places, found the cattle.

1.62.d: इन्द्रस्याङगिरसां चेष्टौ विदत सरमा तनयाय धासिम | बर्हस्पतिर्भिनदद्रिं विदद गाः समुस्रियाभिर्वावशन्त नरः ||
1.62.e: When Indra and the Aṅgirases desired it, Saramā found provision for her offspring.  Bṛhaspati cleft the mountain, found the cattle: the heroes shouted with the kine in triumph.

1.62.d: स सुष्टुभा स सतुभा सप्त विप्रैः सवरेणाद्रिं सवर्यो नवग्वैः | सरण्युभिः फलिगमिन्द्र शक्र वलं रवेणदरयो दशग्वैः ||
1.62.e: Mid shout, loud shout, and roar, with the Navagvas, seven singers, hast thou, heavenly, rent the mountain;  Thou hast, with speeders, with Daśagvas, Indra, Śakra, with thunder rent obstructive Vala.

1.62.d: गर्णानो अङगिरोभिर्दस्म वि वरुषसा सूर्येण गोभिरन्धः | वि भूम्या अप्रथय इन्द्र सानु दिवो रज उपरमस्तभायः ||
1.62.e: Praised by Aṅgirases, thou, foe-destroyer, hast, with the Dawn, Sun, rays, dispelled the darkness.  Thou Indra, hast spread out the earth's high ridges, and firmly fixed the region under heaven.

1.62.d: तदु परयक्षतममस्य कर्म दस्मस्य चारुतममस्ति दंसः | उपह्वरे यदुपरा अपिन्वन मध्वर्णसो नद्यश्चतस्रः ||
1.62.e: This is the deed most worthy of all honour, the fairest marvel of the Wonder-Worker,  That, nigh where heaven bends down, he made four rivers flow full with waves that carry down sweet water.

1.62.d: दविता वि वव्रे सनजा सनीळे अयास्य सतवमानेभिरर्कैः | भगो न मेने परमे वयोमन्नधारयद रोदसी सुदंसाः ||
1.62.e: Unwearied, won with lauding hymns, he parted of old the ancient Pair, united ever.  In highest sky like Bhaga, he the doer of marvels set both Dames and earth and heaven.

1.62.d: सनाद दिवं परि भूमा विरूपे पुनर्भुवा युवती सवेभिरेवैः | कर्ष्णेभिरक्तोषा रुशद्भिर्वपुर्भिरा चरतो अन्यान्या ||
1.62.e: Still born afresh, young Dames, each in her manner, unlike in hue, the Pair in alternation  Round heaven and earth from ancient time have travelled, Night with her dark limbs, Dawn with limbs of splendour.

1.62.d: सनेमि सख्यं सवपस्यमानः सूनुर्दाधार शवसा सुदंसाः | आमासु चिद दधिषे पक्वमन्तः पयः कर्ष्णासु रुशद रोहिणीषु ||
1.62.e: Rich in good actions, skilled in operation, the Son with might maintains his perfect friendship.  Thou in the raw cows, black of hue or ruddy, storest the ripe milk glossy white in colour.

1.62.d: सनात सनीला अवनीरवाता वरता रक्षन्ते अम्र्ताः सहोभिः | पुरू सहस्रा जनयो न पत्नीर्दुवस्यन्ति सवसारो अह्रयाणम ||
1.62.e: Their paths, of old connected, rest uninjured; they with great might preserve the immortal statutes.  For many thousand holy works the Sisters wait on the haughty Lord like wives and matrons.

1.62.d: सनायुवो नमसा नव्यो अर्कैर्वसूयवो मतयो दस्म दद्रुः | पतिं न पत्नीरुशतीरुशन्तं सप्र्शन्ति तवा शवसावन्मनीषाः ||
1.62.e: Thoughts ancient, seeking wealth, with adoration, with newest lauds have sped to thee, O Mighty.  As yearning wives cleave to their yearning husband, so cleave our hymns to thee, O Lord most potent.

1.62.d: सनादेव तव रायो गभस्तौ न कषीयन्ते नोप दस्यन्ति दस्म | दयुमानसि करतुमानिन्द्र धीरः शिक्षा शचीवस्तव नः शचीभिः ||
1.62.e: Strong God, the riches which thy hands have holden from days of old have perished not nor wasted.  Splendid art thou, O Indra, wise, unbending: strengthen us with might, O Lord of Power.

1.62.d: सनायते गोतम इन्द्र नव्यमतक्षद बरह्म हरियोजनाय | सुनीथाय नः शवसान नोधाः परातर मक्षू धियावसुर जगम्यात||
1.62.e: O mighty Indra, Gotama's son Nodhas hath fashioned this new prayer to thee Eternal,  Sure leader, yoker of the Tawny Coursers. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

1.63.d: तवं महानिन्द्र यो ह शुष्मैर्द्यावा जज्ञानः पर्थिवीमे धाः | यद ध ते विश्वा गिरयश्चिदभ्वा भिया दर्ळ्हासः किरणा नैजन ||
1.63.e: THOU art the Mighty One; when born, O Indra, with power thou terrifiedst earth and heaven;  When, in their fear of thee, all firm-set mountains and monstrous creatures shook like dust before thee.

1.63.d: आ यद धरी इन्द्र विव्रता वेरा ते वज्रं जरिता बाह्वोर्धात | येनाविहर्यतक्रतो अमित्रान पुर इष्णासि पुरुहूत पूर्वीः ||
1.63.e: When thy two wandering Bays thou drawest hither, thy praiser laid within thine arms the thunder,  Wherewith, O Much-invoked, in will resistless, thou smitest foemen down and many a castle.

1.63.d: तवं सत्य इन्द्र धर्ष्णुरेतान तवं रभुक्षा नर्यस्त्वंषाट | तवं शुष्णं वर्जने पर्क्ष आणौ यूने कुत्सायद्युमते सचाहन ||
1.63.e: Faithful art thou, these thou defiest, Indra; thou art the Ṛbhus' Lord, heroic, victor.  Thou, by his side, for young and glorious Kutsa, with steed and car in battle slewest Śuṣṇa,

1.63.d: तवं ह तयदिन्द्र चोदीः सखा वर्त्रं यद वज्रिन वर्षकर्मन्नुभ्नाः | यद ध शूर वर्षमणः पराचैर्वि दस्यून्र्योनावक्र्तो वर्थाषाट ||
1.63.e: That, as a friend, thou furtheredst, O Indra, when, Thunderer, strong in act, thou crushedst Vṛtra;  When, Hero, thou, great-souled, with easy conquest didst rend the Dasyus in their  distant dwelling.

1.63.d: तवं ह तयदिन्द्रारिषण्यन दर्ळ्हस्य चिन मर्तानामजुष्टौ | वयस्मदा काष्ठा अर्वते वर्घनेव वज्रिञ्छ्नथिह्यमित्रान ||
1.63.e: This doest thou, and art not harmed, O Indra, e’en in the anger of the strongest mortal.  Lay thou the race-course open for our horses: as with a club, slay, Thunder-armed! our foemen.

1.63.d: तवां ह तयदिन्द्रार्णसातौ सवर्मीळ्हे नर आजा हवन्ते | तव सवधाव इयमा समर्य ऊतिर्वाजेष्वतसाय्या भूत ||
1.63.e: Hence men invoke thee, Indra, in the tumult of battle, in the light-bestowing conflict.  This aid of thine, O Godlike One, was ever to be implored in deeds of might in combat.

1.63.d: तवं ह तयदिन्द्र सप्त युध्यन पुरो वज्रिन पुरुकुत्साय दर्दः | बर्हिर्न यत सुदासे वर्था वर्गंहो राजन वरिवः पूरवे कः ||
1.63.e: Warring for Purukutsa thou, O Indra, Thunder-armed! breakest down the seven castles;  Easily, for Sudās, like grass didst rend them, and out of need, King, broughtest gain to Pūru.

1.63.d: तवं तयां न इन्द्र देव चित्रामिषमापो न पीपयः परिज्मन | यया शूर परत्यस्मभ्यं यंसि तमनमूर्जं न विश्वध कषरध्यै ||
1.63.e: O Indra, God who movest round about us, feed us with varied food plenteous as water—  Food wherewithal, O Hero, thou bestowest vigour itself to flow to us for ever.

1.63.d: अकारि त इन्द्र गोतमेभिर्ब्रह्माण्योक्ता नमसा हरिभ्याम | सुपेशसं वाजमा भरा नः परातर मक्षू धियावसुर जगम्यात ||
1.63.e: Prayers have been made by Gotamas, O Indra, addressed to thee, with laud for thy Bay Horses.  Bring us in noble shape abundant riches. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

1.64.d: वर्ष्णे शर्धाय सुमखाय वेधसे नोधः सुव्र्क्तिं पर भरा मरुद्भ्यः | अपो न धीरो मनसा सुहस्त्यो गिरः समञ्जे विदथेष्वाभुवः ||
1.64.e: BRING for the manly host, wise and majestical, O Nodhas, for the Maruts bring thou a pure gift.  I deck my songs as one deft-handed, wise in mind prepares the water that hath power in solemn rites.

1.64.d: ते जज्ञिरे दिव रष्वास उक्षणो रुद्रस्य मर्या असुरा अरेपसः | पावकासः शुचयः सूर्या इव सत्वानो न दरप्सिनोघोरवर्पसः ||
1.64.e: They spring to birth, the lofty Ones, the Bulls of Heaven, divine, the youths of Rudra, free from spot and stain;  The purifiers, shining brightly even as suns, awful of form like giants, scattering rain-drops down.

1.64.d: युवानो रुद्रा अजरा अभोग्घनो ववक्षुरध्रिगावः पर्वता इव | दर्ळ्हा चिद विश्वा भुवनानि पार्थिवा पर चयावयन्तिदिव्यानि मज्मना ||
1.64.e: Young Rudras, demon-slayers, never growing old, they have waxed, even as mountains, irresistible.  They make all beings tremble with their mighty strength, even the very strongest, both of earth and heaven.

1.64.d: चित्रैरञ्जिभिर्वपुषे वयञ्जते वक्षस्सु रुक्मानधि येतिरे शुभे | अंसेष्वेषां नि मिम्र्क्षुर रष्टयः साकं जज्ञिरे सवधया दिवो नरः ||
1.64.e: With glittering ornaments they deck them forth for show; for beauty on their breasts they bind their chains of gold.  The lances on their shoulders pound to pieces; they were born together, of themselves, the Men of Heaven.

1.64.d: ईशानक्र्तो धुनयो रिशादसो वातान विद्युतस्तविषीभिरक्रत | दुहन्त्यूधर्दिव्यानि धूतयो भूमिं पिन्वन्ति पयसापरिज्रयः ||
1.64.e: Loud roarers, giving strength, devourers of the foe, they make the winds, they make the lightnings with their powers.  The restless shakers drain the udders of the sky, and ever wandering round fill the earth full with milk.

1.64.d: पिन्वन्त्यपो मरुतः सुदानवः पयो घर्तवद विदथेष्वाभुवः | अत्यं न मिहे वि नयन्ति वाजिनमुत्सं दुहन्ति सतनयन्तमक्षितम ||
1.64.e: The bounteous Maruts with the fatness dropping milk fill full the waters which avail in solemn rites.  They lead, as ’twere, the Strong Horse forth, that it may rain: they milk the thundering, the never-failing spring.

1.64.d: महिषासो मायिनश्चित्रभानवो गिरयो न सवतवसो रघुष्यदः | मर्गा इव हस्तिनः खादथा वना यदारुणीषु तविषीरयुग्ध्वम ||
1.64.e: Mighty, with wondrous power and marvellously bright, selfstrong like mountains, ye glide swiftly on your way.  Like the wild elephants ye eat the forests up when ye assume your strength among the bright red flames.

1.64.d: सिंहा इव नानदति परचेतसः पिशा इव सुपिशो विश्ववेदसः | कषपो जिन्वन्तः पर्षतीभिर रष्टिभिः समित सबाधः शवसाहिमन्यवः ||
1.64.e: Exceeding wise they roar like lions mightily, they, all-possessing, are beauteous as antelopes;  Stirring the darkness with lances and spotted deer, combined as priests, with serpents' fury through their might.

1.64.d: रोदसी आ वदता गणश्रियो नर्षाचः शूराः शवसाहिमन्यवः | आ वन्धुरेष्वमतिर्न दर्शता विद्युन न तस्थौ मरुतो रथेषु वः ||
1.64.e: Heroes who march in companies, befriending man, with serpents' ire through strength, ye greet the earth and heaven.  Upon the seats, O Maruts, of your chariots, upon the cars stands lightning visible as light.

1.64.d: विश्ववेदसो रयिभिः समोकसः सम्मिश्लासस्तविषीभिर्विरप्शिनः | अस्तार इषुं दधिरे गभस्त्योरनन्तशुष्मा वर्षखादयो नरः ||
1.64.e: Lords of all riches, dwelling in the home of wealth, endowed with mighty vigour, singers loud of voice,  Heroes, of powers infinite, armed with strong men's rings, the archers, they have laid the arrow on their arms.

1.64.d: हिरण्ययेभिः पविभिः पयोव्र्ध उज्जिघ्नन्त आपथ्यो न पर्वतान | मखा अयासः सवस्र्तो धरुवच्युतो दुध्रक्र्तो मरुतो भराजद्र्ष्टयः ||
1.64.e: They who with golden fellies make the rain increase drive forward the big clouds like wanderers on the way.  Self-moving, brisk, unwearied, they o’erthrow the firm; the Maruts with bright lances make all things to reel.

1.64.d: घर्षुं पावकं वनिनं विचर्षणिं रुद्रस्य सूनुं हवसा गर्णीमसि | रजस्तुरं तवसं मारुतं गणं रजीषिणंव्र्षणं सश्चत शरिये ||
1.64.e: The progeny of Rudra we invoke with prayer, the brisk, the bright, the worshipful, the active Ones  To the strong band of Maruts cleave for happiness, the chasers of the sky, impetuous, vigorous.

1.64.d: पर नू स मर्तः शवसा जनानति तस्थौ व ऊती मरुतो यमावत | अर्वद्भिर्वजं भरते धना नर्भिराप्र्छ्यंक्रतुमा कषेति पुष्यति ||
1.64.e: Maruts, the man whom ye have guarded with your help, he verily in strength surpasseth all mankind.  Spoil with his steeds he gaineth, treasure with his men; he winneth honourable strength and prospereth.

1.64.d: चर्क्र्त्यं मरुतः पर्त्सु दुष्टरं दयुमन्तं शुष्मं मघवत्सु धत्तन | धनस्प्र्तमुक्थ्यं विश्वचर्षणिं तोकं पुष्येम तनयं शतं हिमः ||
1.64.e: O Maruts, to the worshippers give glorious strength invincible in battle, brilliant, bringing wealth,  Praiseworthy, known to all men. May we foster well, during a hundred winters, son and progeny.

1.64.d: नू षठिरं मरुतो वीरवन्तं रतीषाहं रयिमस्मासु धत्त | सहस्रिणं शतिनं शूशुवांसं परातर मक्षू धियावसुर जगम्यात ||
1.64.e: Will ye then, O ye Maruts, grant us riches, durable, rich in men, defying onslaught.  A hundred, thousandfold, ever increasing? May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

1.65.d: पश्वा न तायुं गुहा चतन्तं नमो युजानं नमो वहन्तम | सजोषा धीराः पदैरनु गमन्नुप तवा सीदन विश्वेयजत्राः ||
1.65.e: ONE-MINDED, wise, they tracked thee like a thief lurking in dark cave with a stolen cow:  Thee claiming worship, bearing it to Gods: there nigh to thee sate all the Holy Ones.

1.65.d: रतस्य देवा अनु वरता गुर्भुवत परिष्टिर्द्यौर्न भूम | वर्धन्तीमापः पन्वा सुशिश्विं रतस्य योना गर्भे सुजातम ||
1.65.e: The Gods approached the ways of holy Law; there was a gathering vast as heaven itself.  The waters feed with praise the growing Babe, born nobly in the womb, the seat of Law.

1.65.d: पुष्टिर्न रण्वा कषितिर्न पर्थिवी गिरिर्न भुज्म कषोदो न शम्भु | अत्यो नाज्मन सर्गप्रतक्तः सिन्धुर्न कषोदः क ईं वराते ||
1.65.e: Like grateful food, like some wide dwelling place, like a fruit-bearing hill, a wholesome stream.  Like a steed urged to run in swift career, rushing like Sindhu, who may check his course?

1.65.d: जामिः सिन्धूनां भरातेव सवस्रामिभ्यान न राजा वनान्यत्ति | यद वातजूतो वना वयस्थादग्निर्ह दाति रोमा पर्थिव्याः ||
1.65.e: Kin as a brother to his sister floods, he eats the woods as a King eats the rich.  When through the forest, urged by wind, he spreads, verily Agni shears the hair of earth.

1.65.d: शवसित्यप्सु हंसो न सीदन करत्वा चेतिष्ठो विशामुषर्भुत | सोमो न वेधा रतप्रजातः पशुर्न शिश्वा विभुर्दूरेभाः ||
1.65.e: Like a swan sitting in the floods he pants wisest in mind mid men he wakes at morn.  A Sage like Soma, sprung from Law, he grew like some young creature, mighty, shining far.

1.66.d: रयिर्न चित्रा सूरो न सन्द्र्गायुर्न पराणो नित्यो नसूनुः | तक्वा न भूर्णिर्वना सिषक्ति पयो न धेनुः शुचिर्विभावा ||
1.66.e: LIKE the Sun's glance, like wealth of varied sort, like breath which is the life, like one's own son,  Like a swift bird, a cow who yields her milk, pure and refulgent to the wood he speeds.

1.66.d: दाधार कषेममोको न रण्वो यवो न पक्वो जेता जनानाम | रषिर्न सतुभ्वा विक्षु परशस्तो वाजी न परीतो वयोदधति ||
1.66.e: He offers safety like a pleasant home, like ripened corn, the Conqueror of men.  Like a Seer lauding, famed among the folk; like a steed friendly he vouchsafes us power.

1.66.d: दुरोकशोचिः करतुर्न नित्यो जायेव योनावरं विश्वस्मै | चित्रो यदभ्राट छवेतो न विक्षु रथो न रुक्मी तवेषः समत्सु ||
1.66.e: With flame insatiate, like eternal might; caring for each one like a dame at home;  Bright when he shines forth, whitish mid the folk, like a car, gold-decked, thundering to the fight.

1.66.d: सेनेव सर्ष्टामं दधात्यस्तुर्न दिद्युत तवेषप्रतीका | यमो ह जातो यमो जनित्वं जारः कनीनां पतिर्जनीनाम ||
1.66.e: He strikes with terror like a dart shot forth, e’en like an archer's arrow tipped with flame;  Master of present and of future life, the maidens’ lover and the matrons’ Lord.

1.66.d: तं वश्चराथा वयं वसत्यास्तं न गावो नक्षन्त इद्धम | सिन्धुर्न कषोदः पर नीचीरैनोन नवन्त गावः सवर्द्र्शीके ||
1.66.e: To him lead all your ways: may we attain the kindled God as cows their home at eve.  He drives the flames below as floods their swell: the rays rise up to the fair place of heaven.

1.67.d: वनेषु जायुर्मर्तेषु मित्रो वर्णीते शरुष्टिं राजेवाजुर्यम | कषेमो न साधुः करतुर्न भद्रो भुवत सवाधिर्होता हव्यवाट ||
1.67.e: VICTORIOUS in the wood, Friend among men, ever he claims obedience as a King.  Gracious like peace, blessing like mental power, Priest was he, offering-bearer, full of thought.

1.67.d: हस्ते दधानो नर्म्णा विश्वान्यमे देवान धाद गुहा निषीदन | विदन्तीमत्र नरो धियन्धा हर्दा यत तष्टान मन्त्रानशंसन ||
1.67.e: He, bearing in his hand all manly might, crouched in the cavern, struck the Gods with fear.  Men filled with understanding find him there, when they have sting prayers formed within their heart.

1.67.d: अजो न कषां दाधार पर्थिवीं तस्तम्भ दयां मन्त्रेभिः सत्यैः | परिया पदानि पश्वो नि पाहि विश्वायुरग्ने गुहा गुहं गाः ||
1.67.e: He, like the Unborn, holds the broad earth up; and with effective utterance fixed the sky.  O Agni, guard the spots which cattle love: thou, life of all, hast gone from lair to lair.

1.67.d: य ईं चिकेत गुहा भवन्तमा यः ससाद धारां रतस्य | वि ये चर्तन्त्य रता सपन्त आदिद वसूनि पर ववाचास्मै ||
1.67.e: Whoso hath known him dwelling in his lair, and hath approached the stream of holy Law,—  They who release him, paying sacred rites,—truly to such doth he announce great wealth.

1.67.d: वि यो वीरुत्सु रोधन महित्वोत परजा उत परसूष्वन्तः | चित्तिरपां दमे विश्वायुः सद्मेव धीराः सम्माय चक्रुः ||
1.67.e: He who grows mightily in herbs, within each fruitful mother and each babe she bears,  Wise, life of all men, in the waters’ home,—for him have sages built as ’twere a seat.

1.68.d: शरीणन्नुप सथाद दिवं भुरण्यु सथातुश्चरथमक्तून्व्यूर्णोत | परि यदेषामेको विश्वेषां भुवद देवो देवानां महित्वा ||
1.68.e: COMMINGLING, restless, he ascends the sky, unveiling nights and all that stands or moves,  As he the sole God is preeminent in greatness among all these other Gods.

1.68.d: आदित ते विश्वे करतुं जुषन्त शुष्काद यद देव जीवो जनिष्ठाः | भजन्त विश्वे देवत्वं नाम रतं सपन्तो अम्र्तमेवैः ||
1.68.e: All men are joyful in thy power, O God, that living from the dry wood thou art born.  All truly share thy Godhead while they keep, in their accustomed ways, eternal Law.

1.68.d: रतस्य परेषा रतस्य धीतिर्विश्वायुर्विश्वे अपांसि चक्रुः | यस्तुभ्यं दाशाद यो वा ते शिक्षात तस्मै चिकित्वान्रयिं दयस्व ||
1.68.e: Strong is the thought of Law, the Law's behest; all works have they performed; he quickens all.  Whoso will bring oblation, gifts to thee, to him, bethinking thee, vouchsafe thou wealth.

1.68.d: होता निषत्तो मनोरपत्ये स चिन नवासां पती रयीणाम | इछन्त रेतो मिथस्तनूषु सं जानत सवैर्दक्षैरमूराः ||
1.68.e: Seated as Priest with Manu's progeny, of all these treasures he alone is Lord.  Men yearn for children to prolong their line, and are not disappointed in their hope.

1.68.d: पितुर्न पुत्राः करतुं जुषन्त शरोषन ये अस्य शासं तुरासः | वि राय और्णोद दुरः पुरुक्षुः पिपेश नाकं सत्र्भिर्दमूनाः ||
1.68.e: Eagerly they who hear his word fulfil his wish as sons obey their sire's behest.  He, rich in food, unbars his wealth like doors: he, the House-Friend, hath decked heaven's vault with stars.

1.69.d: शुक्रः शुशुक्वानुषो न जारः पप्रा समीची दिवो नज्योतिः | परि परजातः करत्वा बभूथ भुवो देवानां पिता पुत्रः सन ||
1.69.e: BRIGHT, splendid, like Dawn's lover, he hath filled the two joined worlds as with the light of heaven.  When born, with might thou hast encompassed them: Father of Gods, and yet their Son wast thou.

1.69.d: वेधा अद्र्प्तो अग्निर्विजानन्नूधर्न गोनां सवाद्मा पितूनाम | जने न शेव आहूर्यः सन मध्ये निषत्तो रण्वो दुरोणे ||
1.69.e: Agni, the Sage, the humble, who discerns like the cow's udder, the sweet taste of food,  Like a bliss-giver to be drawn to men, sits gracious in the middle of the house.

1.69.d: पुत्रो न जातो रण्वो दुरोणे वाजी न परीतो विशो वि तारीत | विशो यदह्वे नर्भिः सनीळा अग्निर्देवत्वा विश्वान्यश्याः ||
1.69.e: Born in the dwelling like a lovely son, pleased, like a strong steed, he bears on the folk.  What time the men and I, with heroes, call, may Agni then gain all through Godlike power.

1.69.d: नकिष ट एता वरता मिनन्ति नर्भ्यो यदेभ्यः शरुष्टिं चकर्थ | तत तु ते दंसो यदहन समानैर्न्र्भिर्यद युक्तो विवे रपांसि ||
1.69.e: None breaks these holy laws of thine when thou hast granted audience to these chieftains here.  This is thy boast, thou smotest with thy peers, and joined with heroes dravest off disgrace.

1.69.d: उषो न जारो विभावोस्रः संज्ञातरूपश्चिकेतदस्मै | तमना वहन्तो दुरो वय रण्वन नवन्त विश्वे सवर्द्र्शीके ||
1.69.e: Like the Dawn's lover, spreading light, well-known as hued like morn, may he remember me.  They, bearing of themselves, unbar the doors: they all ascend to the fair place of heaven.

1.70.d: वनेम पूर्वीरर्यो मनीषा अग्निः सुशोको विश्वान्यश्याः | आ दैव्यानि वरता चिकित्वाना मानुषस्य जनस्य जन्म ||
1.70.e: MAY we, the pious, win much food by prayer, may Agni with fair light pervade each act,—  He the observer of the heavenly laws of Gods, and of the race of mortal man.

1.70.d: गर्भो यो अपां गर्भो वनानां गर्भश्च सथातां गर्भश्चरथाम | अद्रौ चिदस्मा अन्तर्दुरोणे विशां न विश्वो अम्र्तः सवाधीः ||
1.70.e: He who is germ of waters, germ of woods, germ of all things that move not and that move,—  To him even in the rock and in the house: Immortal One, he cares for all mankind.

1.70.d: स हि कषपावानग्नी रयीणां दाशद यो अस्मा अरं सूक्तैः | एता चिकित्वो भूमा नि पाहि देवानां जन्म मर्तांश्च विद्वान ||
1.70.e: Agni is Lord of riches for the man who serves him readily with sacred songs.  Protect these beings thou with careful thought, knowing the races both of Gods and men.

1.70.d: वर्धान यं पूर्वीः कषपो विरूपा सथातुश्च रथं रतप्रवीतम | अराधि होता सवर्निषत्तः कर्ण्वन विश्वान्यपांसि सत्या ||
1.70.e: Whom many dawns and nights, unlike, make strong, whom, born in Law, all things that move and stand,—  He hath been won, Herald who sits in light, making effectual all our holy works.

1.70.d: गोषु परशस्तिं वनेषु धिषे भरन्त विश्वे बलिं सवर्णः | वि तवा नरः पुरुत्रा सपर्यन पितुर्न जिव्रेर्वि वेदोभरन्त ||
1.70.e: Thou settest value on our cows and woods: all shall bring tribute to us to the light.  Men have served thee in many and sundry spots, parting, as ’twere, an aged father's wealth.

1.70.d: साधुर्न गर्ध्नुरस्तेव शूरो यातेव भीमस्त्वेषः समत्सु ||
1.70.e: Like a brave archer, like one skilled and bold, a fierce avenger, so he shines in fight.

1.71.d: उप पर जिन्वन्नुशतीरुशन्तं पतिं न नित्यं जनयः सनीळाः | सवसारः शयावीमरुषीमजुष्रञ्चित्रमुछन्तीमुषसं न गावः ||
1.71.e: LOVING the loving One, as wives their husband, the sisters of one home have urged him forward,  Bright-coloured, even, as the cows love morning, dark, breaking forth to view, and redly beaming.

1.71.d: वीळु चिद दर्ळ्हा पितरो न उक्थैरद्रिं रुजन्नङगिरसो रवेण | चक्रुर्दिवो बर्हतो गातुमस्मे अहः सवर्विविदुः केतुमुस्राः ||
1.71.e: Our sires with lauds burst e’en the firm-set fortress, yea, the Aṅgirases, with roar, the mountain.  They made for us a way to reach high heaven, they found us day, light, day's sign, beams of morning.

1.71.d: दधन्न्र्तं धनयन्नस्य धीतिमादिदर्यो दिधिष्वो विभ्र्त्राः | अत्र्ष्यन्तीरपसो यन्त्यछा देवाञ जन्म परयसा वर्धयन्तीः ||
1.71.e: They stablished order, made his service fruitful; then parting them among the longing faithful,  Not thirsting after aught, they come, most active, while with sweet food the race of Gods they strengthen.

1.71.d: मथीद यदीं विभ्र्तो मातरिश्वा गर्हे-गर्हे शयेतो जेन्यो भूत | आदीं राज्ञे न सहीयसे सचा सन्ना दूत्यं भर्गवाणो विवाय ||
1.71.e: Since Mātariśvan, far-diffused, hath stirred him, and he in every house grown bright and noble,  He, Bhṛgu-like I hath gone as his companion, as on commission to a greater Sovran.

1.71.d: महे यत पित्र ईं रसं दिवे करव तसरत पर्शन्यश्चिकित्वान | सर्जदस्ता धर्षता दिद्युमस्मै सवायां देवो दुहितरि तविषिं धात ||
1.71.e: When man poured juice to Heaven, the mighty Father, he knew and freed himself from close embracement.  The archer boldly shot at him his arrow, and the God threw his splendour on his Daughter.

1.71.d: सव आ यस्तुभ्यं दम आ विभाति नमो वा दाशादुशतो अनु दयून | वर्धो अग्ने वयो अस्य दविबर्हा यासद राया सरथं यं जुनासि ||
1.71.e: Whoso, hath flames for thee within his dwelling, or brings the worship which thou lovest daily,  Do thou of double might increase his substance: may he whom thou incitest meet with riches.

1.71.d: अग्निं विश्वा अभि पर्क्षः सचन्ते समुद्रं न सरवतः सप्त यह्वीः | न जामिभिर्वि चिकिते वयो नो विदा देवेषु परमतिं चिकित्वान ||
1.71.e: All sacrificial viands wait on Agni as the Seven mighty Rivers seek the ocean.  Not by our brethren was our food discovered: find with the Gods care for us, thou who knowest.

1.71.d: आ यदिषे नर्पतिं तेज आनट छुचि रेतो निषिक्तं दयौरभीके | अग्निः शर्धमनवद्यं युवानं सवाध्यं जनयत सूदयच्च ||
1.71.e: When light hath filled the Lord of men for increase, straight from the heaven descends the limpid moisture.  Agni hath brought to light and filled with spirit the youthful host blameless and well providing.

1.71.d: मनो न यो.अध्वनः सद्य एत्येकः सत्रा सूरो वस्व ईशे | राजाना मित्रावरुणा सुपाणी गोषु परियमम्र्तं रक्षमाणा ||
1.71.e: He who like thought goes swiftly on his journey, the Sun, alone is ever Lord of riches.  The Kings with fair hands, Varuṇa and Mitra, protect the precious nectar in our cattle.

1.71.d: मा नो अग्ने सख्या पित्र्याणि पर मर्षिष्ठा अभि विदुष कविः सन | नभो न रूपं जरिमा मिनाति पुरा तस्या अभिशस्तेरधीहि ||
1.71.e: O Agni, break not our ancestral friendship, Sage as thou art, endowed with deepest knowledge.  Old age, like gathering cloud, impairs the body: before that evil be come nigh protect me.

1.72.d: नि काव्या वेधसः शश्वतस कर्हस्ते दधानो नर्या पुरूणि | अग्निर्भुवद रयिपती रयीणां सत्रा चक्राणो अम्र्तानि विश्वा ||
1.72.e: THOUGH holding many gifts for men, he humbleth the higher powers of each wise ordainer.  Agni is now the treasure-lord of treasures, for ever granting all immortal bounties.

1.72.d: अस्मे वत्सं परि षन्तं न विन्दन्निछन्तो विश्वे अम्र्ता अमूराः | शरमयुवः पदव्यो धियन्धास्तस्थुः पदे परमेचार्वग्नेः ||
1.72.e: The Gods infallible all searching found not him, the dear Babe who still is round about us.  Worn weary, following his track, devoted, they reached the lovely highest home of Agni.

1.72.d: तिस्रो यदग्ने शरदस्त्वामिच्छुचिं घर्तेन शुचयः सपर्यान | नामानि चिद दधिरे यज्ञियान्यसूदयन्त तन्वः सुजाताः ||
1.72.e: Because with holy oil the pure Ones, Agni, served thee the very pure three autumn seasons,  Therefore they won them holy names for worship, and nobly born they dignified their bodies.

1.72.d: आ रोदसी बर्हती वेविदानाः पर रुद्रिया जभ्रिरे यज्ञियासः | विदन मर्तो नेमधिता चिकित्वानग्निं पदे परमे तस्थिवांसम ||
1.72.e: Making them known to spacious earth and heaven, the holy Ones revealed the powers of Rudra.  The mortal band, discerning in the distance, found Agni standing in the loftiest station.

1.72.d: संजानाना उप सीदन्नभिज्ञु पत्नीवन्तो नमस्यं नमस्यन | रिरिक्वांसस्तन्वः कर्ण्वत सवाः सखा सख्युर्निमिषिरक्षमाणाः ||
1.72.e: Nigh they approached, one-minded, with their spouses, kneeling to him adorable paid worship.  Friend finding in his own friend's eye protection, they made their own the bodies which they chastened.

1.72.d: तरिः सप्त यद गुह्यानि तवे इत पदाविदन निहिता यज्ञियासः | तेभी रक्षन्ते अम्र्तं सजोषाः पशूञ्च सथातॄञ्चरथं च पाहि ||
1.72.e: Soon as the holy beings had discovered the thrice-seven mystic things contained within thee,  With these, one-minded, they preserve the Amṛta: guard thou the life of all their plants and cattle.

1.72.d: विद्वानग्ने वयुनानि कषितीनां वयानुषक छुरुधो जीवसेधाः | अन्तर्विद्वानध्वनो देवयानानतन्द्रो दूतो अभवो हविर्वाट ||
1.72.e: Thou, Agni, knower of men's works, hast sent us good food in constant course for our subsistence:  Thou deeply skilled in paths of Gods becamest an envoy never wearied, offering-bearer.

1.72.d: सवाध्यो दिव आ सप्त यह्वी रायो दुरो वय रतज्ञा अजानन | विदद गव्यं सरमा दर्ळ्हमूर्वं येना नु कं मानुषीभोजते विट ||
1.72.e: Knowing the Law, the seven strong floods from heaven, full of good thought, discerned the doors of riches.  Saramā found the cattle's firm-built prison whereby the race of man is still supported.

1.72.d: आ ये विश्वा सवपत्यानि तस्थुः कर्ण्वानासो अम्र्तत्वाय गातुम | मह्ना महद्भिः पर्थिवी वि तस्थे माता पुत्रैरदितिर्धायसे वेः ||
1.72.e: They who approached all noble operations making a path that leads to life immortal,  To be the Bird's support, the spacious mother, Aditi, and her great Sons stood in power.

1.72.d: अधि सरियं नि दधुश्चारुमस्मिन दिवो यदक्षी अम्र्ता अक्र्ण्वन | अध कषरन्ति सिन्धवो न सर्ष्टाः पर नी चीरग्नेरुषीरजानन ||
1.72.e: When Gods immortal made both eyes of heaven, they gave to him the gift of beauteous glory.  Now they flow forth like rivers set in motion: they knew the Red Steeds coming down, O Agni.

1.73.d: रयिर्न यः पित्र्वित्तो वयोधाः सुप्रणीतिश्चिकितुषो नशासुः | सयोनाशीरतिथिर्न परीणानो होतेव सद्म विधतो वि तारीत ||
1.73.e: HE who gives food, like patrimonial riches and guides aright like some wise man's instruction,  Loved like a guest who lies in pleasant lodging,—may he, as Priest, prosper his servant's dwelling.

1.73.d: देवो न यः सविता सत्यमन्मा करत्वा निपाति वर्जनानि विश्वा | पुरुप्रशस्तो अमतिर्न सत्य आत्मेव शेवो दिधिषाय्यो भूत ||
1.73.e: He who like Savitar the God, true-minded protecteth with his power. all acts of vigour,  Truthful, like splendour, glorified by many, like breath joy-giving,—all must strive to win him.

1.73.d: देवो न यः पर्थिवीं विश्वधाया उपक्षेति हितमित्रो न राजा | पुरःसदः शर्मसदो न वीरा अनवद्या पतिजुष्टेव नारी ||
1.73.e: He who on earth dwells like a king surrounded by faithful friends, like a God all-sustaining,  Like heroes who preside, who sit in safety: like as a blameless dame dear to her husband.

1.73.d: तं तवा नरो दम आ नित्यमिद्धमग्ने सचन्त कषितिषु धरुवासु | अधि दयुम्नं नि दधुर्भूर्यस्मिन भवा विश्वायुर्धरुणो रयीणाम ||
1.73.e: Thee, such, in settlements secure, O Agni, our men serve ever kindled in each dwelling.  On him have they laid splendour in abundance: dear to all men, bearer be he of riches.

1.73.d: वि पर्क्षो अग्ने मघवानो अश्युर्वि सूरयो ददतो विश्वमायुः | सनेम वाजं समिथेष्वर्यो भागं देवेषु शरवसेदधानाः ||
1.73.e: May thy rich worshippers win food, O Agni, and princes gain long life who bring oblation.  May we get booty from our foe in battle, presenting to the Gods their share for glory.

1.73.d: रतस्य हि धेनवो वावशानाः समदूध्नीः पीपयन्त दयुभक्ताः | परावतः सुमतिं भिक्षमाणा वि सिन्धवः समया सस्रुरद्रिम ||
1.73.e: The cows of holy law, sent us by Heaven, have swelled with laden udders, loudly lowing;  Soliciting his favour, from a distance the rivers to the rock have flowed together.

1.73.d: तवे अग्ने सुमतिं भिक्षमाणा दिवि शरवो दधिरे यज्ञियासः | नक्ता च चक्रुरुषसा विरूपे कर्ष्णं च वर्णमरुणं च सं धुः ||
1.73.e: Agni, with thee, soliciting thy favour, the holy Ones have gained glory in heaven.  They made the Night and Dawn of different colours, and set the black and purple hues together.

1.73.d: यान राये मर्तान सुषूदो अग्ने ते सयाम मघवानो वयं च | छायेव विश्वं भुवनं सिसक्ष्यापप्रिवान रोदसी अन्तरिक्षम ||
1.73.e: May we and those who worship be the mortals whom thou, O Agni, leadest on to riches.  Thou hast filled earth and heaven and air's mid-region, and followest the whole world like a shadow.

1.73.d: अर्वद्भिरग्ने अर्वतो नर्भिर्नॄन वीरैर्वीरान वनुयामा तवोताः | ईशानासः पित्र्वित्तस्य रायो वि सूरयः शतहिमा नो अश्युः ||
1.73.e: Aided by thee, O Agni, may we conquer steeds with steeds, men with men, heroes with heroes,  Lords of the wealth transmitted by our fathers: and may our princes live a hundred winters.

1.73.d: एता ते अग्न उचथानि वेधो जुष्टानि सन्तु मनसे हर्दे च | शकेम रायः सुधुरो यमं ते.अधि शरवो देवभक्तं दधानाः ||
1.73.e: May these our hymns of praise, Agni, Ordainer, be pleasant to thee in thy heart and spirit.  May we have power to hold thy steeds of riches, laying on thee the God-sent gift of glory.

1.74.d: उपप्रयन्तो अध्वरं मन्त्रं वोचेमाग्नये | आरे अस्मे च शर्ण्वते ||
1.74.e: As forth to sacrifice we go, a hymn to a hymn let us say,  Who hears us even when afar;

1.74.d: यः सनीहितीषु पूर्व्यः संजग्मानासु कर्ष्टिषु | अरक्षद दाशुषे गयम ||
1.74.e: Who, from of old, in carnage, when the people gathered, hath preserved  His household for the worshipper.

1.74.d: उत बरुवन्तु जन्तव उदग्निर्व्र्त्रहाजनि | धनंजयो रणे-रणे ||
1.74.e: And let men say, Agni is born, e’en he who slayeth Vṛtra, he  Who winneth wealth in every fight.

1.74.d: यस्य दूतो असि कषये वेषि हव्यानि वीतये | दस्मत कर्णोष्यध्वरम ||
1.74.e: Him in whose house an envoy thou lovest to taste his offered gifts,  And strengthenest his sacrifice,

1.74.d: तमित सुहव्यमङगिरः सुदेवं सहसो यहो | जना आहुः सुबर्हिषम ||
1.74.e: Him, Aṅgiras, thou Son of Strength, all men call happy in his God,  His offerings, and his sacred grass.

1.74.d: आ च वहासि तानिह देवानुप परशस्तये | हव्या सुश्चन्द्र वीतये ||
1.74.e: Hitherward shalt thou bring these Gods to our laudation and to taste.  These offered gifts, fair-shining One.

1.74.d: न योरुपब्दिरश्व्यः शर्ण्वे रथस्य कच्चन | यदग्नेयासि दूत्यम ||
1.74.e: When, Agni, on thine embassage thou goest not a sound is heard of steed or straining of thy car.

1.74.d: तवोतो वाज्यह्रयो.अभि पूर्वस्मादपरः | पर दाश्वानग्ने अस्थात ||
1.74.e: Aided by thee uninjured, strong, one after other, goes he forth:  Agni, the offerer forward steps.

1.74.d: उत दयुमत सुवीर्यं बर्हदग्ने विवाससि | देवेभ्यो देव दाशुषे ||
1.74.e: And splendid strength, heroic, high, Agni, thou grantest from the Gods,  Thou God, to him who offers gifts.

1.75.d: जुषस्व सप्रथस्तमं वचो देवप्सरस्तमम | हव्या जुह्वानासनि ||
1.75.e: ACCEPT our loudest-sounding hymn, food most delightful to the Gods,  Pouring our offerings in thy mouth.

1.75.d: अथा ते अङगिरस्तमाग्ने वेधस्तम परियम | वोचेम बरह्म सानसि ||
1.75.e: Now, Agni, will we say to thee, O wisest and best Aṅgiras,  Our precious, much-availing prayer.

1.75.d: कस्ते जामिर्जनानामग्ने को दाश्वध्वरः | को ह कस्मिन्नसि शरितः ||
1.75.e: Who, Agni, is thy kin, of men? who is thy worthy worshipper?  On whom dependent? who art thou?

1.75.d: तवं जामिर्जनानामग्ने मित्रो असि परियः | सखा सखिभ्य ईड्यः ||
1.75.e: The kinsman, Agni, of mankind, their well beloved Friend art thou,  A Friend whom friends may supplicate.

1.75.d: यजा नो मित्रावरुणा यजा देवान रतं बर्हत | अग्ने यक्षिस्वं दमम ||
1.75.e: Bring to us Mitra, Varuṇa, bring the Gods to mighty sacrifice.  Bring them, O Agni, to thine home.

1.76.d: का त उपेतिर्मनसो वराय भुवदग्ने शन्तमा का मनीषा | को वा यज्ञैः परि दक्षं त आप केन वा ते मनसादाशेम ||
1.76.e: How may the mind draw nigh to please thee, Agni? What hymn of praise shall bring us greatest blessing?  Or who hath gained thy power by sacrifices? or with what mind shall we bring thee oblations?

1.76.d: एह्यग्न इह होता नि षीदादब्धः सु पुरेता भवा नः | अवतां तवा रोदसी विश्वमिन्वे यजा महे सौमनसाय देवान ||
1.76.e: Come hither, Agni; sit thee down as Hotar; be thou who never wast deceived our leader.  May Heaven and Earth, the all-pervading, love thee: worship the Gods to win for us their favour.

1.76.d: पर सु विश्वान रक्षसो धक्ष्यग्ने भवा यज्ञानामभिशस्तिपावा | अथा वह सोमपतिं हरिभ्यामातिथ्यमस्मै चक्र्मा सुदाव्ने ||
1.76.e: Burn thou up all the Rākṣasas, O Agni; ward thou off curses from our sacrifices.  Bring hither with his Bays the Lord of Soma: here is glad welcome for the Bounteous Giver.

1.76.d: परजावता वचसा वह्निरासा च हुवे नि च सत्सीह देवैः | वेषि होत्रमुत पोत्रं यजत्र बोधि परयन्तर्जनितर्वसूनाम ||
1.76.e: Thou Priest with lip and voice that bring us children hast been invoked. Here with the Gods be seated.  Thine is the task of Cleanser and Presenter: waken us, Wealth-bestower and Producer.

1.76.d: यथा विप्रस्य मनुषो हविर्भिर्देवानयजः कविभिः कविः सन | एवा होतः सत्यतर तवमद्याग्ने मन्द्रया जुह्वा यजस्व ||
1.76.e: As with oblations of the priestly Manus thou worshippedst the Gods, a Sage with sages,  So now, O truthfullest Invoker Agni, worship this day with joy-bestowing ladle.

1.77.d: कथा दाशेमाग्नये कास्मै देवजुष्टोच्यते भामिने गीः | यो मर्त्येष्वम्र्त रतावा होता यजिष्ठ इत कर्णोति देवान ||
1.77.e: How shall we pay oblation unto Agni? What hymn, Godloved, is said to him refulgent?  Who, deathless, true to Law, mid men a herald, bringeth the Gods as best of sacrificers?

1.77.d: यो अध्वरेषु शन्तम रतावा होता तमू नमोभिरा कर्णुध्वम | अग्निर्यद वेर्मर्ताय देवान स चा बोधाति मनसायजाति ||
1.77.e: Bring him with reverence hither, most propitious in sacrifices, true to Law, the herald;  For Agni, when he seeks the Gods for mortals, knows them full well and worships them in spirit.

1.77.d: स हि करतुः स मर्यः स साधुर्मित्रो न भूदद्भुतस्य रथीः | तं मेधेषु परथमं देवयन्तीर्विश उप बरुवते दस्ममारीः ||
1.77.e: For he is mental power, a man, and perfect; he is the bringer, friend-like, of the wondrous.  The pious Āryan tribes at sacrifices address them first to him who doeth marvels.

1.77.d: स नो नर्णां नर्तमो रिशाद अग्निर्गिरो.अवसा वेतु धीतिम | तना च ये मघवानः शविष्ठ वाजप्रसूता इषयन्तमन्म ||
1.77.e: May Agni, foe-destroyer, manliest Hero, accept with love our hymns and our devotion.  So may the liberal lords whose strength is strongest, urged by their riches, stir our thoughts with vigour.

1.77.d: एवाग्निर्गोतमेभिर्र्तावा विप्रेभिरस्तोष्ट जातवेदाः | स एषु दयुम्नं पीपयत स वाजं स पुष्टिं याति जोषमा चिकित्वान ||
1.77.e: Thus Agni Jātavedas, true to Order, hath by the priestly Gotamas been lauded.  May he augment in them splendour and vigour: observant, as he lists, he gathers increase.

1.78.d: अभि तवा गोतमा गिरा जातवेदो विचर्षणे | दयुम्नैरभि पर णोनुमः ||
1.78.e: O JĀTAVEDAS, keen and swift, we Gotamas with sacred song exalt thee for thy glories' sake.

1.78.d: तमु तवा गोतमो गिरा रायस्कामो दुवस्यति | दयुम्नैरभि पर णोनुमः ||
1.78.e: Thee, as thou art, desiring wealth Gotama worships with his song:  We laud thee for thy glories' sake.

1.78.d: तमु तवा वाजसातममङगिरस्वद धवामहे | दयुम्नैरभि पर णोनुमः ||
1.78.e: As such, like Aṅgiras we call on thee best winner of the spoil:  We laud thee for thy glories' sake.

1.78.d: तमु तवा वर्त्रहन्तमं यो दस्यून्रवधूनुषे | दयुम्नैरभि पर णोनुमः ||
1.78.e: Thee, best of Vṛtra-slayers, thee who shakest off our Dasyu foes:  We laud thee for thy glories' sake.

1.78.d: अवोचाम रहूगणा अग्नये मधुमद वचः | दयुम्नैरभि पर णोनुमः ||
1.78.e: A pleasant song to Agni we, sons of Rahūgaṅa, have sung:  We laud thee for thy glories' sake.

1.79.d: हिरण्यकेशो रजसो विसारे.अहिर्धुनिर्वात इव धरजीमान | शुचिभ्राजा उषसो नवेदा यशस्वतीरपस्युवो न सत्याः ||
1.79.e: HE in mid-air's expanse hath golden tresses; a raging serpent, like the rushing tempest:  Purely refulgent, knowing well the morning; like honourable dames, true, active workers.

1.79.d: आ ते सुपर्णा अमिनन्तमेवैः कर्ष्णो नोनाव वर्षभो यदीदम | शिवाभिर्न समयमानाभिरागात पतन्ति मिहः सतनयन्त्यभ्रा ||
1.79.e: Thy well-winged flashes strengthen in their manner, when the black Bull hath bellowed round about us.  With drops that bless and seem to smile he cometh: the waters fall, the clouds utter their thunder.

1.79.d: यदीं रतस्य पयसा पियानो नयन्न्र्तस्य पथिभी रजिष्ठैः | अर्यमा मित्रो वरुनः परिज्मा तवचं पर्ञ्चन्त्युपरस्य योनौ ||
1.79.e: When he comes streaming with the milk of worship, conducting by directest paths of Order  Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa, Parijman fill the hide full where lies the nether press-stone.

1.79.d: अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो | अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि शरवः ||
1.79.e: O Agni, thou who art the lord of wealth in kine, thou Son of Strength,  Vouchsafe to us, O Jātavedas, high renown.

1.79.d: स इधनो वसुष कविरग्निरीळेन्यो गिरा | रेवदस्मभ्यम्पुर्वणीक दीदिहि ||
1.79.e: He, Agni, kindled, good and wise, must be exalted in our song:  Shine, thou of many forms, shine radiantly on us.

1.79.d: कषपो राजन्नुत तमनाग्ने वस्तोरुतोषसः | स तिग्मजम्भ रक्षसो दह परति ||
1.79.e: O Agni, shining of thyself by night and when the morning breaks,  Burn, thou whose teeth are sharp, against the Rākṣasas.

1.79.d: अवा नो अग्न ऊतिभिर्गायत्रस्य परभर्मणि | विश्वासु धीषु वन्द्य ||
1.79.e: Adorable in all our rites, favour us, Agni, with thine aid,  When the great hymn is chanted forth.

1.79.d: आ नो अग्ने रयिं भर सत्रासाहं वरेण्यम | विश्वासु पर्त्सुदुष्टरम ||
1.79.e: Bring to us ever-conquering wealth, wealth, Agni, worthy of our choice,  In all our frays invincible.

1.79.d: आ नो अग्ने सुचेतुना रयिं विश्वायुपोषसम | मार्डीकं धेहि जीवसे ||
1.79.e: Give us, O Agni, through thy grace wealth that supporteth all our life,  Thy favour so that we may live.

1.79.d: पर पूतास्तिग्मशोचिषे वाचो गोतमाग्नये | भरस्व सुम्नयुर्गिरः ||
1.79.e: O Gotama, desiring bliss present thy songs composed with care  To Agni of the pointed flames.

1.79.d: यो नो अग्ने.अभिदासत्यन्ति दूरे पदीष्ट सः | अस्माकमिद वर्धे भव ||
1.79.e: May the man fall, O Agni, who near or afar assaileth us:  Do thou increase and prosper us.

1.79.d: सहस्राक्षो विचर्षणिरग्नी रक्षांसि सेधति | होता गर्णीत उक्थ्यः ||
1.79.e: Keen and swift Agni, thousand-eyed, chaseth the Rākṣasas afar:  He singeth, herald meet for lauds.

1.80.d: इत्था हि सोम इन मदे बरह्मा चकार वर्धनम | शविष्ठ वज्रिन्नोजसा पर्थिव्या निः शशा अहिमर्चन्ननु सवराज्यम ||
1.80.e: THUS in the Soma, in wild joy the Brahman hath exalted thee:  Thou, mightiest thunder-armed, hast driven by force the Dragon from the earth, lauding thine own imperial sway.

1.80.d: स तवामदद वर्षा मदः सोमः शयेनाभ्र्तः सुतः | येना वृत्रं निरद्भ्यो जघन्थ वज्रिन्नोजसार्चन्ननु स्वराज्यम् ||
1.80.e: The mighty flowing Soma-draught, brought by the Hawk, hath gladdened thee,  That in thy strength, O Thunderer, thou hast struck down Vṛtra from the floods, lauding thine own imperial sway.

1.80.d: परेह्यभीहि धर्ष्णुहि न ते वज्रो नि यंसते | इन्द्र नृम्णं हि ते शवो हनो वृत्रं जया अपोऽर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यम् ||
1.80.e: Go forward, meet the foe, be bold; thy bolt of thunder is not checked.  Manliness, Indra, is thy might: stay Vṛtra, make the waters thine, lauding thine own imperial sway.

1.80.d: निरिन्द्र भूम्या अधि वर्त्रं जघन्थ निर्दिवः | सृजा मरुत्वतीरव जीवधन्या इमा अपोऽर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यम् ||
1.80.e: Thou smotest Vṛtra from the earth, smotest him, Indra, from the sky.  Let these life-fostering waters flow attended by the Marut host, lauding thine own imperial sway.

1.80.d: इन्द्रो वर्त्रस्य दोधतः सानुं वज्रेण हीळितः | अभिक्रम्याव जिघ्नतेऽपः सर्माय चोदयन्नर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यम् ||
1.80.e: The wrathful Indra with his bolt of thunder rushing on the foe,  Smote fierce on trembling Vṛtra's back, and loosed the waters free to run, lauding his own imperial sway.

1.80.d: अधि सानौ नि जिघ्नते वज्रेण शतपर्वणा | मन्दान इन्द्रो अन्धसः सखिभ्यो गातुमिछत्यर्चन्न... ||
1.80.e: With hundred-jointed thunderbolt Indra hath struck him on the back,  And, while rejoicing in the juice, seeketh prosperity for friends, lauding his own imperial sway.

1.80.d: इन्द्र तुभ्यमिदद्रिवो.अनुत्तं वज्रिन वीर्यम | यद ध तयम्मायिनं मर्गं तमु तवं माययावधीरर्चन्न... ||
1.80.e: Indra, unconquered might is thine, Thunderer, Caster of the Stone;  For thou with thy surpassing power smotest to death the guileful beast, lauding thine own imperial sway.

1.80.d: वि ते वज्रासो अस्थिरन नवतिं नाव्या अनु | महत त इन्द्र वीर्यं बाह्वोस्ते बलं हितमर्चन्न... ||
1.80.e: Far over ninety spacious floods thy thunderbolts were cast abroad:  Great, Indra, is thy hero might, and strength is seated in thine arms, lauding thine own imperial sway.

1.80.d: सहस्रं साकमर्चत परि षटोभत विंशतिः | शतैनमन्वनोनवुरिन्द्राय बरह्मोद्यतमर्चन्न... ||
1.80.e: Laud him a thousand all at once, shout twenty forth the hymn of praise.  Hundreds have sung aloud to him, to Indra hath the prayer been raised, lauding his own imperial sway.

1.80.d: इन्द्रो वर्त्रस्य तविषीं निरहन सहसा सहः | महत तदस्य पौंस्यं वर्त्रं जघन्वानस्र्जदर्चन्न... ||
1.80.e: Indra hath smitten down the power of Vṛtra,—might with stronger might.  This was his manly exploit, he slew Vṛtra and let loose the floods, lauding his own imperial sway.

1.80.d: इमे चित तव मन्यवे वेपेते भियसा मही | यदिन्द्र वज्रिन्नोजसा वर्त्रं मरुत्वानवधीरर्चन्न... ||
1.80.e: Yea, even this great Pair of Worlds trembled in terror at thy wrath,  When, Indra, Thunderer, Marut-girt, thou slewest Vṛtra in thy strength, lauding thine own imperial sway.

1.80.d: न वेपसा न तन्यतेन्द्रं वर्त्रो वि बीभयत | अभ्येनं वज्र आयसः सहस्रभ्र्ष्टिरायतार्चन्न... ||
1.80.e: But Vṛtra scared not Indra with his shaking or his thunder roar.  On him that iron thunderbolt fell fiercely with its thousand points, lauding his own imperial sway.

1.80.d: यद वर्त्रं तव चशनिं वज्रेण समयोधयः | अहिमिन्द्रजिघांसतो दिवि ते बद्बधे शवो.अर्चन्न... ||
1.80.e: When with the thunder thou didst make thy dart and Vṛtra meet in war,  Thy might, O Indra, fain to slay the Dragon, was set firm in heaven, lauding thine own imperial sway.

1.80.d: अभिष्टने ते अद्रिवो यत सथा जगच्च रेजते | तवष्टा चित तव मन्यव इन्द्र वेविज्यते भियार्चन्न... ||
1.80.e: When at thy shout, O Thunder-armed, each thing both fixed and moving shook,  E’en Tvaṣṭar trembled at thy wrath and quaked with fear because of thee, lauding thine own imperial sway.

1.80.d: नहि नु यादधीमसीन्द्रं को वीर्या परः | तस्मिन नर्म्णमुत करतुं देवा ओजांसि सं दधुरर्चन्न... ||
1.80.e: There is not, in our knowledge, one who passeth Indra in his strength:  In him the Deities have stored manliness, insight, power and might, lauding his own imperial sway.

1.80.d: यमथर्व मनुष पिता दध्यं धियमत्नत | तस्मिन बरह्माणि पुर्वथेन्द्र उक्था समग्मतार्चन्न... ||
1.80.e: Still as of old, whatever rite Atharvan, Manus sire of all,  Dadhyach performed, their prayer and praise united in that Indra meet, lauding his own imperial sway.

1.81.d: इन्द्रो मदाय वाव्र्धे शवसे वर्त्रहा नर्भिः | तमिन महत्स्वाजिषूतेमर्भे हवामहे स वाजेषु पर नो.अविषत ||
1.81.e: THE men have lifted Indra up, the Vṛtra slayer, to joy and strength:  Him, verily, we invocate in battles whether great or small: be he our aid in deeds of might.

1.81.d: असि हि वीर सेन्यो.असि भूरि पराददिः | असि दभ्रस्य चिद्व्र्धो यजमानाय शिक्षसि सुन्वते भूरि ते वसु ||
1.81.e: Thou, Hero, art a warrior, thou art giver of abundant spoil.  Strengthening e’en the feeble, thou aidest the sacrificer, thou givest the offerer ample wealth.

1.81.d: यदुदीरत आजयो धर्ष्णवे धीयते धना | युक्ष्वा मदच्युता हरी कं हनः कं वसौ दधो.अस्मानिन्द्र वसौ दधः ||
1.81.e: When war and battles are on foot, booty is laid before the bold.  Yoke thou thy wildly-rushing Bays. Whom wilt thou slay and whom enrich? Do thou, O Indra, make us rich.

1.81.d: करत्वामहाननुष्वधं भीम आ वाव्र्धे शवः | शरियर्ष्व उपाकयोर्नि शिप्री हरिवान दधे हस्तयोर्वज्रमायसम ||
1.81.e: Mighty through wisdom, as he lists, terrible, he hath waxed in strength.  Lord of Bay Steeds, strong-jawed, sublime, he in joined hands for glory's sake hath grasped his iron thunderbolt.

1.81.d: आ पप्रौ पार्थिवं रजो बद्बधे रोचना दिवि | न तवावानिन्द्र कश्चन न जातो न जनिष्यते.अति विश्वं ववक्षिथ ||
1.81.e: He filled the earthly atmosphere and pressed against the lights in heaven.  None like thee ever hath been born, none, Indra, will be born like thee. Thou hast waxed mighty over all.

1.81.d: यो अर्यो मर्तभोजनं पराददाति दाशुषे | इन्द्रो अस्मभ्यंशिक्षतु वि भजा भूरि ते वसु भक्षीय तव राधसः ||
1.81.e: May he who to the offerer gives the foeman's man-sustaining food,  May Indra lend his aid to us. Deal forth—abundant is thy wealth—that in thy bounty I may share.

1.81.d: मदे-मदे हि नो ददिर्यूथा गवां रजुक्रतुः | सं गर्भायपुरू शतोभयाहस्त्या वसु शिशीहि राय आ भर ||
1.81.e: He, righteous-hearted, at each time of rapture gives us herds of kine.  Gather in both thy hands for us treasures of many hundred sorts. Sharpen thou us, and bring us wealth.

1.81.d: मादयस्व सुते सचा शवसे शूर राधसे | विद्मा हि तवापुरूवसुमुप कामान सस्र्ज्महे.अथा नो.अविता भव ||
1.81.e: Refresh thee, Hero, with the juice outpoured for bounty and for strength.  We know thee Lord of ample store, to thee have sent our hearts' desires: be therefore our Protector thou.

1.81.d: एते त इन्द्र जन्तवो विश्वं पुष्यन्ति वार्यम | अन्तर्हि खयोजनानामर्यो वेदो अदाशुषां तेषां नो वेद आ भर ||
1.81.e: These people, Indra, keep for thee all that is worthy of thy choice.  Discover thou, as Lord, the wealth of men who offer up no gifts: bring thou to us this wealth of theirs.

1.82.d: उपो षु शर्णुही गिरो मघवन मातथा इव | यदा नः सून्र्तावतः कर आदर्थयास इद योजा नविन्द्र ते हरी ||
1.82.e: GRACIOUSLY listen to our songs, Maghavan, be not negligent.  As thou hast made us full of joy and lettest us solicit thee, now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.

1.82.d: अक्षन्नमीमदन्त हयव परिया अधूषत | अस्तोषत सवभानवो विप्रा नविष्ठया मती योजा ... ||
1.82.e: Well have they eaten and rejoiced; the friends have risen and passed away.  The sages luminous in themselves have. praised thee with their latest hymn. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.

1.82.d: सुसन्द्र्शं तवा वयं मघवन वन्दिषीमहि | पर नूनं पूर्णवन्धुर सतुतो याहि वशाननु योजा ... ||
1.82.e: Maghavan, we will reverence thee who art so fair to look upon.  Thus praised, according to our wish come now with richly laden car. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.

1.82.d: स घा तं वर्षणं रथमधि तिष्ठाति गोविदम | यःपात्रं हारियोजनं पूर्णमिन्द्र चिकेतति योजा ... ||
1.82.e: He will in very truth ascend the powerful car that finds the kine,  Who thinks upon the well-filled bowl, the Tawny Coursers' harnesser. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.

1.82.d: युक्तस्ते अस्तु दक्षिण उत सव्यः शतक्रतो ||
1.82.e: Let, Lord of Hundred Powers, thy Steeds be harnessed on the right and left.  Therewith in rapture of the juice, draw near to thy beloved Spouse. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.

1.82.d: तेन जायामुप परियां मन्दानो याह्यन्धसो योजा ... ||
1.82.e: With holy prayer I yoke thy long-maned pair of Bays: come hitherward; thou holdest them in both thy hands.  The stirring draughts of juice outpoured have made thee glad: thou, Thunderer, hast rejoiced with Pūṣan and thy Spouse.

1.82.d: युनज्मि ते बरह्मणा केशिना हरी उप पर याहि दधिषे गभस्त्योः | उत तवा सुतासो रभसा अमन्दिषुः पूषण्वान वज्रिन समु पत्न्यामदः ||

1.83.d: अश्वावति परथमो गोषु गछति सुप्रावीरिन्द्र मर्त्यस्तवोतिभिः | तमित पर्णक्षि वसुना भवीयसा सिन्धुमापो यथाभितो विचेतसः ||
1.83.e: INDRA, the mortal man well guarded by thine aid goes foremost in the wealth of horses and of kine.  With amplest wealth thou fillest him, as round about the waters clearly seen afar fill Sindhu full.

1.83.d: आपो न देवीरुप यन्ति होत्रियमवः पश्यन्ति विततं यथा रजः | पराचैर्देवासः पर णयन्ति देवयुं बरह्मप्रियं जोषयन्ते वरा इव ||
1.83.e: The heavenly Waters come not nigh the priestly bowl: they but look down and see how far mid-air is spread:  The Deities conduct the pious man to them: like suitors they delight in him who loveth prayer.

1.83.d: अधि दवयोरदधा उक्थ्यं वचो यतस्रुचा मिथुना या सपर्यतः | असंयत्तो वरते ते कषेति पुष्यति भद्रा शक्तिर्यजमानाय सुन्वते ||
1.83.e: Praiseworthy blessing hast thou laid upon the pair who with uplifted ladle serve thee, man and wife.  Unchecked he dwells and prospers in thy law: thy power brings blessing to the sacrificer pouring gifts.

1.83.d: आदङगिराः परथमं दधिरे वय इद्धाग्नयः शम्या येसुक्र्त्यया | सर्वं पणेः समविन्दन्त भोजनमश्वावन्तं गोमन्तमा पशुं नरः ||
1.83.e: First the Aṅgirases won themselves vital power, whose fires were kindled through good deeds and sacrifice.  The men together found the Paṇi's hoarded wealth, the cattle, and the wealth in horses and in kine.

1.83.d: यज्ञैरथर्वा परथमः पथस्तते ततः सूर्यो वरतपावेन आजनि | आ गा आजदुशना काव्यः सचा यमस्य जातमम्र्तं यजामहे ||
1.83.e: Atharvan first by sacrifices laid the paths then, guardian of the Law, sprang up the loving Sun.  Uśanā Kāvya straightway hither drove the kine. Let us with offerings honour Yama's deathless birth.

1.83.d: बर्हिर्वा यत सवपत्याय वर्ज्यते.अर्को वा शलोकमाघोषतेदिवि | गरावा यत्र वदति कारुरुक्थ्यस्तस्येदिन्द्रो अभिपित्वेषु रण्यति ||
1.83.e: When sacred grass is trimmed to aid the auspicious work, or the hymn makes its voice of praise sound to the sky.  Where the stone rings as ’twere a singer skilled in laud,—Indra in truth delights when these come near to him.

1.84.d: असावि सोम इन्द्र ते शविष्ठ धर्ष्णवा गहि | आ तवा पर्णक्त्विन्द्रियं रजः सूर्यो न रश्मिभिः ||
1.84.e: The Soma hath been pressed for thee, O Indra; mightiest, bold One, come.  May Indra-vigour fill thee full, as the Sun fills mid-air with rays.

1.84.d: इन्द्रमिद धरी वहतो.अप्रतिध्र्ष्टशवसम | रषीणां च सतुतीरुप यज्ञं च मानुषाणाम ||
1.84.e: His pair of Tawny Coursers bring Indra of unresisted might  Hither to Ṛṣis’ songs of praise and sacrifice performed by men.

1.84.d: आ तिष्ठ वर्त्रहन रथं युक्ता ते बरह्मणा हरी | अर्वाचीनं सु ते मनो गरावा कर्णोतु वग्नुना ||
1.84.e: Slayer of Vṛtra, mount thy car; thy Bay Steeds have been yoked by prayer.  May, with its voice, the pressing-stone draw thine attention hitherward.

1.84.d: इममिन्द्र सुतं पिब जयेष्ठममर्त्यं मदम | शुक्रस्य तवाभ्यक्षरन धारा रतस्य सादने ||
1.84.e: This poured libation, Indra, drink, immortal, gladdening, excellent.  Streams of the bright have flowed to thee here at the seat of holy Law.

1.84.d: इन्द्राय नूनमर्चतोक्थानि च बरवीतन | सुता अमत्सुरिन्दवो जयेष्ठं नमस्यता सहः ||
1.84.e: Sing glory now to Indra, say to him your solemn eulogies.  The drops poured forth have made him glad: pay reverence to his might supreme.

1.84.d: नकिष टवद रथीतरो हरी यदिन्द्र यछसे | नकिष टवानु मज्मना नकिः सवश्व आनशे ||
1.84.e: When, Indra, thou dost yoke thy Steeds, there is no better charioteer:  None hath surpassed thee in thy might, none with good steeds o’ertaken thee.

1.84.d: य एक इद विदयते वसु मर्ताय दाशुषे | ईशानो अप्रतिष्कुत इन्द्रो अङग ||
1.84.e: He who alone bestoweth on mortal man who offereth gifts,  The ruler of resistless power, is Indra, sure.

1.84.d: कदा मर्तमराधसं पदा कषुम्पमिव सफुरत | कदा नःशुश्रवद गिर इन्द्रो अङग ||
1.84.e: When will he trample, like a weed, the man who hath no gift for him?  When, verily, will Indra hear our songs of praise?

1.84.d: यश्चिद धि तवा बहुभ्य आ सुतावानाविवासति | उग्रं तत पत्यते शव इन्द्रो अङग ||
1.84.e: He who with Soma juice prepared amid the many honours thee,—  Verily Indra gains thereby tremendous might.

1.84.d: सवादोरित्था विषूवतो मध्वः पिबन्ति गौर्यः | या इन्द्रेण सयावरीर्व्र्ष्णा मदन्ति शोभसे वस्वीरनु सवराज्यम ||
1.84.e: The juice of Soma thus diffused, sweet to the taste, the bright cows drink,  Who for the sake of splendour close to mighty Indra's side rejoice, good in their own supremacy.

1.84.d: ता अस्य पर्शनायुवः सोमं शरीणन्ति पर्श्नयः | परिया इन्द्रस्य धेनवो वज्रं हिन्वन्ति सायकं वस्वीर... ||
1.84.e: Craving his touch the dappled kine mingle the Soma with their milk.  The milch-kine dear to Indra send forth his death-dealing thunderbolt, good in their own supremacy.

1.84.d: ता अस्य नमसा सहः सपर्यन्ति परचेतसः | वरतान्यस्य सश्चिरे पुरूणि पूर्वचित्तये वस्वीर... ||
1.84.e: With veneration, passing wise, honouring his victorious might,  They follow close his many laws to win them due preeminence, good in their  own supremacy.

1.84.d: इन्द्रो दधीचो अस्थभिर्व्र्त्राण्यप्रतिष्कुतः | जघान नवतीर्नव ||
1.84.e: With bones of Dadhyach for his arms, Indra, resistless in attack,  Struck nine-and-ninety Vṛtras dead.

1.84.d: इछन्नश्वस्य यच्छिरः पर्वतेष्वपश्रितम | तद विदच्छर्यणावति ||
1.84.e: He, searching for the horse's head, removed among the mountains, found  At Śaryaṇāvān what he sought.

1.84.d: अत्राह गोरमन्वत नाम तवष्टुरपीच्यम | इत्था चन्द्रमसो गर्हे ||
1.84.e: Then verily they recognized the essential form of Tvaṣṭar's Bull,  Here in the mansion of the Moon.

1.84.d: को अद्य युङकते धुरि गा रतस्य शिमीवतो भामिनो दुर्ह्र्णायून | असन्निषून हर्त्स्वसो मयोभून य एषां भर्त्यां रणधत स जीवात ||
1.84.e: Who yokes to-day unto the pole of Order the strong and passionate steers of checkless spirit,  With shaft-armed mouths, heart-piercing, health-bestowing?  Long shall he live who richly pays their service.

1.84.d: क ईषते तुज्यते को बिभाय को मंसते सन्तमिन्द्रं को अन्ति | कस्तोकाय क इभायोत राये.अधि बरवत तन्वे को जनाय ||
1.84.e: Who fleeth forth? who suffereth? who feareth? Who knoweth Indra present, Indra near us?  Who sendeth benediction on his offspring, his household, wealth and person, and the People?

1.84.d: को अग्निमीट्टे हविषा घर्तेन सरुचा यजाता रतुभिर्ध्रुवेभिः | कस्मै देवा आ वहानाशु होम को मंसते वीतिहोत्रः सुदेवः ||
1.84.e: Who with poured oil and offering honours Agni, with ladle worships at appointed seasons?  To whom to the Gods bring oblation quickly? What offerer, God-favoured, knows him thoroughly?

1.84.d: तवमङग पर शंसिषो देवः शविष्ठ मर्त्यम | न तवदन्यो मघवन्नस्ति मर्डितेन्द्र बरवीमि ते वचः ||
1.84.e: Thou as a God, O Mightiest, verily blessest mortal man.  O Maghavan, there is no comforter but thou: Indra, I speak my words to thee.

1.84.d: मा ते राधांसि मा त ऊतयो वसो.अस्मान कदा चना दभन | विश्वा च न उपमिमीहि मानुष वसूनि चर्षणिभ्य आ ||
1.84.e: Let not thy bounteous gifts, let not thy saving help fail us, good Lord, at any time;  And measure out to us, thou lover of mankind, all riches hitherward from men.

1.85.d: पर ये शुम्भन्ते जनयो न सप्तयो यामन रुद्रस्य सूनवःसुदंससः | रोदसी हि मरुतश्चक्रिरे वर्धे मदन्ति वीरा विदथेषु घर्ष्वयः ||
1.85.e: THEY who are glancing forth, like women, on their way, doers of mighty deeds, swift racers, Rudra's Sons,  The Maruts have made heaven and earth increase and grow: in sacrifices they delight, the strong and wild.

1.85.d: त उक्षितासो महिमानमाशत दिवि रुद्रासो अधि चक्रिरे सदः | अर्चन्तो अर्कं जनयन्त इन्द्रियमधि शरियो दधिरे पर्श्निमातरः ||
1.85.e: Grown to their perfect strength greatness have they attained; the Rudras have established their abode in heaven.  Singing their song of praise and generating might, they have put glory on, the Sons whom Pṛśni bare.

1.85.d: गोमातरो यच्छुभयन्ते अञ्जिभिस्तनूषु शुभ्रा दधिरे विरुक्मतः | बाधन्ते विश्वमभिमातिनमप वर्त्मान्येषामनु रीयते घर्तम ||
1.85.e: When, Children of the Cow, they shine in bright attire, and on their fair limbs lay their golden ornaments,  They drive away each adversary from their path, and, following their traces, fatness floweth down,

1.85.d: वि ये भराजन्ते सुमखास रष्टिभिः परच्यावयन्तो अच्युताचिदोजसा | मनोजुवो यन मरुतो रथेष्वा वर्षव्रातासः पर्षतीरयुग्ध्वम ||
1.85.e: When, mighty Warriors, ye who glitter with your spears, o’erthrowing with your strength e’en what is ne’er o’erthrown,  When, O ye Maruts, ye the host that send the rain, had harnessed to your cars the thought-fleet spotted deer.

1.85.d: पर यद रथेषु पर्षतीरयुग्ध्वं वाजे अद्रिं मरुतो रंहयन्तः | उतारुषस्य वि षयन्ति धाराश्चर्मेवोदभिर्व्युन्दन्ति भूम ||
1.85.e: When ye have harnessed to your cars the spotted deer, urging the thunderbolt, O Maruts, to the fray,  Forth rush the torrents of the dark red stormy cloud, and moisten, like a skin, the earth with water-floods.

1.85.d: आ वो वहन्तु सप्तयो रघुष्यदो रघुपत्वानः पर जिगात बाहुभिः | सीदता बर्हिरुरु वः सदस कर्तं मादयध्वं मरुतो मध्वो अन्धसः ||
1.85.e: Let your swift-gliding coursers bear you hitherward with their fleet pinions. Come ye forward with your arms.  Sit on the grass; a wide seat hath been made for you: delight yourselves, O Maruts, in the pleasant food.

1.85.d: ते.अवर्धन्त सवतवसो महित्वना नाकं तस्थुरुरु चक्रिरे सदः | विष्णुर्यद धावद वर्षणं मदच्युतं वयो न सीदन्नधि बर्हिषि परिये ||
1.85.e: Strong in their native strength to greatness have they grown, stepped to the firmament and made their dwelling wide.  When Viṣṇu saved the Soma bringing wild delight, the Maruts sate like birds on their dear holy grass.

1.85.d: शूरा इवेद युयुधयो न जग्मयः शरवस्यवो न पर्तनासु येतिरे | भयन्ते विश्वा भुवना मरुद्भ्यो राजान इव तवेषसन्द्र्शो नरः ||
1.85.e: In sooth like heroes fain for fight they rush about, like combatants fame-seeking have they striven in war.  Before the Maruts every creature is afraid: the men are like to Kings, terrible to behold.

1.85.d: तवष्टा यद वज्रं सुक्र्तं हिरण्ययं सहस्रभ्र्ष्टिं सवपा अवर्तयत | धत्त इन्द्रो नर्यपांसि कर्तवे.अहन वर्त्रं निरपामौब्जदर्णवम ||
1.85.e: When Tvaṣṭar deft of hand had turned the thunderbolt, golden, with thousand edges, fashioned more skilfully,  Indra received it to perform heroic deeds. Vṛtra he slew, and forced the flood of water forth.

1.85.d: ऊर्ध्वं नुनुद्रे.अवतं त ओजसा दद्र्हाणं चिद बिभिदुर्विपर्वतम | धमन्तो वाणं मरुतः सुदानवो मदे सोमस्य रण्यानि चक्रिरे ||
1.85.e: They with their vigorous strength pushed the well up on high, and clove the cloud in twain though it was passing strong.  The Maruts, bounteous Givers, sending forth their voice, in the wild joy of Soma wrought their glorious deeds.

1.85.d: जिह्मं नुनुद्रे.अवतं तया दिशासिञ्चन्नुत्सं गोतमाय तर्ष्णजे | आ गछन्तीमवसा चित्रभानवः कामं विप्रस्यतर्पयन्त धामभिः ||
1.85.e: They drave the cloud transverse directed hitherward, and poured the fountain forth for thirsting Gotama.  Shining with varied light they come to him with help: they with their might fulfilled the longing of the sage.

1.85.d: या वः शर्म शशमानाय सन्ति तरिधातूनि दाशुषे यछताधि | अस्मभ्यं तानि मरुतो वि यन्त रयिं नो धत्त वर्षणः सुवीरम ||
1.85.e: The shelters which ye have for him who lauds you, bestow them threefold on the man who offers.  Extend the same boons unto us, ye Maruts. Give us, O Heroes, wealth with noble offspring.

1.86.d: मरुतो यस्य हि कषये पाथा दिवो विमहसः | स सुगोपातमो जनः ||
1.86.e: THE best of guardians hath that man within whose dwelling place ye drink,  O Maruts, giants of the sky.

1.86.d: यज्ञैर्वा यज्ञवाहसो विप्रस्य वा मतीनाम | मरुतः शर्णुता हवम ||
1.86.e: Honoured with sacrifice or with the worship of the sages’ hymns,  O Maruts, listen to the call.

1.86.d: उत वा यस्य वाजिनो.अनु विप्रमतक्षत | स गन्ता गोमतिव्रजे ||
1.86.e: Yea, the strong man to whom ye have vouchsafed to give a sage, shall move  Into a stable rich in kine.

1.86.d: अस्य वीरस्य बर्हिषि सुतः सोमो दिविष्टिषु | उक्थं मदश्च शस्यते ||
1.86.e: Upon this hero's sacred grass Soma is poured in daily rites:  Praise and delight are sung aloud.

1.86.d: अस्य शरोषन्त्वा भुवो विश्वा यश्चर्षणीरभि | सूरं चित सस्रुषीरिषः ||
1.86.e: Let the strong Maruts hear him, him surpassing all men: strength be his  That reaches even to the Sun.
For, through the swift Gods’ loving help, in many an autumn, Maruts, we  Have offered up our sacrifice.

1.86.d: सुभगः स परयज्यवो मरुतो अस्तु मर्त्यः | यस्य परयांसिपर्षथ ||
1.86.e: Fortunate shall that mortal be, O Maruts most adorable,  Whose offerings ye bear away.

1.86.d: शशमानस्य वा नरः सवेदस्य सत्यशवसः | विदा कामस्यवेनतः ||
1.86.e: O Heroes truly strong, ye know the toil of him who sings your praise,  The heart's desire of him who loves.

1.86.d: यूयं तत सत्यशवस आविष कर्त महित्वना | विध्यता विद्युता रक्षः ||
1.86.e: O ye of true strength, make this thing manifest by your greatness: strike  The demon with your thunderbolt.

1.86.d: गूहता गुह्यं तमो वि यात विश्वमत्रिणम | जयोतिष कर्ता यदुश्मसि ||
1.86.e: Conceal the horrid darkness, drive far from us each devouring fiend.  Create the light for which we long.

1.87.d: परत्वक्षसः परतवसो विरप्शिनो.अनानता अविथुरा रजीषिणः | जुष्टतमासो नर्तमासो अञ्जिभिर्व्यानज्रे के चिदुस्रा इव सत्र्भिः ||
1.87.e: LOUD Singers, never humbled, active, full of strength, immovable, impetuous, manliest, best-beloved,  They have displayed themselves with glittering ornaments, a few in number only, like the heavens with stars.

1.87.d: उपह्वरेषु यदचिध्वं ययिं वय इव मरुतः केन चित पथा | शचोतन्ति कोशा उप वो रथेष्वा घर्तमुक्षता मधुवर्णमर्चते ||
1.87.e: When, Maruts, on the steeps ye pile the moving cloud, ye are like birds on whatsoever path it be.  Clouds everywhere shed forth the rain upon your cars. Drop fatness, honey-hued, for him who sings your praise.

1.87.d: परैषामज्मेषु विथुरेव रेजते भूमिर्यामेषु यद ध युञ्जते शुभे | ते करीळयो धुनयो भराजद्र्ष्टयः सवयं महित्वं पनयन्त धूतयः ||
1.87.e: Earth at their racings trembles as if weak and worn, when on their ways they yoke their cars for victory.  They, sportive, loudly roaring, armed with glittering spears, shakers of all, themselves admire their mightiness.

1.87.d: स हि सवस्र्त पर्षदश्वो युवा गणो.अया ईशानस्तविषीभिराव्र्तः | असि सत्य रणयावानेद्यो.अस्या धियः पराविताथा वर्षा गणः ||
1.87.e: Self-moving is that youthful band, with spotted steeds; thus it hath lordly sway, endued with power and might.  Truthful art thou, and blameless, searcher out of sin: so thou, Strong Host, wilt be protector of this prayer.

1.87.d: पितुः परत्नस्य जन्मना वदामसि सोमस्य जिह्वा पर जिगाति चक्षसा | यदीमिन्द्रं शम्य रक्वाण आशतादिन नामानि यज्ञियानि दधिरे ||
1.87.e: We speak by our descent from our primeval Sire; our tongue, when we behold the Soma, stirs itself.  When, shouting, they had joined Indra in toil of fight, then only they obtained their sacrificial names.

1.87.d: शरियसे कं भानुभिः सं मिमिक्षिरे ते रश्मिभिस्त रक्वभिः सुखादयः | ते वाशीमन्त इष्मिणो अभीरवो विद्रे परियस्य मारुतस्य धाम्नः ||
1.87.e: Splendours they gained for glory, they who wear bright rings; rays they obtained, and men to celebrate their praise.  Armed with their swords, impetuous and fearing naught, they have possessed the Maruts’ own beloved home.

1.88.d: आ विद्युन्मद्भिर्मरुतः सवर्कै रथेभिर्यात रष्टिमद्भिरश्वपर्णैः | आ वर्षिष्ठया न इषा वयो न पप्तता सुमायाः ||
1.88.e: COME hither, Maruts, on your lightning laden cars, sounding with sweet songs, armed with lances, winged with steeds.  Fly unto us with noblest food, like birds, O ye of mighty power.

1.88.d: ते.अरुणेभिर्वरमा पिशङगैः शुभे कं यान्ति रथतूर्भिरश्वैः | रुक्मो न चित्रः सवधितीवान पव्या रथस्य जङघनन्त भूम ||
1.88.e: With their red-hued or, haply, tawny coursers which speed their chariots on, they come for glory.  Brilliant like gold is he who holds the thunder. Earth have they smitten with the chariot's felly.

1.88.d: शरिये कं वो अधि तनूषु वाशीर्मेधा वना न कर्णवन्त ऊर्ध्वा | युष्मभ्यं कं मरुतः सुजातास्तुविद्युम्नासो धनयन्ते अद्रिम ||
1.88.e: For beauty ye have swords upon your bodies. As they stir woods so may they stir our spirits.  For your sake, O ye Maruts very mighty and well-born, have they set the stone, in motion.

1.88.d: अहानि गर्ध्राः पर्या व आगुरिमां धियं वार्कार्यांच देवीम | बरह्म कर्ण्वन्तो गोतमासो अर्कैरूर्ध्वं नुनुद्रौत्सधिं पिबध्यै ||
1.88.e: The days went round you and came back O yearners, back, to this prayer and to this solemn worship.  The Gotamas making their prayer with singing have pushed the well's lid up to drink the water.

1.88.d: एतत तयन न योजनमचेति सस्वर्ह यन मरुतो गोतमो वः | पश्यन हिरण्यचक्रानयोदंष्ट्रान विधावतो वराहून ||
1.88.e: No hymn way ever known like this aforetime which Gotama sang forth for you, O Maruts,  What time upon your golden wheels he saw you, wild boars rushing about with tusks of iron.

1.88.d: एषा सया वो मरुतो.अनुभर्त्री परति षटोभति वाघतो न वाणी | अस्तोभयद वर्थासामनु सवधां गभस्त्योः ||
1.88.e: To you this freshening draught of Soma rusheth, O Maruts, like the voice of one who prayeth.  It rusheth freely from our hands as these libations wont to flow.

1.89.d: आ नो भद्राः करतवो कष्यन्तु विश्वतो.अदब्धासो अपरीतास उद्भिदः | देवा नो यथा सदमिद वर्धे असन्नप्रायुवो रक्षितारो दिवे-दिवे ||
1.89.e: MAY powers auspicious come to us from every side, never deceived, unhindered, and victorious,  That the Gods ever may be with us for our gain, our guardians day by day unceasing in their care.

1.89.d: देवानां भद्रा सुमतिर्र्जूयतां देवानां रातिरभि नोनि वर्तताम | देवानां सख्यमुप सेदिमा वयं देवा न आयुः पर तिरन्तु जीवसे ||
1.89.e: May the auspicious favour of the Gods be ours, on us descend the bounty of the righteous Gods.  The friendship of the Gods have we devoutly sought: so may the Gods extend our life that we may live.

1.89.d: तान पूर्वया निविदा हूमहे वयं भगं मित्रमदितिं दक्षमस्रिधम | अर्यमणं वरुणं सोममश्विना सरस्वतीनः सुभगा मयस करत ||
1.89.e: We call them hither with a hymn of olden time, Bhaga, the friendly Dakṣa, Mitra, Aditi,  Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, the Aśvins. May Sarasvatī, auspicious, grant felicity.

1.89.d: तन नो वातो मयोभु वातु भेषजं तन माता पर्थिवी तत्पिता दयौः | तद गरावाणः सोमसुतो मयोभुवस्तदश्विना शर्णुतं धिष्ण्या युवम ||
1.89.e: May the Wind waft to us that pleasant medicine, may Earth our Mother give it, and our Father Heaven,  And the joy-giving stones that press the Soma's juice. Aśvins, may ye, for whom our spirits long, hear this.

1.89.d: तमीशानं जगतस्तस्थुषस पतिं धियंजिन्वमवसे हूमहे वयम | पूषा नो यथा वेदसामसद वर्धे रक्षिता पायुरदब्धः सवस्तये ||
1.89.e: Him we invoke for aid who reigns supreme, the Lord of all that stands or moves, inspirer of the soul,  That Pūṣan may promote the increase of our wealth, our keeper and our guard infallible for our good.

1.89.d: सवस्ति न इन्द्रो वर्द्धश्रवाः सवस्ति नः पुषा विश्ववेदाः | सवस्ति नस्तार्क्ष्यो अरिष्टनेमिः सवस्ति नो बर्हस्पतिर्दधातु ||
1.89.e: Illustrious far and wide, may Indra prosper us: may Pūṣan prosper us, the Master of all wealth.  May Tārkṣya with uninjured fellies prosper us: Bṛhaspati vouchsafe to us prosperity.

1.89.d: पर्षदश्वा मरुतः पर्श्निमातरः शुभंयावानो विदथेषुजग्मयः | अग्निजिह्वा मनवः सूरचक्षसो विश्वे नो देवा अवसा गमन्निह ||
1.89.e: The Maruts, Sons of Pṛśni, borne by spotted steeds, moving in glory, oft visiting holy rites,  Sages whose tongue is Agni, brilliant as the Sun,—hither let all the Gods for our protection come.

1.89.d: भद्रं कर्णेभिः शर्णुयाम देवा भद्रं पश्येमाक्षभिर्यजत्राः | सथिरैरङगैस्तुष्टुवांसस्तनूभिर्व्यशेमदेवहितं यदायुः ||
1.89.e: Gods, may we with our ears listen to what is good, and with our eyes see what is good, ye Holy Ones.  With limbs and bodies firm may we extolling you attain the term of life appointed by the Gods.

1.89.d: शतमिन नु शरदो अन्ति देवा यत्रा नश्चक्रा जरसं तनूनाम | पुत्रासो यत्र पितरो भवन्ति मा नो मध्या रीरिषतायुर्गन्तोः ||
1.89.e: A hundred autumns stand before us, O ye Gods, within whose space ye bring our bodies to decay;  Within whose space our sons become fathers in turn. Break ye not in the midst our course of fleeting life.

1.89.d: अदितिर्द्यौरदितिरन्तरिक्षमदितिर्माता स पिता स पुत्रः | विश्वे देवा अदितिः पञ्च जना अदितिर्जातमदितिर्जनित्वम ||
1.89.e: Aditi is the heaven, Aditi is mid-air, Aditi is the Mother and the Sire and Son.  Aditi is all Gods, Aditi five-classed men, Aditi all that hath been born and shall be born.

1.90.d: रजुनीती नो वरुणो मित्रो नयतु विद्वान | अर्यमा देवैः सजोषाः ||
1.90.e: MAY Varuṇa with guidance straight, and Mitra lead us, he who knows,  And Aryaman in accord with Gods.

1.90.d: ते हि वस्वो वसवानास्ते अप्रमूरा महोभिः | वरता रक्षन्ते विश्वाहा ||
1.90.e: For they are dealers forth of wealth, and, not deluded, with their might  Guard evermore the holy laws.

1.90.d: ते अस्मभ्यं शर्म यंसन्नम्र्ता मर्त्येभ्यः | बाधमानाप दविषः ||
1.90.e: Shelter may they vouchsafe to us, Immortal Gods to mortal men,  Chasing our enemies away.

1.90.d: वि नः पथः सुविताय चियन्त्विन्द्रो मरुतः | पूषा भगो वन्द्यासः ||
1.90.e: May they mark out our paths to bliss, Indra, the Maruts, Pūṣan,  and Bhaga, the Gods to be adored.

1.90.d: उत नो धियो गोग्राः पूषन विष्णवेवयावः | कर्ता नः सवस्तिमतः ||
1.90.e: Yea, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, ye who run your course, enrich our hymns with kine;  Bless us with all prosperity.

1.90.d: मधु वाता रतायते मधु कषरन्ति सिन्धवः | माध्वीर्नः सन्त्वोषधीः ||
1.90.e: The winds waft sweets, the rivers pour sweets for the man who keeps the Law  So may the plants be sweet for us.

1.90.d: मधु नक्तमुतोषसो मधुमत पार्थिवं रजः | मधु दयौरस्तु नः पिता ||
1.90.e: Sweet be the night and sweet the dawns, sweet the terrestrial atmosphere;  Sweet be our Father Heaven to us.

1.90.d: मधुमान नो वनस्पतिर्मधुमानस्तु सूर्यः | माध्वीर्गावो भवन्तु नः ||
1.90.e: May the tall tree be full of sweets for us, and full of sweets the Sun:  May our milch-kine be sweet for us.

1.90.d: शं नो मित्रः शं वरुणः शं नो भवत्वर्यमा | शं न इन्द्रो बर्हस्पतिः शं नो विष्णुरुरुक्रमः ||
1.90.e: Be Mitra gracious unto us, and Varuṇa and Aryaman:  Indra, Bṛhaspati be kind, and Viṣṇu of the mighty stride.

1.91.d: तवं सोम पर चिकितो मनीषा तवं रजिष्ठमनु नेषि पन्थाम | तव परणीती पितरो न इन्दो देवेषु रत्नमभजन्त धीराः ||
1.91.e: Thou, Soma, art preeminent for wisdom; along the straightest path thou art our leader.  Our wise forefathers by thy guidance, Indu, dealt out among the Gods their share of treasure.

1.91.d: तवं सोम करतुभिः सुभूस्त्वं दक्षैः सुदक्षो विश्ववेदाः | तवं वर्षा वर्षत्वेभिर्महित्वा दयुम्नेभिर्द्युम्न्यभवो नर्चक्षाः ||
1.91.e: Thou by thine insight art most wise, O Soma, strong by thine energies and all possessing,  Mighty art thou by all thy powers and greatness, by glories art thou glorious, guide of mortals.

1.91.d: राज्ञो नु ते वरुणस्य वरतानि बर्हद गभीरं तव सोम धाम | शुचिष टवमसि परियो न मित्रो दक्षाय्यो अर्यमेवासिसोम ||
1.91.e: Thine are King Varuṇa's eternal statutes, lofty and deep, O Soma, is thy glory.  All-pure art thou like Mitra the beloved, adorable, like Aryaman, O Soma.

1.91.d: या ते धामानि दिवि या पर्थिव्यां या पर्वतेष्वोषधीष्वप्सु | तेभिर्नो विश्वैः सुमना अहेळन राजन सोम परतिहव्या गर्भाय ||
1.91.e: With all thy glories on the earth, in heaven, on mountains, in the plants, and in the waters,—  With all of these, well-pleased and not in anger, accept, O royal Soma, our oblations.

1.91.d: तवं सोमासि सत्पतिस्त्वं राजोत वर्त्रहा | तवं भद्रो असि करतुः ||
1.91.e: Thou, Soma, art the Lord of heroes, King, yea, Vṛtra-slayer thou:  Thou art auspicious energy.

1.91.d: तवं च सोम नो वशो जीवातुं न मरामहे | परियस्तोत्रो वनस्पतिः ||
1.91.e: And, Soma, let it be thy wish that we may live and may not die:  Praise-loving Lord of plants art thou.

1.91.d: तवं सोम महे भगं तवं यून रतायते | दक्षं दधासि जीवसे ||
1.91.e: To him who keeps the law, both old and young, thou givest happiness,  And energy that he may live.

1.91.d: तवं नः सोम विश्वतो रक्षा राजन्नघायतः | न रिष्येत्त्वावतः सखा ||
1.91.e: Guard us, King Soma, on all sides from him who threatens us: never let  The friend of one like thee be harmed.

1.91.d: सोम यास्ते मयोभुव ऊतयः सन्ति दाशुषे | ताभिर्नो.अविता भव ||
1.91.e: With those delightful aids which thou hast, Soma, for the worshipper,—  Even with those protect thou us.

1.91.d: इमं यज्ञमिदं वचो जुजुषाण उपागहि | सोम तवं नोव्र्धे भव ||
1.91.e: Accepting this our sacrifice and this our praise, O Soma, come,  And be thou nigh to prosper us.

1.91.d: सोम गीर्भिष टवा वयं वर्धयामो वचोविदः | सुम्र्ळीकोन आ विश ||
1.91.e: Well-skilled in speech we magnify thee, Soma, with our sacred songs:  Come thou to us, most gracious One.

1.91.d: गयस्फानो अमीवहा वसुवित पुष्टिवर्धनः | सुमित्रः सोमनो भव ||
1.91.e: Enricher, healer of disease, wealth-finder, prospering our store,  Be, Soma, a good Friend to us.

1.91.d: सोम रारन्धि नो हर्दि गावो न यवसेष्वा | मर्य इव सवोक्ये ||
1.91.e: Soma, be happy in our heart, as milch-kine in the grassy meads,  As a young man in his own house.

1.91.d: यः सोम सख्ये तव रारणद देव मर्त्यः | तं दक्षः सचते कविः ||
1.91.e: O Soma, God, the mortal man who in thy friendship hath delight,  Him doth the mighty Sage befriend.

1.91.d: उरुष्या णो अभिशस्तेः सोम नि पाह्यंहसः | सखा सुशेव एधि नः ||
1.91.e: Save us from slanderous reproach, keep us., O Soma, from distress:  Be unto us a gracious Friend.

1.91.d: आ पयायस्व समेतु ते विश्वतः सोम वर्ष्ण्यम | भवा वाजस्य संगथे ||
1.91.e: Soma, wax great. From every side may vigorous powers unite in thee:  Be in the gathering-place of strength.

1.91.d: आ पयायस्व मदिन्तम सोम विश्वेभिरंशुभिः | भवा नःसुश्रवस्तमः सखा वर्धे ||
1.91.e: Wax, O most gladdening Soma, great through all thy rays of light, and be  A Friend of most illustrious fame to prosper us.

1.91.d: सं ते पयांसि समु यन्तु वाजाः सं वर्ष्ण्यान्यभिमातिषाहः | आप्यायमानो अम्र्ताय सोम दिवि शरवांस्युत्तमानि धिष्व ||
1.91.e: In thee be juicy nutriments united, and powers and mighty foe-subduing vigour,  Waxing to immortality, O Soma: win highest glories for thyself in heaven.

1.91.d: या ते धामानि हविषा यजन्ति ता ते विश्वा परिभूरस्तुयज्ञम | गयस्फानः परतरणः सुवीरो.अवीरहा पर चरा सोम दुर्यान ||
1.91.e: Such of thy glories as with poured oblations men honour, may they all invest our worship.  Wealth-giver, furtherer with troops of heroes, sparing the brave, come, Soma, to our houses.

1.91.d: सोमो धेनुं सोमो अर्वन्तमाशुं सोमो वीरं कर्मण्यं ददाति | सादन्यं विदथ्यं सभेयं पित्र्श्रवणं यो ददाशदस्मै ||
1.91.e: To him who worships Soma gives the milch-cow, a fleet steed and a man of active knowledge,  Skilled in home duties, meet for holy synod, for council meet, a glory to his father.

1.91.d: अषाळ्हं युत्सु पर्तनासु पप्रिं सवर्षामप्सां वर्जनस्यगोपाम | भरेषुजां सुक्षितिं सुश्रवसं जयन्तं तवामनु मदेम सोम ||
1.91.e: Invincible in fight, saver in battles, guard of our camp, winner of light and water,  Born amid hymns, well-housed, exceeding famous, victor, in thee will we rejoice, O Soma.

1.91.d: तवमिमा ओषधीः सोम विश्वास्त्वमपो अजनयस्त्वं गाः | तवमा ततन्थोर्वन्तरिक्षं तवं जयोतिषा वि तमो ववर्थ ||
1.91.e: These herbs, these milch-kine, and these running waters, all these, O Soma, thou hast generated.  The spacious firmament hast thou expanded, and with the light thou hast dispelled the darkness.

1.91.d: देवेन नो मनसा देव सोम रायो भागं सहसावन्नभि युध्य | मा तवा तनदीशिषे वीर्यस्योभयेभ्यः पर चिकित्सा गविष्टौ ||
1.91.e: Do thou, God Soma, with thy Godlike spirit, victorious, win for us a share of riches.  Let none prevent thee: thou art Lord of valour. Provide for both sides in the fray for booty.
